## TOPIC: README

# Building Rive files with `rive`

`rive` turns a directory of plain source files — Luau scripts, WGSL shaders, RML
markup, images, fonts — into a `.riv` (the runtime format) and a `.rev` (which
opens in the Rive editor).

Everything here is what you need to author those files without access to the
Rive codebase.

Read any topic below with `rive docs <topic>` — the link target minus the
`.md`, so [drawing.md](drawing.md) is `rive docs drawing` and
[luau/protocols.md](luau/protocols.md) is `rive docs luau/protocols`.
`rive docs` on its own prints this index, and `rive docs --search <text>`
lists every line, in every topic, that mentions `<text>`, as
`topic:line: text`.

The RML in these topics is excerpted: every file wraps its elements in a
`<Rive version="1" kind="fragment">` root, which the examples leave out. See
[format.md](format.md) for the document shape.

## Seeing the result

There are exactly two ways to look at what you built:

| Who is looking | Run |
|---|---|
| the user | `rive <project-dir>` — the previewer: a window that rebuilds on every save |
| you | `rive <project-dir> --screenshot --advance=1` — a png at `build/<name>.png` |

`rive <project-dir>` does not exit until its window is closed. Start it in the
background, once, and leave it running; every later edit shows up in it on
its own.

Nothing else is a preview:

- **Not `rive push`.** It uploads the project to a file in the user's Rive
  account and adds a revision. Push only when asked to.
- **Not an HTML page or a web runtime.** Local builds carry unsigned scripts,
  which web runtimes reject, so a scripted file shows nothing there. The one
  command that does produce a web page is `rive <project-dir> --publish=web`,
  which signs the build first; it ships the work, it is not the authoring
  loop. See [publishing.md](publishing.md) and [publish-web.md](publish-web.md).
- **Not a `.riv` on its own.** `rive` opens project directories; there is no
  command that opens a built `.riv` by itself.

## The loop

```bash
rive <project-dir> --verify
```

Compiles everything — RML, Luau, shaders — and exits non-zero on errors,
without writing a `.riv`. This is the command to run after every edit.

`--publish` also builds, and writes the `.riv`; `--verify` is the check. Only
`--publish` needs a login. **A file with scripts that is destined for the
web must be built with `--publish`** — unsigned scripts are rejected by the CDN
and web runtimes, and nothing local will warn you. See
[publishing.md](publishing.md).

```bash
rive inspect <project-dir> --summary
rive inspect <project-dir> --json
```

`--summary` prints the `problems` list and a count of objects per type, per
artboard and for the other roots; `--json` prints the whole resolved tree.

It works offline too, and reports *both* kinds of failure — the misspellings
that stop a build, and the wiring mistakes that do not:

```json
{"severity": "error",   "kind": "syntax", "line": 21,
 "message": "unknown element <Elipse>; did you mean <Ellipse>?"}
{"severity": "warning", "kind": "no-default-state-machine", "line": 3,
 "message": "artboard \"A\" has animations or state machines but no defaultStateMachineId; ..."}
```

Every entry has `severity` (`error` or `warning`), `kind`, `line` and
`message`, and `inspect` exits non-zero when there is an error.

**Run both — neither is a superset of the other.** They share only syntax
checking; beyond that they cover different ground:

| | `--verify` | `inspect` |
|---|---|---|
| syntax, unknown names | yes | yes |
| Luau type checking | **yes** | no |
| shaders | **yes** | no |
| bind paths, state machines, the rest of `problems` | no | **yes** |

So a scene can pass `--verify` cleanly and still be wired to nothing, and a
script with type errors will not show up in `inspect` at all. If your project is
pure RML, `inspect` is doing nearly all the work; the moment there is a `.luau`
file, `--verify` is the only thing reading it.

**Neither of them looks at a pixel.** An invisible shape, a collapsed icon, text
in the wrong place, a shader reading black — every one of those builds clean and
inspects clean. The third check is to render:

```bash
rive <dir> --screenshot=out.png             # one frame, headless, no window
rive <dir> --screenshot=t.png --advance=60  # 60 frames in, for animation
rive <dir> --screenshot=h.png --pointer=click@120,60   # drive it first
```

See [workflow.md](workflow.md) for the full sequence.

One thing the capture cannot see: it always renders at `@1x`, so a script that
sizes its own canvas in points rather than device pixels looks perfect here and
soft on every Retina screen. That one needs the live window — see
[gotchas.md](gotchas.md#dropping-resizes-scale-renders-your-effect-at-half-resolution).

The rest of the output is worth knowing:

| Key | Holds |
|---|---|
| `artboards` | the resolved scene trees |
| `defaultArtboard` | which artboard actually got picked |
| `backboard` | file-level metadata, synthesized from `rive.yaml` for a project |
| `roots` | root elements: view models, assets, converters |
| `problems` | the list above |
| `schema` | type information for what was built |

`defaultArtboard` answers a question you will otherwise guess at: with several
artboards, the choice is `main` in `rive.yaml`, then the first declared.

### What `problems` does and does not cover

Knowing the boundary matters more than any single check, because an empty
`problems` is otherwise easy to read as "this file is correct".

**Checked:**

| Kind | Catches |
|---|---|
| `syntax` | unknown elements, unknown attributes, bad value types |
| `unresolved-bind-path` | a `sourcePathIds` that leads nowhere |
| `bind-target-missing-property` | a bind whose target has no such property |
| `incompatible-bind-types` | source and target types that cannot connect |
| `missing-reference` | a required id left **unset**, on a fixed list of types |
| `no-default-state-machine` | an artboard with animations or state machines but no `defaultStateMachineId`, so which one runs is left to each host |
| `no-artboards` / `no-default-artboard` | file-level structure |
| `derived-property-authored` | setting a `D` property that is computed |
| `incomparable-condition` | a transition condition that cannot evaluate |
| `duplicate-script-name` | two scripts claiming one name |
| `paint-without-shape-paint` | a `SolidColor` or gradient outside a `Fill`/`Stroke` |
| `paint-mutator-count` | a `Fill`/`Stroke` with no `SolidColor` or gradient, or with more than one (a `RadialGradient` counts as a gradient) |
| `reference-wrong-type` | an id that resolves, but to the wrong kind of thing: `stateToId` naming a shape rather than a state. Only on properties whose def declares a referent |
| `implied-reference-authored` | a reference the nesting always sets, written out anyway, so the value never reaches the file |
| `wrong-parent` | an element nested where it cannot work, from the def's `parents` — a `LayoutParticipant` beside its shape, a `GridTrack` inside the style, a `GridItemPlacement` inside the participant |
| `library-component-outside-asset` | a `LibraryViewModel` or `LibraryDataEnum` outside the `LibraryAsset` it was imported through |
| `duplicate-sibling` | a value repeated within its scope, from the def's `unique`. Both this and `wrong-parent` are fallbacks: a def may name its own kind instead |
| `scroll-without-physics` | a `ScrollConstraint` with no physics, so it scrolls without momentum |
| `scroll-physics-parent` | a scroll physics with a `parentId`; physics belong to the file and are reached only through `physicsId` |
| `semantic-listener-target-without-data` | a semantic listener whose target is not the node holding the `SemanticData` |
| `semantic-listener-without-input-type` | a `semanticAction` trigger that is not a `ListenerInputTypeSemantic` |
| `draw-target-not-child-of-rules` | a `DrawRules` whose `DrawTarget` is not nested inside it |
| `artboards-overlap` | two artboards sharing stage space, so they stack when opened in the editor |
| `states-overlap` | two states of a layer at the same graph position, so they stack in the editor |
| `listener-converter-on-write` | a from-property listener change with its converter on the write bind, where the editor does not look |
| `converter-loop` | a bind on a converter's property (or formula token, template argument, script input) whose converter leads back to that converter, which the runtime drops, so the value arrives unconverted (warning); or groups that hold each other, which the runtime clones without end (error) |
| `artboard-without-style` | an artboard with no linked `LayoutComponentStyle` |
| `rotation-looks-like-degrees` | a `rotation` past a full turn, which is almost always degrees |
| `text-style-without-font-names` | a text style left without `familyName` or `styleName` over a `FontAsset` with no file, so the build cannot name the font and the editor's Font and Style dropdowns show `-`; see [text.md](text.md#name-the-face-not-just-the-file) |
| `interpolated-step` | a linear or eased key whose value jumps within one frame the animation plays (8% of the property's range over those frames or 20/255 on a colour channel, and over 4x faster than a segment beside it moving the same way; in a loop whose values at its end and start are under that 8% apart, the segments either side of the seam are beside each other, unless a work-area boundary falls inside an eased segment). A host drawing between frames (a 120 Hz screen) shows the value halfway. Make it a hold key. The build and `--verify` also print it as a warning |
| `component-without-asset` / `nested-artboard-not-component` | a component with no `ComponentAsset`, or a nested artboard that is not a component |
| `stateful-instance-not-exported` / `stateful-instance-view-model-mismatch` / `instance-on-plain-nested-artboard` | a per-placement view model instance that the runtime will ignore |
| mesh, skin and bone kinds | malformed rigging; see [rigging.md](rigging.md) |

Two more mistakes fail the **build** rather than landing in `problems`: an id
attribute naming an id no element declares (`stateToId="0:99"`), and an asset
`file` that is missing, empty or an unfetched Git LFS pointer.

**Structural problems the runtime cannot survive fail the build too.** A def's
`parents` or `children` rule marked `"enforced": true` describes a structure the
runtime crashes on or rejects the whole file over. Those rules are refused by
the build, `--rev` export and `push`, and nothing is written. They include:

- `paint-without-shape-paint`: a gradient or `SolidColor` outside a paint.
- `paint-mutator-count`: a `Fill` or `Stroke` with no color source, or with two.
- `wrong-parent`, for an enforced rule: a `TrimPath` or `Dash` outside its paint, a
  constraint off a transform, a `Bone` or vertex out of its chain, a
  `TextValueRun` outside its `Text`, and the other rules `dev/defs` marks.
- `converter-loop`, as an error: converter groups that hold each other, or a
  group that holds itself, which the runtime clones without end. A bind whose
  converter loops is only a warning, since the runtime drops that converter.

The error leads with the kind, for example `paint-mutator-count: Fill "F" holds
2 of <SolidColor> or <LinearGradient>, and at most 1 is allowed; ...`, at the
line of the element to remove.

Rules whose element is only ignored elsewhere stay lint, reported by `inspect`
alone: a `Feather` off its paint, a `GridItemPlacement` in a list. An agent's
`commit_rml` is held to the enforced rules, but only for problems its sandbox
adds, so one the live file already had does not block an unrelated edit.

**Not checked — all of these build and inspect completely clean:**

- **Id lists.** `sourcePathIds`, `dataBindPathIds` and `tagIds` are not checked
  for dangling entries; bind paths are checked separately, above.
- **An asset a script asks for by name** (`context:image('backdrop')`) that the
  project does not have.
- **A state that covers a transition.** `states-overlap` compares exact
  positions only, so a state sitting on the line between two others passes.
  See [gotchas.md](gotchas.md#unpositioned-states-and-artboards-all-land-on-the-same-point).
- **A keyframe whose type does not match its property.**
- **A modifier value with no matching `modify*` flag.**
- **Anything about appearance** — size, overflow, spacing, colour.
- **Anything at all in a `.luau` script.** `inspect` does not read Luau at all.
  Scripts are type-checked in strict mode and type errors fail the build — run
  `rive <dir> --verify` for those. See
  [luau/protocols.md](luau/protocols.md#checking-a-script).

So `problems: []` means "nothing on the left-hand list is wrong". Confirming the
rest means querying the tree for what you intended, which is why every doc here
ends with a `jq` check rather than a build command.

**One thing the tree cannot tell you: bind paths.** `inspect` omits `List<Id>`
properties, so a `DataBindContext` reads back as
`{"type":"DataBindContext","propertyKey":268,"flags":0}` — the `sourcePathIds`
you authored are not there. Editor-only properties are absent too, so
`defaultInstanceId`, `exports` and `viewModelInstanceId` never appear either.

For those, `problems` is the only readback there is, and it is good as far as
it goes: `unresolved-bind-path` and `bind-target-missing-property` both fire
with precise messages.

**But do not read the absence of a problem as "the bind is wired."**
`unresolved-bind-path` walks the path inside the view model the path *names*;
it never checks that the artboard is bound to that view model. A bind copied
between artboards can name a perfectly valid path in the wrong view model,
resolve nothing at runtime, and report clean.

```bash
rive schema <Type>              # properties, defaults, enum names, propertyKeys
rive schema --search <text>     # find the type name in the first place
```

There are 417 core types. Do not guess names — search for them. On a terminal
`--search` opens a picker over the matches, and enter describes the type the
row belongs to; piped or in CI it prints them under `types:` and `properties:`
as it always has.

Setting the tool up by hand for the first time? Read
[getting-started.md](getting-started.md) — install, login, first project.

New to Rive? Read [overview.md](overview.md) first — it is the mental model
the rest assumes.

`rive samples` picks one of the runnable example projects that ship with the
CLI and copies it into a directory you name. Starting from one is often
faster than starting from an empty scene.

Read [format.md](format.md) before writing any RML. It is short, and nearly
every mistake this tool sees comes from skipping it.

## Two ways to put something on screen

**A script alone.** Any Luau file returning the `Layout` protocol, or `.as`
file exporting a class that extends `Layout`, gets its own artboard
automatically. A project can be one script and a `rive.yaml`.
Good for procedural drawing and generative work.

**RML markup.** A `.rml` file describes the whole document — artboards, shapes,
text, animations, state machines, view models, data binding. When one is
present it replaces the automatic artboards; scripts still compile and attach by
reference. Good for anything with structure, and the only way to produce a file
a designer can meaningfully edit afterwards.

The two combine: RML scenes can attach scripts to objects and pass them typed
inputs.

### Use each for what it is good at

A script *can* draw an entire interface — buttons, panels, score readouts — and
it will work. It is almost always the wrong choice, and it is the most common
structural mistake in generated projects.

| Build it in | When |
|---|---|
| **RML** | anything with a fixed structure: screens, panels, buttons, labels, HUDs, menus, cards, lists |
| **Luau** | a simulation or a generated image: particles, physics, procedural geometry, data-driven drawing, per-frame maths |

The rule of thumb: **if you could draw it in a design tool, build it in RML.**
If it only exists because something is being computed each frame, script it.

A game is the clearest case. Put the playfield — the simulation, the collision,
the moving pieces — in a script, and build the surrounding UI (score, lives,
menus, buttons, game-over panel) in RML with layouts, text and a state machine.
Doing the UI in the script instead costs you:

- **layout**, so every panel and label is hand-positioned in code and nothing
  responds to the artboard's size
- **text**, which scripts cannot draw at all — there is no font API on
  `Renderer`, so lettering has to be hand-built from paths
- **state machines and listeners**, so buttons and screen transitions become
  bespoke hit-testing and flags
- **editability**, since a designer can change an RML scene and cannot change
  your script

Scripts and RML compose, so this is not a trade-off: attach the script to a
`LayoutComponent` in the scene and let markup own everything around it. See
[layout.md](layout.md) and [luau/protocols.md](luau/protocols.md#what-to-put-in-a-script).

## Verifying your work

Run the checks above after every pass, not at the end — see
[workflow.md](workflow.md). A build that succeeds proves little; query the tree
for what you meant to build:

```bash
rive inspect . --json | jq '[..|objects|select(.type=="KeyedProperty")|.propertyKey]'
```

Empty after keying a rotation means nothing is animated.

# Artboards and components

<!-- GENERATED by docsgen/gen_as_api.py from
     rasc/animascript/std/rive -- do not edit -->

Import from `"rive/artboard"`. Declares: `Animation`, `Artboard`, `Drawable`, `DrawableProperty`, `NodeData`, `PropertyKey`, `PropertyKind`

```as
/// A node of an artboard instance, with its transform and access to its
/// parent and children. Get one by name with `Artboard.node`. Reads always
/// show the node as the artboard last posed it, animation included.
///
/// ```as
/// let node = instance.node("Hips");
/// if (node != null) {
///     node.rotation = Math.PI / 4;
///     node.setPosition(Vector.xy(199, 299));
/// }
/// ```
export class NodeData {
    /// The x coordinate of the local position.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// node.x = 100;
    /// ```
    get x(): f64;
    set x(value: f64);

    /// The y coordinate of the local position.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// node.y = 200;
    /// ```
    get y(): f64;
    set y(value: f64);

    /// The local rotation in radians.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// node.rotation = Math.PI / 4;
    /// ```
    get rotation(): f64;
    set rotation(value: f64);

    /// The x component of the local scale.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// node.scaleX = 2;
    /// ```
    get scaleX(): f64;
    set scaleX(value: f64);

    /// The y component of the local scale.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// node.scaleY = 2;
    /// ```
    get scaleY(): f64;
    set scaleY(value: f64);

    /// The local position.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// let position = node.position();
    /// ```
    position(): Vector;

    /// Sets the local position.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// node.setPosition(Vector.xy(199, 299));
    /// ```
    setPosition(value: Vector): void;

    /// The local scale.
    scale(): Vector;

/// An animation of an artboard instance, played by script. Get one by name
/// with `Artboard.animation`. It poses the instance it came from; advance

/// state machine; otherwise let the machine play.
///
/// ```as
/// export class Walker extends Node {
///     @input character: Artboard? = null;
///     instance: Artboard? = null;
///     walk: Animation? = null;
///
///     override init(context: Context): bool {
///         let character = this.character;
///         if (character != null) {
///             let instance = character.instance();
///             this.walk = instance.animation("Walk");
///             this.instance = instance;
///         }
///         return true;
///     }

///     override advance(seconds: f64): bool {
///         let instance = this.instance;
///         let walk = this.walk;

    /// nothing afterwards.

/// The kind of a custom property on a `Drawable`.
export enum PropertyKind {
    /// A number.
    number,

    /// A boolean.
    boolean,

    /// A string.
    string,

    /// A color.
    color,

    /// An enum, whose value reads as a string.
    enumeration,

    /// A trigger.
    trigger,
}

/// One custom property, as `Drawable.properties` lists them.
export class DrawableProperty {
    /// The property's name.
    name: string;

    /// The property's kind.
    kind: PropertyKind;
}

/// What a custom property is read by. Get one from `Artboard.propertyKey`
/// once, in `init`, and keep it: resolving a name scans the file's name
/// table, reading by key does not.
export type PropertyKey = u32;

/// A drawable that carries custom properties, handed to the visitor of
/// `Artboard.draw`. It is only valid inside that visitor call. Custom
/// properties are added to a drawable in the editor's inspector.
export class Drawable {
    /// Whether the drawable has a custom property of this key, of any kind.

    /// Whether the drawable has a custom property of this key and kind. Use
    /// it to tell a missing property from one holding the typed reads'
    /// fallback value.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// if (drawable.holds(EMISSIVE, PropertyKind.number)) {
    ///     console.log(drawable.number(EMISSIVE).toString());
    /// }
    /// ```
    holds(key: PropertyKey, kind: PropertyKind): bool;

    /// The custom number property of this key, 0 when there is none. Use
    /// `numberOrNull` to tell the two apart.
    number(key: PropertyKey): f64;

    /// The custom boolean property of this key, false when there is none.
    boolean(key: PropertyKey): bool;

    /// The custom color property of this key, 0 when there is none.
    color(key: PropertyKey): Color;

    /// The custom string property of this key, empty when there is none.
    string(key: PropertyKey): string;

    /// The custom number property of this key, or null when there is none.
    ///

    /// let emissive = drawable.numberOrNull(EMISSIVE);
    /// if (emissive != null) {
    ///     console.log(emissive.value.toString());
    /// }
    /// ```
    numberOrNull(key: PropertyKey): Box<f64>?;

    /// The custom boolean property of this key, or null when there is none.
    booleanOrNull(key: PropertyKey): Box<bool>?;

    /// The custom color property of this key, or null when there is none.
    colorOrNull(key: PropertyKey): Box<Color>?;

    /// The custom string property of this key, or null when there is none.
    stringOrNull(key: PropertyKey): string?;

    /// Every custom property on the drawable. For tooling and debugging:
    /// the editor and rive-cli have it, a shipping runtime does not, so do
    /// not call it from a script you ship.
    properties(): DrawableProperty[];

    /// Draws the drawable under the renderer's current state.
    draw(renderer: Renderer): void;
}

/// An artboard instance a script draws, advances and forwards pointer
/// events to, with access to its
/// named nodes, animations and data.
///
/// Declare one as an input and make instances of it. `T` is a class
/// extending `ViewModel` that names the view model the artboard binds, so
/// the editor offers matching view models for an input declared as
/// `Artboard<Character>`, and `data` returns a `Character`.
///
/// ```as
/// export class Scene extends Node {
///     @input character: Artboard? = null;
///     instance: Artboard? = null;
///
///     override init(context: Context): bool {
///         let character = this.character;
///         if (character != null) {
///             this.instance = character.instance(ViewModel.create("Character"));
///         }
///         return true;
///     }
///
///     override advance(seconds: f64): bool {
///         return this.instance?.advance(seconds) ?? true;
///     }
///
///     override draw(renderer: Renderer): void {
///         let instance = this.instance;
///         if (instance != null) {
///             renderer.save();
///             instance.draw(renderer);
///             renderer.restore();
///         }
///     }
/// }
/// ```
export class Artboard<T = ViewModel> {
    /// Creates a new instance of the artboard with independent state, bound
    /// to `viewModel` when one is given.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// let instance = character.instance(ViewModel.create("Character"));
    /// ```
    instance(viewModel: T? = null): Artboard<T>;

    /// Advances the artboard by the given time in seconds. Returns true if
    /// the artboard should keep receiving advance calls.
    advance(seconds: f64): bool;

    /// The key custom properties called `name` are read by. When no property
    /// in the file carries that name the key matches nothing, so every read
    /// by it finds no property.
    propertyKey(name: string): PropertyKey;

    /// Draws the artboard with the color modulation set, per drawable, from
    /// its custom property of this key: a number as a gray level clamped to
    /// 0 to 1, a color as is. Drawables without it draw under the renderer's
    /// current state. Levels multiply down through tagged drawables that
    /// hold others: inside a nested artboard tagged 0.5, a shape tagged 0.2
    /// draws at 0.1 and an untagged one at 0.5. Nothing calls back into the
    /// script, so this is the cheapest way to draw a pass like emission.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// // In init: EMISSIVE = artboard.propertyKey("emissive");
    /// // Everything black except drawables tagged emissive.
    /// renderer.save();
    /// renderer.setColorModulation(Color.rgba(0, 0, 0, 255));
    /// artboard.drawModulated(renderer, EMISSIVE);
    /// renderer.restore();
    /// ```
    drawModulated(renderer: Renderer, key: PropertyKey): void;

    /// Draws the artboard using the provided renderer.
    ///
    /// With a `visitor`, each drawable that has custom properties is handed
    /// to it instead of being drawn: the visitor decides whether to call
    /// `drawable.draw(renderer)` and under what renderer state. Whatever it
    /// sets on the renderer ends with that visit. Every other drawable draws
    /// as usual, and clipping still applies. `context` is passed through to
    /// the visitor untouched.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// let GLOW: PropertyKey = 0; // In init: GLOW = artboard.propertyKey("glow");
    ///
    /// // Draws only the drawables tagged glow, in their own paint.
    /// function drawGlow(context: usize, drawable: Drawable, renderer: Renderer): void {
    ///     if (drawable.boolean(GLOW)) {
    ///         drawable.draw(renderer);
    ///     }
    /// }
    ///
    /// artboard.draw(renderer, drawGlow);
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Drawing a tagged nested artboard visits the tagged drawables inside
    /// it from within that `drawable.draw` call, so a value carries down in
    /// a variable:
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// let level: f64 = 1;
    ///
    /// function drawEmission(context: usize, drawable: Drawable, renderer: Renderer): void {
    ///     let outer = level;
    ///     level = outer * Math.min(drawable.number(EMISSIVE), 1);
    ///     let c = <u32>Math.floor(level * 255);
    ///     renderer.setColorModulation(Color.rgba(c, c, c, 255));
    ///     drawable.draw(renderer);
    ///     level = outer;
    /// }
    /// ```
    draw(
        renderer: Renderer,
        visitor: ((context: usize, drawable: Drawable, renderer: Renderer) => void)? = null,
        context: usize = 0
    ): void;

    /// The view model bound to the artboard, typed as `T`, or null when none
    /// is bound.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// let data = instance.data();
    /// if (data != null) {
    ///     let nickname = data.getString("nickname");
    ///     if (nickname != null) {
    ///         console.log(nickname.value);
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    data(): T?;

    /// The width of the artboard.
    get width(): f64;
    set width(value: f64);

    /// The height of the artboard.
    get height(): f64;
    set height(value: f64);

    /// If true, the artboard's origin is treated as the frame origin.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// instance.frameOrigin = true;
    /// ```
    get frameOrigin(): bool;
    set frameOrigin(value: bool);

    /// Creates an instance of the named animation that plays into this
    /// artboard, or null when there is no animation by that name.
    animation(name: string): Animation?;

    /// Adds the artboard's visible shapes to `path`, transformed by
    /// `transform` when given.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// // Rebuild an outline of the artboard each frame, offset slightly.
    /// outline.reset();
    /// instance.addToPath(outline, Mat2D.withTranslation(8, 8));
    /// renderer.drawPath(outline, outlinePaint);
    /// ```
    addToPath(path: Path, transform: Mat2D = Mat2D()): void;

    /// The node with the given name, or null when no such node exists.
    /// The node's name must be exported
    /// (in the Hierarchy, right-click the node and select **Export Name**).
    /// Names that aren't exported are left out of the exported file, so
    /// `node` returns null for them.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// let root = instance.node("Root");
    /// if (root != null) {
    ///     root.decompose(Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 100));
    /// }
    /// ```
    node(name: string): NodeData?;

    /// The bounding box of the artboard as its minimum point `v0` and
    /// maximum point `v1`.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// let bounds = instance.bounds();
    /// console.log((bounds.v1.x - bounds.v0.x).toString());
    /// console.log((bounds.v1.y - bounds.v0.y).toString());
    /// ```
    bounds(): ArtboardBounds;

    /// Forwards a pointer down event to the artboard. Returns a hit test
    /// result, 0 when nothing was hit. Only returns a non zero value when a
    /// hit testable object inside the artboard is hit.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// override pointerDown(event: PointerEvent): void {
    ///     let instance = this.instance;
    ///     if (instance != null && instance.pointerDown(event) != 0) {
    ///         event.hit();
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    pointerDown(event: PointerEvent): f64;

    /// Forwards a pointer move event to the artboard. Returns a hit test
    /// result, 0 when nothing was hit.
    pointerMove(event: PointerEvent): f64;

    /// Forwards a pointer up event to the artboard. Returns a hit test
    /// result, 0 when nothing was hit.
    pointerUp(event: PointerEvent): f64;

    /// Forwards a pointer exit event to the artboard. Returns a hit test
    /// result, 0 when nothing was hit.
    pointerExit(event: PointerEvent): f64;

    /// Forwards a mouse wheel or trackpad scroll to the artboard, where a
    /// `ScrollConstraint` view under the position can take it. Returns a hit
    /// test result, 0 when nothing took it.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// override pointerScroll(event: ScrollEvent): void {
    ///     let instance = this.instance;
    ///     if (instance == null) {
    ///         return;
    ///     }
    ///     let local = new ScrollEvent(event.id,
    ///                                 event.position - Vector.xy(this.x, this.y),
    ///                                 event.delta, event.phase,
    ///                                 event.precise, event.timeStamp);
    ///     if (instance.pointerScroll(local) != 0) {
    ///         event.hit();
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    pointerScroll(event: ScrollEvent): f64;

    /// Forwards a gamepad connection to the artboard: its focused control
    /// first, then every scripted node that did not take it. Returns how
    /// many scripted nodes received it.
    /// ```as
    /// override gamepadConnected(event: GamepadEvent): void {
    ///     this.instance.gamepadConnected(event);
    /// }
    /// ```
    gamepadConnected(event: GamepadEvent): f64;

    /// Forwards a gamepad button or axis change to the artboard, the same
    /// way as `gamepadConnected`.
    gamepadEvent(event: GamepadEvent): f64;

    /// Forwards a gamepad disconnection to the artboard, the same way as
    /// `gamepadConnected`.
    gamepadDisconnected(event: GamepadEvent): f64;

    /// Releases the artboard instance now instead of when it is collected.
    /// Do not use it afterwards.
    release(): void;
}
```

///     }
/// }
/// ```
export class AudioSource {

    /// The audio's own sample rate in Hz. Playback resamples it to the
    /// engine's rate, `Audio.sampleRate()`.

    /// frames are queued, so a processor started then plays from the start.
    /// Rejects in builds that cannot run audio processors, when the audio
    /// does not decode, or when shared memory has no room for the queue.
    /// ```as
    /// let stream = await source.stream(Audio.processorSampleRate(), Audio.processorChannels());
    /// stream.loop = true;
    /// this.player = Audio.start(() => new StreamPlayer(), stream.reader);

    set volume(value: f64);

    /// Releases the sound now instead of when it is collected. Later calls
    /// on it do nothing.
    release(): void;
}

/// What the audio thread drives. Extend `AudioProcessor` rather than this.
export abstract class AudioProcessorBase {
    /// Renders one block of `frames` interleaved frames into `out`, which
    /// arrives zeroed. `startFrame` is the block's first frame on the engine's
    /// clock, the one `Audio.timeFrame` reads. In a browser and on NRDP it
    /// counts the page's audio output instead, whose frames and rate
    /// `Audio.timeFrame` and `Audio.sampleRate` do not report. Runs on the
    /// audio thread, so it must neither wait nor allocate: drain rings with
    /// `receiveInto` and read snapshots with `latestInto`, into values made
    /// in init, rather than with `receive` and `latest`. A throw, a trap, or
    /// a block past the hard limit the host sets, 2 blocks by default, takes
    /// the processor out of the mix for good: its handle's `failed` says
    /// why, and only a new `Audio.start` plays again. In a browser and on
    /// NRDP a block past its hard limit ends at its next fuel check, which
    /// debug bakes and wasmFuel bakes give the processor; one without fuel
    /// ends only once it returns. A block that stalls the audio thread fails
    /// every processor: after a second in a browser, which drops the output,
    /// and after a tenth of a second on NRDP, which ends the thread.
    process(out: StaticArray<f32>, frames: i32, startFrame: f64): void;
}

/// Script that renders audio itself, started with `Audio.start`. It runs in
/// its own instance of the module, talking to other lanes only through the
/// shared memory in its argument: rings for messages and samples, snapshots
/// for knobs and meters, signals to wake a worker. A block reads them in place
/// with `receiveInto` and `latestInto`, which never allocate.
/// ```as
/// export class Knobs {
///     gain: f64 = 0.2;
///     pitch: f64 = 440;
/// }
///
/// export class Tone extends AudioProcessor<Snapshot<Knobs>> {
///     knobs: Snapshot<Knobs>? = null;
///     current: Knobs = new Knobs();
///     phase: f64 = 0;
///     rate: f64 = 0;
///     channels: i32 = 2;
///
///     override init(sampleRate: f64, maxFrames: i32, channels: i32, knobs: Snapshot<Knobs>): void {
///         this.knobs = knobs;
///         this.rate = sampleRate;
///         this.channels = channels;
///     }
///
///     override process(out: StaticArray<f32>, frames: i32, startFrame: f64): void {
///         this.knobs!.latestInto(this.current);
///         let channels = this.channels;
///         for (let i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
///             let sample = <f32>(Math.sin(this.phase) * this.current.gain);
///             for (let c = 0; c < channels; c++) {
///                 out[i * channels + c] = sample;
///             }
///             this.phase += 2 * Math.PI * this.current.pitch / this.rate;
///         }
///     }
/// }
/// ```
export abstract class AudioProcessor<A> extends AudioProcessorBase {
    /// Runs once before the first block: natively off the audio thread, in a
    /// browser on the audio worklet's render thread, so heavy setup there
    /// delays the mix. One still running after a second fails the processor,
    /// in a browser and on NRDP only when it has fuel. maxFrames is the most
    /// frames a block asks for, and channels how many interleave in each
    /// frame.
    init(sampleRate: f64, maxFrames: i32, channels: i32, arg: A): void;
}

/// A processor `Audio.start` started; `stop` takes it out of the mix.
export class AudioHandle extends Lane {
}

/// Plays `AudioSource` assets and reads the audio engine's clock.
///
/// Every play function returns the new `AudioSound`, or null when there is
/// no audio engine or the source was released.
/// ```as
/// let source = context.audio("myAudio");
/// if (source != null) {
///     // Start half a second from now.
///     let sound = Audio.playInTime(source, 0.5);
/// }
/// ```
export namespace Audio {
    /// Plays the source immediately.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     this.sound = Audio.play(source);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function play(source: AudioSource): AudioSound?;

    /// Plays the source at an absolute engine time in seconds, to the
    /// millisecond, for scheduling against `Audio.time`.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     this.sound = Audio.playAtTime(source, Audio.time() + 1);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function playAtTime(source: AudioSource, seconds: f64): AudioSound?;

    /// Plays the source after a delay in seconds, relative to the current
    /// engine time.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     this.sound = Audio.playInTime(source, this.scheduleSeconds);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function playInTime(source: AudioSource, seconds: f64): AudioSound?;

    /// Plays the source at an absolute engine time in PCM frames, for precise
    /// scheduling against `Audio.timeFrame`.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     let frame = Audio.timeFrame() + Audio.sampleRate();
    ///     this.sound = Audio.playAtFrame(source, frame);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function playAtFrame(source: AudioSource, frame: f64): AudioSound?;

    /// Plays the source after a delay in PCM frames, relative to the current
    /// engine time. Convert from seconds with frames = seconds *
    /// `Audio.sampleRate()`.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     this.sound = Audio.playInFrame(source, this.scheduleFrames);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function playInFrame(source: AudioSource, frame: f64): AudioSound?;

    /// Returns the absolute time of the audio engine in seconds, a clock
    /// independent of any sound.
    /// ```as
    /// override advance(seconds: f64): bool {
    ///     this.engineTime = Audio.time();
    ///     this.engineTimeFrame = Audio.timeFrame();
    ///     this.sampleRate = Audio.sampleRate();
    ///     return true;
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function time(): f64;

    /// Returns the absolute time of the audio engine in PCM frames.
    export function timeFrame(): f64;

    /// Returns the sample rate of the audio engine in Hz. Use it to convert
    /// seconds to frames: frames = seconds * sample rate.
    export function sampleRate(): f64;

    /// The rate in Hz a processor started now renders at, the one its init
    /// is given, or 0 when it would not play. In a browser and on NRDP it is
    /// the page's audio output rather than `Audio.sampleRate()`.
    /// ```as
    /// let samples = await source.toBlob(Audio.processorSampleRate(), Audio.processorChannels());
    /// ```
    export function processorSampleRate(): f64;

    /// The channels a processor started now renders, the count its init is
    /// given, or 0 when it would not play.
    /// ```as
    /// let stream = await source.stream(Audio.processorSampleRate(), Audio.processorChannels());
    /// ```
    export function processorChannels(): u32;

    /// Starts a processor rendering on the audio thread, mixed into the
    /// output, its argument deep copied into the processor's init. It returns
    /// at once: init runs later, natively off the audio thread and in a
    /// browser on the worklet's render thread, and the processor joins the

    /// writes each call, so Audio.start is never taken as a value.
    /// ```as
    /// this.player = Audio.start(() => new RingPlayer(), this.ring);
    /// ```
    @builtin export function start<A>(factory: () => AudioProcessor<A>, arg: A): AudioHandle;
}

/// A class that holds one value, so a value that cannot be null on its own can
/// be optional. Numbers, booleans and structs are never null, so an optional
/// one is written `Box<T>?`: `null` means no value.
///
/// Like the other std generics, `Box` does not take a struct type argument, so
/// use `Box_Vector` and `Box_Mat2D` for `Vector` and `Mat2D`.
/// ```as
/// import { Box } from "rive/box";
///
/// function half(value: f64): Box<f64>? {
///   return value > 0 ? new Box<f64>(value / 2) : null;
/// }
///
/// export function describe(value: f64): string {
///   return half(value)?.value.toString() ?? "none";
/// }
/// ```
export class Box<T> {
    /// The held value.
    value: T;

    /// Creates a box holding `value`.
    constructor(value: T);
}

/// A `Box` for a `Vector`, so an optional vector can be written
/// `Box_Vector?`.
export class Box_Vector {
    /// The held vector.
    value: Vector;

    /// Creates a box holding `value`.
    constructor(value: Vector);
}

/// A `Box` for a `Mat2D`, so an optional matrix can be written
/// `Box_Mat2D?`.
export class Box_Mat2D {
    /// The held matrix.
    value: Mat2D;

    /// Creates a box holding `value`.
    constructor(value: Mat2D);
}

/// Reads and writes binary data in an `ArrayBuffer`, such as file contents or
/// packed vertex data.
///
/// Offsets are byte positions starting at 0. Offsets, counts and values are
/// `f64` and truncated to integers. Integer writes keep the low bits of the

/// buffer throws `"buffer access out of bounds"`, as in Luau.

///
/// export function roundTrip(): f64 {
///   let b = Buffer.create(8);
///   Buffer.writeu16(b, 0, 513);
///   Buffer.writef32(b, 4, 1.5);
///   return Buffer.readu16(b, 0) + Buffer.readf32(b, 4);
/// }
/// ```

    /// Creates a zero filled buffer of `size` bytes. Throws for a negative
    /// size.

    /// The size of `b` in bytes.
    export function len(b: ArrayBuffer): f64;

    /// Reads an unsigned 8 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function readu8(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64): f64;

    /// Reads a signed 8 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function readi8(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64): f64;

    /// Reads an unsigned 16 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function readu16(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64): f64;

    /// Reads a signed 16 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function readi16(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64): f64;

    /// Reads an unsigned 32 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function readu32(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64): f64;

    /// Reads a signed 32 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function readi32(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64): f64;

    /// Reads a 32 bit float at `offset`.
    export function readf32(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64): f64;

    /// Reads a 64 bit float at `offset`.
    export function readf64(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64): f64;

    /// Writes `value` as an unsigned 8 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function writeu8(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64, value: f64): void;

    /// Writes `value` as a signed 8 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function writei8(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64, value: f64): void;

    /// Writes `value` as an unsigned 16 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function writeu16(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64, value: f64): void;

    /// Writes `value` as a signed 16 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function writei16(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64, value: f64): void;

    /// Writes `value` as an unsigned 32 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function writeu32(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64, value: f64): void;

    /// Writes `value` as a signed 32 bit integer at `offset`.
    export function writei32(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64, value: f64): void;

    /// Writes `value` as a 32 bit float at `offset`.
    export function writef32(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64, value: f64): void;

    /// Writes `value` as a 64 bit float at `offset`.
    export function writef64(b: ArrayBuffer, offset: f64, value: f64): void;

    /// Copies `count` bytes from `source` at `sourceOffset` into `target` at
    /// `targetOffset`. Without `count`, copies to the end of `source`. The
    /// ranges may overlap.
    export function copy(
        target: ArrayBuffer,
        targetOffset: f64,
        source: ArrayBuffer,
        sourceOffset: f64 = 0,
        count: f64 = NaN
    ): void;

    /// Sets `count` bytes of `b` from `offset` to `value`, truncated to a byte.
    /// Without `count`, fills to the end of `b`.
    export function fill(
        b: ArrayBuffer,
        offset: f64,
        value: f64,

    /// Reads `bitCount` bits, 0 to 32, starting `bitOffset` bits into `b`, as

    /// import { Buffer } from "rive/buffer";

    ///   Buffer.writeu8(b, 0, 0xa5);

    /// throws.
    export function writestring(
        b: ArrayBuffer,
        offset: f64,
        text: string,
        count: f64 = NaN
    ): void;
}

/// An offscreen target for Rive 2D drawing. Call `beginFrame` to get a
/// `Renderer`, draw with it, then call `endFrame`. Composite the result by
/// drawing `image`, or sample it in a shader through `image.view()`. Its
/// contents last until the next `beginFrame`, so a frame that skips it still
/// draws or samples the last one.
///
/// ```as
/// let canvas = context.canvas(256, 256);
/// if (canvas != null) {
///     let r = canvas.beginFrame(0xFF000000);
///     if (r != null) {
///         r.drawPath(path, paint);
///         canvas.endFrame();
///     }
///     renderer.drawImage(canvas.image, sampler, BlendMode.srcOver, 1);
/// }
/// ```
export class Canvas {
    /// Creates a canvas of the given size in pixels. A zero size allocates
    /// nothing until `resize`. `context.canvas()` does the same and answers
    /// null when the host cannot make a canvas.
    constructor(width: u32 = 0, height: u32 = 0);

    /// Width in pixels.
    get width(): u32;

    /// Height in pixels.
    get height(): u32;

    /// Resizes the canvas. Returns false, leaving the canvas as it was,
    /// between `beginFrame` and `endFrame` or when the device refuses the
    /// size. A reference to `image` kept across a resize follows the new
    /// backing.
    resize(width: u32, height: u32): bool;

    /// The image holding what the canvas drew, for `drawImage` on a
    /// `Renderer`. It is never null, and 0x0 until the canvas has a size.
    get image(): Image;

    /// Begins a frame and returns a `Renderer` that draws into the canvas
    /// until `endFrame`. `clearColor` is a packed ARGB color, such as
    /// `0xFF000000` for opaque black; the default is transparent. Returns
    /// null when the canvas has no size, a frame is already open, or the
    /// host cannot record canvas frames.
    beginFrame(clearColor: u32 = 0): Renderer?;

    /// Ends the frame, flushing its drawing into `image`. The renderer from
    /// `beginFrame` must not be used after this.
    endFrame(): void;

    /// Frees the canvas and its backing now instead of when it is collected.
    release(): void;
}

/// A view model property that notifies listeners when its value changes.
/// Each kind of property is a subclass with a typed `value`.
export class Property {
    /// Registers a listener that is called whenever the property's value
    /// changes. Listening stops when the host disposes the script instance
    /// that added it.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// function onHealthChanged(): void {
    ///     console.log("health changed");
    /// }
    ///
    /// let health = vm.getNumber("health");
    /// if (health != null) {
    ///     health.addListener(onHealthChanged);
    ///     health.value = 50; // Notifies onHealthChanged
    /// }
    /// ```
    addListener(listener: () => void): void;

    /// Registers a listener that receives `context` each time it is called,
    /// and keeps `context` alive while registered. Remove it with
    /// `removeListenerWith`.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// export class Cannon extends Node {
    ///     shots: i32 = 0;
    ///
    ///     override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///         let vm = context.viewModel();
    ///         if (vm != null) {
    ///             let fire = vm.getTrigger("fire");
    ///             if (fire != null) {
    ///                 fire.addListenerWith(this, (self: Cannon): void => {
    ///                     self.shots++;
    ///                 });
    ///             }
    ///         }
    ///         return true;
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    addListenerWith<K>(context: K, listener: (context: K) => void): void;

    /// Removes every registration of a listener added with `addListener`,
    /// matched by function.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// health.removeListener(onHealthChanged);
    /// ```
    removeListener(listener: () => void): void;

    /// Removes every registration of a listener added with `addListenerWith`
    /// with this same `context` and `listener`. Other contexts registered
    /// with the same function keep listening.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// export class Cannon extends Node {
    ///     fire: PropertyTrigger? = null;
    ///     shots: i32 = 0;
    ///
    ///     static onFire(self: Cannon): void {
    ///         self.shots++;
    ///     }
    ///
    ///     override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///         let vm = context.viewModel();
    ///         if (vm != null) {
    ///             let fire = vm.getTrigger("fire");
    ///             if (fire != null) {
    ///                 fire.addListenerWith(this, Cannon.onFire);
    ///                 this.fire = fire;
    ///             }
    ///         }
    ///         return true;
    ///     }
    ///
    ///     stopListening(): void {

/// A pointer interaction: the pointer's id and its position in local
/// coordinates.
///
/// `Node` pointer handlers receive one, and an `Artboard` instance takes one
/// to forward the interaction to its state machine.
/// ```as
/// export class RenderInstance extends Node {
///     @input character: Artboard? = null;
///     instance: Artboard? = null;
///     x: f32 = 100;
///     y: f32 = 50;
///
///     override init(context: Context): bool {
///         let character = this.character;
///         if (character != null) {
///             this.instance = character.instance();
///         }
///         return true;
///     }
///
///     override pointerDown(event: PointerEvent): void {
///         let instance = this.instance;
///         if (instance != null) {
///             let localPos = event.position - Vector.xy(this.x, this.y);
///             let localEvent = new PointerEvent(event.id, localPos);
///             if (instance.pointerDown(localEvent) != 0) {
///                 event.hit();
///             }
///         }
///     }
/// }
/// ```
export class PointerEvent {
    /// The unique identifier for the pointer.
    id: f64;

    /// The position of the pointer in local coordinates.
    position: Vector;

    /// The pointer's previous position in local coordinates. Set on events a
    /// `ListenerContext` delivers; `Node` pointer handlers read the origin.
    previousPosition: Vector;

    /// The kind of interaction: `pointerEnter`, `pointerExit`, `pointerDown`,
    /// `pointerUp`, `pointerMove`, `click`, `pointerDrag` or `unknown`.
    /// `pointerMove` handlers see every move, enter, click and drag this way.
    type: string;

    /// When the interaction happened, in seconds.
    timeStamp: f64;

    /// Creates a pointer event with the given id and position, for example to
    /// forward an interaction to an `Artboard` instance in its own space.
    /// ```as
    /// let event = new PointerEvent(0, Vector.xy(10, 20));
    /// ```
    constructor(
        id: f64,
        position: Vector,
        previousPosition: Vector = Vector(),
        type: string = "unknown",
        timeStamp: f64 = 0

    /// each move of a drag, and the release) or the event keeps travelling

    /// `ScrollConstraint` viewport is the usual one: without this, dragging a
    /// control inside a scroll view scrolls the view instead.

    /// whatever is behind it.

```as
/// Formats `value` as a whole number, truncated toward zero. The text is padded
/// on the left to `width` characters, with spaces or, when `zero` is true, with
/// zeros after any minus sign. Matches `%d` in `format`.
export function formatInt(value: f64, width: i32 = 0, zero: bool = false): string;

/// Formats `value` with `precision` digits after the decimal point, rounded
/// from its exact value with ties to even, as C's `printf` does: 0.125 gives
/// `0.12` with precision 2. `width` and `zero` pad as in `formatInt`. Matches
/// `%f` in `format`.
export function formatFixed(
    value: f64,
    precision: i32 = 6,
    width: i32 = 0,
    zero: bool = false
): string;

/// Formats the whole part of `value` in hexadecimal, lowercase unless `upper`
/// is true. A negative value prints as its 64 bit two's complement, so -1
/// gives `ffffffffffffffff`. `width` and `zero` pad as in `formatInt`. Matches
/// `%x` and `%X` in `format`.
export function formatHex(
    value: f64,
    width: i32 = 0,
    zero: bool = false,
    upper: bool = false
): string;

/// Formats `value` the way a number prints as text: the fewest digits that
/// read back as the same number, in fixed point such as `0.000001` or
/// `100000000000000000000`, and in exponent form such as `1e-07` or `1e+21`
/// beyond those. Special values print as `nan`, `inf` or `-inf`. Matches `%s`
/// given a number in `format`.
export function formatNumber(value: f64): string;

/// One argument to `format`: a number, a string or a bool. Create it with
/// `FormatArg.number`, `FormatArg.string` or `FormatArg.bool`.
export class FormatArg {
    /// An argument holding the number `value`.
    static number(value: f64): FormatArg;

    /// An argument holding the string `text`.
    static string(text: string): FormatArg;

    /// An argument holding the bool `flag`. Only `%*` accepts it.
    static bool(flag: bool): FormatArg;
}

/// Builds a string from `pattern`, replacing each specifier with the next
/// argument from `args`, as Luau's `string.format` does.
///
/// A specifier is `%`, optional flags, an optional width and an optional
/// `.precision`, each at most two digits, then one of:
///
/// | Specifier | Output |
/// | --- | --- |
/// | `%d` / `%i` | A whole number, truncated toward zero |
/// | `%u` | A whole number as unsigned, so a negative one wraps around 2^64 |
/// | `%o` / `%x` / `%X` | The unsigned whole number in octal, or in lowercase or uppercase hexadecimal |
/// | `%c` | The character with code `value`, modulo 256 |
/// | `%f` | A number with `precision` decimals, 6 by default |
/// | `%e` / `%E` | A number in exponent form, `1.500000e+03`, with `precision` decimals |
/// | `%g` / `%G` | `%f` when the exponent is at least -4 and below `precision`, else `%e`, with `precision` significant digits, 6 by default, and trailing zeros dropped |
/// | `%s` | Text, or a number as `formatNumber` prints it, with at most `precision` characters |
/// | `%q` | Text in double quotes, with quotes, backslashes and line breaks escaped |
/// | `%*` | Any argument as text, including a bool as `true` or `false`; takes no flags |
/// | `%%` | A literal `%` |
///
/// The flags are `-` to pad on the right, `+` to show a plus sign on positive
/// numbers, a space to put a space there instead, `#` for a `0x` prefix on
/// hexadecimal, a leading `0` on octal or a point that always shows, and `0`
/// to pad with zeros. Floats round from their exact value with ties to even,
/// as C's `printf` does. Number specifiers read a numeric string argument as a
/// number.
///
/// Like Luau, `format` throws for an unknown specifier, for a specifier with
/// no argument left, for a bool given to anything but `%*`, and for a string
/// that is not a number given to a number specifier.
/// ```as
/// import { format, FormatArg } from "rive/format";
///
/// export function label(name: string, score: f64): string {
///   // "Ana: 012.5 (0XFF) +1.2e+03" for score 12.5.
///   return format("%-4s %05.1f (%#X) %+.1e", [
///     FormatArg.string(name + ":"),
///     FormatArg.number(score),
///     FormatArg.number(255),
///     FormatArg.number(1234),
///   ]);
/// }
/// ```
export function format(pattern: string, args: Array<FormatArg>): string;
```

/// A GPU buffer for vertex, index or uniform data.
export class GPUBuffer {
    /// Size in bytes.

    /// Creates a buffer of `sizeInBytes` bytes for `usage`. When given,
    /// `data` is the initial contents and must be exactly `sizeInBytes`
    /// long. An `immutable` buffer takes its contents from `data` and cannot
    /// be updated afterward. Raises an error when `sizeInBytes` is 0, when
    /// `data` has another length, or when an `immutable` buffer has no `data`.
    ///
    /// The size is not checked against the shader's struct. Lay a uniform
    /// buffer out by hand to the WGSL alignment rules (`vec2` to 8 bytes,
    /// `vec3`, `vec4` and array elements to 16); a wrong offset reads garbage
    /// silently.
    constructor(usage: BufferUsage, sizeInBytes: u32, data: ArrayBuffer? = null, immutable: bool = false);

    /// A buffer for `usage` holding a copy of `byteCount` bytes of `blob`
    /// from byte `srcOffset` on, sized to them; a `byteCount` of zero takes
    /// the rest of the blob. As in `updateFromBlob`, the host copies straight
    /// from shared memory, so the blob may be released at once. An
    /// `immutable` buffer cannot be updated afterward, and the host keeps no
    /// CPU copy of it.
    ///
    /// Raises an error when the blob was released, or when the range runs
    /// past the end of the blob or is empty.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// let mesh = job.join()!.value;
    /// let vertices = GPUBuffer.fromBlob(BufferUsage.vertex, mesh, true);
    /// mesh.release();

    static fromBlob(usage: BufferUsage, blob: Blob, immutable: bool = false, byteCount: u32 = 0, srcOffset: u32 = 0): GPUBuffer;

    /// Copies bytes of `data`, starting at byte `srcOffset`, into the buffer
    /// at byte offset `dstOffset`. `byteCount` limits the copy, so a region
    /// of an oversized staging buffer uploads without slicing; zero copies
    /// the rest of `data` from `srcOffset`.
    ///
    /// Raises an error when the buffer is immutable, when the source range
    /// runs past the end of `data`, or when the copy runs past the end of
    /// the buffer.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// // Uploads bytes 64 to 127 of staging to the start of the buffer.
    /// buffer.update(0, staging, 64, 64);
    /// ```
    update(dstOffset: u32, data: ArrayBuffer, byteCount: u32 = 0, srcOffset: u32 = 0): void;

    /// As `update`, from a `Blob`. The host copies straight from shared
    /// memory, so the bytes never pass through the script's own: a job's
    /// result uploads without a staging buffer.

    /// Raises the errors `update` does, and one when the blob was released.
    ///
    /// ```as

    /// ```

///
/// ```as
/// let canvas = context.gpuCanvas(256, 256);

///     let color = new GPUColorAttachment();
///     color.loadOp = LoadOp.clear;
///     color.storeOp = StoreOp.store;
///     let desc = new GPUPassDesc();
///     desc.color = [color];
///     let pass = canvas.beginRenderPass(desc);

    get format(): u32;

    resize(width: u32, height: u32): bool;

    index = 1,

    /// Uniform data, bound with a `GPUBindGroupUBO`.
    uniform = 2,
}

/// the device; check `GPUFeatures` before using them.

    /// One 16 bit float channel. Rendering into it needs the `colorBufferHalfFloat` feature.
    r16float = 7,

    rgba32float = 8,

    rg32float = 9,

    r32float = 10,

    depth24plusStencil8 = 14,

    depth32float = 15,

    /// BC1 (DXT1) compressed RGBA. Needs the `bc` feature.
    bc1unorm = 17,

/// Raw decoded image pixels, delivered by `Context.decodeImage` to an
/// `ImageDecodeListener`.
export class DecodedImage {
    /// Width in pixels.
    width: u32;

    /// Height in pixels.
    height: u32;

    /// Premultiplied RGBA8 pixel data, `width * height * 4` bytes.
    data: ArrayBuffer;
}

/// Receives the result of `Context.decodeImage`. Extend it and override the
/// callbacks you need; both fire on a later advance.
/// ```as
/// class AvatarDecode extends ImageDecodeListener {
///     width: u32 = 0;
///     height: u32 = 0;
///
///     override onImageDecoded(image: DecodedImage): void {
///         this.width = image.width;
///         this.height = image.height;
///     }
/// }
/// ```
export abstract class ImageDecodeListener {
    /// Called with the decoded pixels when a decode succeeds.
    onImageDecoded(image: DecodedImage): void;

    /// Called with a description of the error when a decode fails.
    onImageDecodeFailed(message: string): void;
}

/// The bridge between a script and the Rive runtime, passed to `init`. It
/// gives access to:
/// - Update scheduling: request an `update` on the next frame.
/// - Data: the view models bound to the script's object or the root
///   artboard.
/// - Assets: the images, fonts, audio, blobs and shaders added to the file.
/// - Canvases: offscreen 2D and GPU render targets.
export class Context {
    /// Logs a message through the host: the CLI watch log and problems
    /// surface, or the editor console.
    /// ```as
    /// override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///     context.log("hello");
    ///     return true;
    /// }
    /// ```
    log(message: string): void;

    /// The value the host gave this run for name, or null when it gave none.
    /// rive-cli sets them with `--arg name=value`, so one bake runs with other
    /// options.
    /// ```as
    /// override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///     let steps = context.arg("steps");
    ///     this.steps = steps != null ? I32.parseInt(steps) : 4;
    ///     return true;
    /// }
    /// ```
    arg(name: string): string?;

    /// Marks the object as needing an update on the next frame. Call it when
    /// something has changed, for example from an event handler, and the
    /// runtime should call `update` again.
    ///
    /// Calls from inside `update` are ignored. Use it from `init`,
    /// `advance`, listener callbacks or event handlers instead.
    /// ```as
    /// override advance(seconds: f64): bool {
    ///     this.elapsed += seconds;
    ///     let context = this.context;
    ///     if (context != null) {
    ///         context.markNeedsUpdate();
    ///     }
    ///     return true;
    /// }
    /// ```
    markNeedsUpdate(): void;

    /// Returns the image asset with the given name, or null if not found.
    /// Draw it with `Renderer.drawImage`. See also `ImageSampler`.
    /// ```as
    /// export class DrawImage extends Node {
    ///     myImage: Image? = null;
    ///     sampler: ImageSampler = ImageSampler(ImageWrap.clamp, ImageWrap.clamp, ImageFilter.bilinear);
    ///
    ///     override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///         this.myImage = context.image("myImage");
    ///         return true;
    ///     }
    ///
    ///     override draw(renderer: Renderer): void {
    ///         let image = this.myImage;
    ///         if (image != null) {
    ///             renderer.drawImage(image, this.sampler, BlendMode.srcOver, 1);
    ///         }
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    image(name: string): Image?;

    /// Returns the font asset with the given name, or null if not found.
    /// ```as
    /// let font = context.font("Inter");
    /// if (font != null) {
    ///     let style = new TextRunStyle(font);
    ///     style.size = 24;
    /// }
    /// ```
    font(name: string): Font?;

    /// Returns the audio asset with the given name, or null if not found.
    /// Play it with the `Audio` functions.
    /// ```as
    /// export class AudioExample extends Node {
    ///     source: AudioSource? = null;
    ///
    ///     override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///         this.source = context.audio("myAudio");
    ///         return true;
    ///     }
    ///
    ///     override pointerDown(event: PointerEvent): void {
    ///         let source = this.source;
    ///         if (source != null) {
    ///             Audio.play(source);
    ///         }
    ///         event.hit();
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    audio(name: string): AudioSource?;

    /// Returns the `ViewModel` bound to the object's immediate data context,
    /// or null before data binds. This is the most common way to read data
    /// bound properties from a script.
    /// ```as
    /// override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///     let vm = context.viewModel();
    ///     if (vm != null) {
    ///         this.cannon = vm.getTrigger("cannon");
    ///     }
    ///     return true;
    /// }
    /// ```
    viewModel(): ViewModel?;

    /// Returns the `ViewModel` bound to the root artboard's data context, or
    /// null if there is none. Useful for reaching top level data from a
    /// deeply nested object.
    /// ```as
    /// let vm = context.rootViewModel();
    /// if (vm != null) {
    ///     let score = vm.getNumber("score");
    /// }
    /// ```
    rootViewModel(): ViewModel?;

    /// Returns the global `ViewModel` with the given name, or null if there is
    /// no global view model by that name or none is currently bound. Global
    /// view models are shared, singleton like view models addressed by name
    /// rather than through the object's own data context.
    /// ```as
    /// let settings = context.globalViewModel("AppSettings");
    /// if (settings != null) {
    ///     let volume = settings.getNumber("volume");
    /// }
    /// ```
    globalViewModel(name: string): ViewModel?;

    /// Returns the names of all global view models defined in the file, in
    /// file order. Pass any of them to `globalViewModel` to fetch that view
    /// model. Returns an empty array when the file defines none.
    /// ```as
    /// let names = context.globalViewModelNames();
    /// for (let i = 0; i < names.length; i++) {
    ///     context.log(names[i]);
    /// }
    /// ```
    globalViewModelNames(): Array<string>;

    /// Returns the data context provided to this object, or null if there is
    /// none.
    /// ```as
    /// let dc = context.dataContext();
    /// if (dc != null) {
    ///     let parent = dc.parent();
    ///     let vm = dc.viewModel();
    /// }
    /// ```
    dataContext(): DataContext?;

    /// Creates a 2D `Canvas` for Rive Renderer drawing, or returns null when
    /// the host cannot create one. Draw into it with `beginFrame` and
    /// `endFrame` during `draw`.
    ///
    /// A zero width or height, the default, creates a deferred canvas with no
    /// backing texture, useful in layouts that do not know their size at
    /// `init`. Call `resize` once the size is known. While deferred, `width`
    /// and `height` read 0 and `beginFrame` returns null.
    /// ```as
    /// override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///     this.canvas = context.canvas(256, 256);
    ///     return true;
    /// }
    ///
    /// override draw(renderer: Renderer): void {
    ///     let canvas = this.canvas;
    ///     if (canvas == null) {
    ///         return;
    ///     }
    ///     let frame = canvas.beginFrame(0xFF202020);
    ///     if (frame != null) {
    ///         frame.drawPath(this.path, this.paint);
    ///         canvas.endFrame();
    ///     }
    ///     renderer.drawImage(canvas.image, ImageSampler(), BlendMode.srcOver, 1);
    /// }
    /// ```
    canvas(width: u32 = 0, height: u32 = 0): Canvas?;

    /// Creates a `GPUCanvas`, a 1x presentation target, or returns null when
    /// the host cannot create one. Render to it with `beginRenderPass`. For
    /// MSAA, allocate the multisampled color and depth textures yourself and
    /// resolve into the canvas.
    ///
    /// A zero width or height, the default, creates a deferred canvas with no
    /// backing texture, useful in layouts that do not know their size at
    /// `init`. Call `resize` once the size is known. While deferred, `width`
    /// and `height` read 0 and `view` is null.
    gpuCanvas(width: u32 = 0, height: u32 = 0): GPUCanvas?;

    /// Returns Rive's own render target: passes into it land under all of
    /// Rive's content. It cannot be sampled and starts each frame undefined,
    /// so the first pass must clear or cover it. With a `sampleCount` of 1 it
    /// can resolve a script's MSAA texture. On a frame the host hides it,
    /// `view` is null and passes into it are dropped.
    ///
    /// Returns null where the host can never expose one; keep a `gpuCanvas`
    /// and draw its image instead.
    gpuTarget(): GPUTarget?;

    /// Returns the GPU features and limits the current backend supports.
    features(): GPUFeatures;

    /// Returns the bytes of the blob asset with the given name, or null if
    /// not found or empty. Useful for loading custom data files embedded in
    /// the Rive file. The blob's size is the buffer's `byteLength`.
    /// ```as
    /// let bytes = context.blob("myBlob");
    /// if (bytes != null && bytes.byteLength > 0) {
    ///     let first = Uint8Array.wrap(bytes)[0];
    /// }
    /// ```
    blob(name: string): ArrayBuffer?;

    /// Returns the compiled shader modules for the current backend from the
    /// shader asset with the given name (as added in the editor, with no
    /// `.wgsl` extension), ready for a `GPUPipelineDesc`. Returns null when
    /// the asset is not found or was not compiled for this backend.
    shader(name: string): GPUShaderModule?;

    /// Decodes compressed image data (PNG, JPEG or WebP) into premultiplied
    /// RGBA8 pixels. The listener receives the `DecodedImage`, or the error,
    /// on a later advance.
    ///
    /// Returns a token for `cancelImageDecode`. Returns 0 when this platform
    /// cannot decode images, after calling the listener's
    /// `onImageDecodeFailed`.
    /// ```as
    /// let bytes = context.blob("avatar");
    /// if (bytes != null) {
    ///     this.decodeToken = context.decodeImage(bytes, new AvatarDecode());
    /// }
    /// ```
    decodeImage(bytes: ArrayBuffer, listener: ImageDecodeListener): u32;

    /// Cancels a pending decode started by `decodeImage`. Its listener is not
    /// called.
    cancelImageDecode(token: u32): void;

    /// Decodes the bytes of a .riv file, such as a `fetch` response body.
    /// The promise resolves with the file, or rejects with
    /// "malformed: <message>" or "unsupportedVersion: <message>". It may
    /// settle on a later frame, so wait for it with `await` or `andThen`
    /// rather than reading its status right away. Only assets embedded in the
    /// file load, and its scripts run only if Rive signed them.
    ///
    /// ```as
    /// async loadCharacter(context: Context): Promise<void> {
    ///     let vm = context.viewModel();
    ///     if (vm == null) {
    ///         return;
    ///     }
    ///     let character = vm.getArtboard("character");
    ///     let response = await fetch("https://example.com/a.riv");
    ///     let file = await context.decodeFile(await response.arrayBuffer());
    ///     if (character != null) {
    ///         character.value = file.bindableArtboard();
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    decodeFile(bytes: ArrayBuffer): Promise<RiveFile>;

    /// Returns the id of the shader asset with the given name, or 0 when the
    /// file has none. Modules returned by `shader` already carry it.
    shaderAssetId(name: string): u32;
}

/// The hooks every script shares. A script extends one of its subclasses,
/// `Node`, `Layout`, `Converter`, `PathEffect`, `ListenerAction`,
/// `TransitionCondition` or `Interpolator`, never `Protocol` itself.
///
/// Override only the hooks the script needs; the host calls only those.
/// Abstract hooks such as `Converter.convert` are required. Declare inputs
/// as fields marked `@input`.
/// ```as
/// export class MyNode extends Node {
///     @input speed: f64 = 1;
///     @input title: string = "Rive";
///     @input enabled: bool = false;
///
///     override init(context: Context): bool {
///         return true;
///     }
/// }
/// ```
export abstract class Protocol {
    /// Called once when the script is created. Return true if
    /// initialization succeeds, or false to stop the script.
    /// ```as
    /// override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///     this.context = context;
    ///     return true;
    /// }
    /// ```
    init(context: Context): bool;

    /// Called every frame to advance the script over time. `seconds` is the
    /// time since the previous frame. Return true to keep receiving advance
    /// calls.
    /// ```as
    /// override advance(seconds: f64): bool {
    ///     this.elapsed += seconds;
    ///     return true;
    /// }
    /// ```
    advance(seconds: f64): bool;

    /// Called once when the host drops the script, for example when its
    /// artboard is disposed or the editor reloads. Release long lived
    /// resources here.
    dispose(): void;
}

/// A script that renders shapes, images, text, artboards and more. A
/// scripted node can be attached to any Node and renders in the local
/// transform space of the hosting Node.
///
/// It inherits `init`, `advance` and `dispose` from `Protocol`.
/// ```as
/// export class Spinner extends Node {
///     @input speed: f64 = 1;
///     angle: f64 = 0;
///     path: Path = new Path();
///     paint: Paint = new Paint();
///
///     override init(context: Context): bool {
///         this.paint.color = Color.rgba(255, 180, 90, 255);
///         return true;
///     }
///
///     override advance(seconds: f64): bool {
///         this.angle += seconds * this.speed;
///         return true;
///     }
///
///     override draw(renderer: Renderer): void {
///         let x = <f32>(Math.cos(this.angle) * 50);
///         let y = <f32>(Math.sin(this.angle) * 50);
///         this.path.reset();
///         this.path.moveTo(Vector.xy(0, 0));
///         this.path.lineTo(Vector.xy(x, y));
///         this.path.lineTo(Vector.xy(-y, x));
///         this.path.close();
///         renderer.drawPath(this.path, this.paint);
///     }
/// }
/// ```
export abstract class Node extends Protocol {
    /// Called when an input value changes, and on the next frame after
    /// `Context.markNeedsUpdate`.
    /// ```as
    /// override update(): void {

/// ```as
/// export class Panel extends Layout {

///     height: f64 = 0;
///
///     override measure(): Vector {

///         this.height = height;
///     }

/// export class AddOne extends Converter {
///     override convert(input: DataValue): DataValue? {
///         if (input.isNumber()) {
///             return new DataValueNumber((<DataValueNumber>input).value + 1);
///         }
///         return null;
///     }

///     override reverseConvert(input: DataValue): DataValue? {
///         if (input.isNumber()) {
///             return new DataValueNumber((<DataValueNumber>input).value - 1);
///         }
///         return null;
///     }

    abstract convert(input: DataValue): DataValue?;

    /// Converts an output value back to an input value, a view model
    /// property.
    reverseConvert(input: DataValue): DataValue?;

/// `advance`.

/// ```as
/// export class Shrink extends PathEffect {
///     outPath: Path = new Path();
///
///     override update(path: Path, node: PathEffectNode): Path {
///         this.outPath.reset();
///         this.outPath.add(path, Mat2D.withScale(0.5, 0.5));

///     }

    /// path to render.

///
///     override performAction(context: ListenerContext): void {
///         if (context.isPointerEvent()) {
///             this.clicks++;
///         }
///     }

/// ```

    /// describing the event that triggered it.
    performAction(context: ListenerContext): void;

/// A condition a transition between state machine states must meet to be
