```as
/// How a promise settled, from `settled` on a `Promise`.
export class Settled<T> {
    /// True when the promise fulfilled, so `value` is readable.
    ok: bool;

    /// True when the promise was cancelled.
    cancelled: bool;

    /// The rejection error, the reason after a cancellation, or
    /// empty when `ok` is true.
    error: string;

    /// The fulfilled value. Throws when `ok` is false.
    get value(): T;
}

/// A value that will be available in the future, or an error if the work behind
/// it fails. Create one with `new Promise<T>()` and settle it once with
/// `resolve` or `reject`, or start from `Promise.resolve`, `Promise.reject` or
/// `Promise.all`. Chain work with `andThen`, `catch`, `finally`, `map`,
/// `flatMap` and `recover`, or `await` it inside an `async` function.
///
/// Each chaining method returns a new promise that settles once its handler
/// has run, so steps chain one after another. A rejection skips the steps that
/// have no rejection handler and reaches the next `catch`. Errors are strings.
/// Handlers run inside the `resolve` or `reject` call that settles the promise,
/// or right away when it has already settled. A handler that throws stops the
/// script rather than rejecting its chained promise; return
/// `Promise.reject` from `flatMap` to reject instead.
///
/// `await p` gives the fulfilled value. A rejection or cancellation stops the
/// async function and rejects its promise with the same error, or with the
/// cancel's reason, `"Promise was cancelled"` unless it gave one. To handle a
/// failure inline, await `p.settled()`, which always fulfills. Each resumed
/// function runs inside the call that settled its promise, so a chain of
/// thousands of async functions awaiting each other can run out of stack.
/// ```as
/// import { Promise } from "rive/promise";
///
/// let ready = new Promise<f64>();
/// let result = 0.0;
///
/// async function doubled(): Promise<f64> {
///   let value = await ready;
///   return value * 2;
/// }
///
/// export function start(): void {
///   doubled()
///     .map((value: f64): f64 => value + 1)
///     .andThen((value: f64): void => {
///       result = value;
///     })
///     .catch((error: string): void => {
///       result = -1;
///     });
///   // Runs the rest of doubled, then map and andThen: result is 43.
///   ready.resolve(21);
/// }
/// ```
export class Promise<T> extends PromiseLink {
    /// A promise already fulfilled with `value`.
    /// ```as
    /// let ready = Promise.resolve<f64>(42);
    /// ```
    static resolve<V>(value: V): Promise<V>;

    /// A promise already rejected with `error`. Name the value type, which the
    /// error cannot tell.
    /// ```as
    /// let failed = Promise.reject<f64>("not found");
    /// ```
    static reject<V>(error: string = "rejected"): Promise<V>;

    /// A promise that fulfills with the values of `promises`, in their order,
    /// once every one has fulfilled. It rejects with the first rejection, and
    /// then cancels the other inputs that nothing else waits on. Cancelling it
    /// cancels those inputs too. An empty list fulfills right away. The inputs
    /// need a value type, so `Promise<void>` cannot be combined.
    /// ```as
    /// import { Promise } from "rive/promise";
    ///
    /// export function total(a: Promise<f64>, b: Promise<f64>): Promise<f64> {
    ///   return Promise.all<f64>([a, b]).map((values: Array<f64>): f64 =>
    ///     values[0] + values[1]);
    /// }
    /// ```
    static all<V>(promises: Array<Promise<V>>): Promise<Array<V>>;

    /// Registers `onFulfilled` to run with the value when the promise fulfills,
    /// and `onRejected` to run with the error when it rejects. Returns a new
    /// promise that fulfills once the handler that ran returns. Without
    /// `onRejected`, a rejection passes to the new promise unchanged. Handlers
    /// run in the order they were added. For a handler that returns a value, use
    /// `map` or `flatMap`.
    andThen(
        onFulfilled: (value: T) => void,
        onRejected: ((error: string) => void)? = null,
    ): Promise<void>;

    /// Registers `onRejected` to run with the error when the promise rejects.
    /// Returns a new promise that fulfills once the promise fulfills or the
    /// handler returns. For a handler that returns a replacement value, use
    /// `recover`.
    catch(onRejected: (error: string) => void): Promise<void>;

    /// Registers `onFinally` to run once the promise fulfills or rejects, after
    /// every other handler. It never runs for a cancelled promise. Returns a new
    /// promise that settles like this one once `onFinally` returns.
    finally(onFinally: () => void): Promise<T>;

    /// Returns a new promise that fulfills with what `onFulfilled` returns when
    /// given this promise's value: Luau's `andThen` with a handler that returns a
    /// value. A rejection passes through unchanged. The new value type comes
    /// from the handler's return type, so give a function expression one, or
    /// name it as in `map<string>`.
    /// ```as
    /// import { Promise } from "rive/promise";
    ///
    /// export function label(count: Promise<f64>): Promise<string> {
    ///   return count.map((value: f64): string => value.toString() + " items");
    /// }
    /// ```
    map<U>(onFulfilled: (value: T) => U): Promise<U>;

    /// Returns a new promise that follows the promise `onFulfilled` returns when
    /// given this promise's value: Luau's `andThen` with a handler that returns a
    /// promise. It fulfills, rejects or is cancelled as that promise is, so
    /// returning `Promise.reject` rejects it. A rejection of this promise passes
    /// through unchanged. The new value type comes from the handler's return
    /// type, as with `map`.
    /// ```as
    /// import { Promise } from "rive/promise";
    ///
    /// function check(value: f64): Promise<f64> {
    ///   return value >= 0 ? Promise.resolve<f64>(value) : Promise.reject<f64>("negative");
    /// }
    ///
    /// export function validated(input: Promise<f64>): Promise<f64> {
    ///   return input.flatMap((value: f64): Promise<f64> => check(value));
    /// }
    /// ```
    flatMap<U>(onFulfilled: (value: T) => Promise<U>): Promise<U>;

    /// Returns a new promise that fulfills with this promise's value, or with
    /// what `onRejected` returns when this promise rejects: Luau's `catch` with
    /// a handler that returns a value.
    /// ```as
    /// import { Promise } from "rive/promise";
    ///
    /// export function orZero(value: Promise<f64>): Promise<f64> {
    ///   return value.recover((error: string): f64 => 0);
    /// }
    /// ```
    recover(onRejected: (error: string) => T): Promise<T>;

    /// Cancels a pending promise for good: its `onCancel` hooks run, none of
    /// its handlers ever will, and async functions awaiting it stop. The
    /// promises chained from it are cancelled too, and the promise it was
    /// chained from is cancelled once every promise chained from that one is
    /// cancelled and no async function awaits it. Cancelling the promise of an
    /// async function stops that function, and cancels the promise it awaits
    /// when nothing else waits on that one. The reason is what `settled()`
    /// reports and what awaiting functions reject with, here and in the
    /// promises chained from it. Does nothing once the promise has settled.
    /// Returns this promise.
    cancel(reason: string = "Promise was cancelled"): Promise<T>;

    /// Registers `hook` to run when the promise is cancelled, to clean up work
    /// in flight such as a network request. Hooks add up rather than replace
    /// each other. Ignored once the promise has settled. Returns this promise.
    onCancel(hook: () => void): Promise<T>;

    /// The current state: `"Pending"`, `"Fulfilled"`, `"Rejected"` or
    /// `"Cancelled"`.
    getStatus(): string;

    /// Fulfills a pending promise with `value` and runs its handlers. Does
    /// nothing once the promise has settled or been cancelled.
    resolve(value: T): void;

    /// Rejects a pending promise with `error` and runs its handlers. Does
    /// nothing once the promise has settled or been cancelled.
    reject(error: string): void;

    /// A promise that always fulfills with a `Settled` telling how this one
    /// settled, so an async function can handle a failure without stopping.
    /// Cancelling it cancels this promise when nothing else waits on it.
    /// ```as
    /// import { Promise } from "rive/promise";
    ///
    /// async function load(source: Promise<string>): Promise<string> {
    ///   let outcome = await source.settled();
    ///   if (!outcome.ok) {
    ///     return "failed: " + outcome.error;
    ///   }
    ///   return outcome.value;
    /// }
    /// ```
    settled<S = T>(): Promise<Settled<S>>;
}
```

/// Draws paths and images, manages clipping and applies transforms. A node
/// receives one in its `draw` method, valid only for that call.
export class Renderer {
    /// Saves the current rendering state, including the transform, clipping and
    /// modulation, until the matching `restore`.
    /// ```as
    /// export class MyGame extends Node {
    ///   enemies: Array<Artboard> = [];
    ///
    ///   override draw(renderer: Renderer): void {
    ///     for (let i = 0; i < this.enemies.length; i++) {
    ///       renderer.save();
    ///       this.enemies[i].draw(renderer);
    ///       renderer.restore();
    ///     }
    ///   }
    /// }
    /// ```
    save(): void;

    /// Restores the most recently saved rendering state.
    /// ```as
    /// renderer.save();
    /// renderer.transform(Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 0));
    /// renderer.drawPath(path, paint);
    /// renderer.restore();
    /// ```
    restore(): void;

    /// Applies a transform on top of the current one. Transforms accumulate until
    /// the matching `restore`.
    /// ```as
    /// let m = Mat2D.withScale(2, 3);
    /// // Adjust matrix terms directly for additional skew or stretch.
    /// m.xx = 5;
    ///
    /// renderer.save();
    /// renderer.transform(m);
    /// renderer.drawImage(image, sampler, BlendMode.srcOver, 1);
    /// renderer.restore();
    /// ```
    transform(m: Mat2D): void;

    /// Draws `path` with `paint`.
    /// ```as
    /// export class Rectangle extends Node {
    ///   path: Path = new Path();
    ///   paint: Paint = new Paint();
    ///
    ///   override draw(renderer: Renderer): void {
    ///     renderer.drawPath(this.path, this.paint);
    ///   }
    /// }
    /// ```
    drawPath(path: Path, paint: Paint): void;

    /// Restricts later drawing to the area inside `path`. The clip stays in effect
    /// until the matching `restore`.
    /// ```as
    /// renderer.save();
    /// renderer.clipPath(clip);
    /// renderer.drawImage(image, sampler, BlendMode.srcOver, 1);
    /// renderer.restore();
    /// ```
    clipPath(path: Path): void;

    /// Multiplies the opacity of later draws by `opacity`, from 0 to 1. Calls stack
    /// multiplicatively and are scoped by `save` and `restore`.
    /// ```as
    /// renderer.save();
    /// renderer.modulateOpacity(0.5);
    /// renderer.drawPath(path, paint);
    /// renderer.restore();
    /// ```
    modulateOpacity(opacity: f64): void;

    /// Multiplies `color` into later draws, channel by channel. Calls stack like
    /// `modulateOpacity` and are scoped by `save` and `restore`.
    modulateColor(color: Color): void;

    /// Sets the modulation color outright instead of multiplying, which lets an
    /// inner scope undo an outer one: draw an artboard under black, then set the
    /// color for the drawables that should keep their paint. Scoped by `save` and
    /// `restore`. Inside a draw visitor it ends with the visit, so the visitor
    /// needs no `save` or `restore` of its own.
    setColorModulation(color: Color): void;

    /// Draws `image` with `sampler`, `blend` and `opacity`.
    /// ```as
    /// export class DrawImage extends Node {
    ///   myImage: Image? = null;
    ///   sampler: ImageSampler = ImageSampler(ImageWrap.clamp, ImageWrap.clamp, ImageFilter.bilinear);
    ///
    ///   override init(context: Context): bool {
    ///     this.myImage = context.image("myImage");
    ///     return true;
    ///   }
    ///
    ///   override draw(renderer: Renderer): void {
    ///     let image = this.myImage;
    ///     if (image != null) {
    ///       renderer.drawImage(image, this.sampler, BlendMode.srcOver, 1);
    ///     }
    ///   }
    /// }
    /// ```
    drawImage(image: Image, sampler: ImageSampler, blend: BlendMode, opacity: f32): void;

    /// Draws `image` over a mesh: `vertices` holds the positions, `uvs` the texture
    /// coordinates and `triangles` the vertex indices.
    /// ```as
    /// renderer.drawImageMesh(
    ///   image,
    ///   sampler,
    ///   vertices,
    ///   uvs,
    ///   triangles,
    ///   BlendMode.srcOver,
    ///   1
    /// );
    /// ```
    drawImageMesh(
        image: Image,
        sampler: ImageSampler,
        vertices: VertexBuffer,
        uvs: VertexBuffer,
        triangles: TriangleBuffer,
        blend: BlendMode,
        opacity: f32
    ): void;

    /// Draws one mesh once per entry of `instances`, in a single call. The blend
    /// mode is always `srcOver`. Opacity and the UV transform come from each
    /// instance.
    /// ```as
    /// renderer.drawImageMeshInstanced(
    ///   image,
    ///   sampler,
    ///   vertices,
    ///   uvs,
    ///   triangles,
    ///   instances
    /// );
    /// ```
    drawImageMeshInstanced(
        image: Image,
        sampler: ImageSampler,
        vertices: VertexBuffer,
        uvs: VertexBuffer,
        triangles: TriangleBuffer,
        instances: MeshInstances
    ): void;
}

/// A feature a runtime may lack, because it shipped before the feature did
/// or was built without it.
export enum Feature {
    /// Parallel calls: `Parallel.run`, `Parallel.runParts` and
    /// `Parallel.runUpTo` from rive/parallel.
    parallelCalls = 0,
}

/// Whether the runtime running this script has feature. A runtime from
/// before a feature answers false for it. Only the main lane may ask.
/// ```as
/// import { Feature, supports } from "rive/runtime";
///
/// const parallelCalls = supports(Feature.parallelCalls);
/// ```
export function supports(feature: Feature): bool;

```as
/// A handle on memory every lane shares, by its process wide id. On the
/// main lane each handle holds its object until the handle is collected or
/// released. A job, worker or audio processor holds each object it was
/// started with or received once, until it releases it or is gone. A value
/// sent through a ring or snapshot holds what it names while in flight, so
/// the sender may let go at once: a ring's record until it is read, a
/// snapshot's value until another replaces it. The object goes once nothing
/// holds it, or with the script that made it.
@sendable
export class Shared {
    /// The process wide id every lane names the object by; 0 once released.
    id: u32;

    /// A handle on the object id names, such as an id kept in a region. On
    /// the main lane it takes a hold of its own, and its id is 0 when the
    /// object is gone or another script's.
    constructor(id: u32);

    /// Gives back this handle's hold now instead of when it is collected.
    /// Off the main lane it gives back what the lane created or holds; a
    /// long lived worker releases what it made or received once done with it.
    release(): void;
}

/// Bytes that never change once made, so any lane reads them without a
/// lock, and sending one to a job, worker or audio processor copies nothing.
/// A job may make one for a large result; it lasts while the job's handle
/// does, unless the main lane decodes it. A worker holds one it makes until
/// it releases it, or until the worker is over and its handle goes, so a
/// long lived worker releases each blob it posts.
/// ```as
/// let tile = Blob.from(bytes);
/// let job = Jobs.run(decodeTile, tile);
/// ```
@sendable
export class Blob extends Shared {
    /// A blob holding a copy of bytes, or of byteLength of them from
    /// byteOffset on, so part of a buffer needs no slice first; -1 takes the
    /// rest. Throws when the range leaves bytes.
    static from(bytes: ArrayBuffer, byteOffset: i32 = 0, byteLength: i32 = -1): Blob;

    /// A blob holding a copy of values, a typed array or an Array or
    /// StaticArray of numbers, or of count of them from offset on; -1 takes
    /// the rest. Throws when the range leaves values.
    static fromArray<U extends ArrayLike<number>>(values: U, offset: i32 = 0, count: i32 = -1): Blob;

    /// 0 once released.
    get byteLength(): u32;

    /// A copy of the bytes in this lane's memory.
    toArrayBuffer(): ArrayBuffer;

    /// Copies the bytes from srcOffset on into out, which is an ArrayBuffer, a
    /// typed array, or an Array or StaticArray of numbers, and answers how
    /// many it copied: fewer where the blob ends first. dstOffset, count and
    /// the answer count bytes for an ArrayBuffer and numbers for an array,
    /// which receives only whole values. A count of -1 fills the rest of out.
    /// Throws when the range leaves out. It allocates nothing, so audio code
    /// reads a blob this way.
    readInto<U>(srcOffset: u32, out: U, dstOffset: i32 = 0, count: i32 = -1): u32;
}

/// Bytes behind one lock. A lane holds at most one region at a time, so the
/// lock can never deadlock; joining a job while holding one throws.
/// ```as
/// let stats = SharedRegion.create(64);
/// stats.exclusive((view) => {
///     view.setU32(0, view.getU32(0) + 1);
/// });
/// ```
@sendable
export class SharedRegion extends Shared {
    /// A zeroed region of size bytes.
    static create(size: u32): SharedRegion;

    /// The region's bytes; 0 once it is gone.
    get size(): u32;

    /// True once a lane trapped while holding the region, so its bytes may be
    /// half written.
    get poisoned(): bool;

    /// Runs fn holding the region's lock. A wait never outlasts the
    /// caller's call budget, nor two seconds without one (a tenth of a
    /// second on the web's main thread); past that it throws. A lock asked
    /// for in the last 20 ms of a call waits at most half of what is left.
    exclusive(fn: (view: RegionView) => void): void;

    /// As exclusive, giving up after the given seconds, or the limits
    /// exclusive waits under; false when it did.
    tryExclusive(fn: (view: RegionView) => void, seconds: f64 = 0): bool;

    /// The word at a 4 byte aligned offset, read without the lock. Each
    /// atomic throws outside the region or once it is gone.
    atomicLoad(offset: u32): u32;

    /// Stores the word at a 4 byte aligned offset without the lock.
    atomicStore(offset: u32, value: u32): void;

    /// Adds and answers the word's value before the add.
    atomicAdd(offset: u32, value: u32): u32;

    /// Swaps in desired when the word equals expected; answers the value it
    /// held, so equality with expected means the swap happened.
    atomicCompareExchange(offset: u32, expected: u32, desired: u32): u32;
}

/// A region's bytes while its lock is held; valid only inside exclusive.
export class RegionView {
    /// The region's id.
    id: u32;

    /// Reads the u8 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    getU8(offset: u32): u8;

    /// Reads the u32 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    getU32(offset: u32): u32;

    /// Reads the i32 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    getI32(offset: u32): i32;

    /// Reads the f32 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    getF32(offset: u32): f32;

    /// Reads the f64 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    getF64(offset: u32): f64;

    /// Writes the u8 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    setU8(offset: u32, value: u8): void;

    /// Writes the u32 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    setU32(offset: u32, value: u32): void;

    /// Writes the i32 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    setI32(offset: u32, value: i32): void;

    /// Writes the f32 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    setF32(offset: u32, value: f32): void;

    /// Writes the f64 at offset; throws outside the region or its lock.
    setF64(offset: u32, value: f64): void;

    /// Copies count bytes out.
    readBytes(offset: u32, count: u32): ArrayBuffer;

    /// Copies the bytes from offset on into out, which is an ArrayBuffer, a
    /// typed array, or an Array or StaticArray of numbers. dstOffset and count
    /// count bytes for an ArrayBuffer and numbers for an array, and a count of
    /// -1 fills the rest of out. Throws when the range leaves out, the region
    /// or its lock. It allocates nothing.
    readInto<U>(offset: u32, out: U, dstOffset: i32 = 0, count: i32 = -1): void;

    /// Copies values, which is an ArrayBuffer, a typed array, or an Array or
    /// StaticArray of numbers, in at offset. srcOffset and count count bytes
    /// for an ArrayBuffer and numbers for an array, and a count of -1 takes
    /// the rest of values. Throws when the range leaves values, the region or
    /// its lock.
    writeFrom<U>(offset: u32, values: U, srcOffset: i32 = 0, count: i32 = -1): void;

    /// Stores a Sendable value at offset, length first; answers the bytes
    /// used. A region cannot hold shared objects, so a value naming one
    /// throws; send it through a ring or snapshot.
    @sends
    storeValue<T>(offset: u32, value: T): u32;

    /// Loads what storeValue stored at offset, as the type it was stored as.
    @sends
    loadValue<T>(offset: u32): T;
}

/// An eventcount: notify bumps the sequence. Read seq before checking a
/// condition, so a notify in between is never missed.
@sendable
export class Signal extends Shared {
    /// A signal whose sequence starts at 0.
    static create(): Signal;

    /// Bumps the sequence and wakes every wait on it. It never waits, so
    /// the audio thread may notify.
    notify(): void;

    /// How many notifies the signal has seen; 0 once it is gone.
    get seq(): f64;

    /// True once seq passed after, a sequence read earlier.
    changedSince(after: f64): bool;

    /// Settles once seq passes after, with the new sequence; with
    /// kWaitTimedOut once the given seconds pass, with kWaitGone when the
    /// signal goes, and inside a worker with kWaitStopping when it is being
    /// stopped. Waiting suspends only this async call, never a thread; on
    /// the main lane it settles on an advance.
    next(after: f64, seconds: f64 = Infinity): Promise<f64>;

    /// Waits on the main lane, blocking as a job's join does, until seq
    /// passes after: answers the new sequence, kWaitTimedOut once the given
    /// seconds pass, or kWaitGone when the signal is gone. The wait never
    /// outlasts the call's budget, nor two seconds without one; on the
    /// web's main thread it spins and lasts at most a tenth of a second,
    /// and without threads it never waits. It throws inside
    /// SharedRegion.exclusive. Only the main lane may block: a worker
    /// awaits next.
    /// ```as
    /// let seen = done.seq;
    /// requests.post(route);
    /// if (done.waitWithin(seen, 0.004) > seen) {
    ///     this.show(results.latest()!.value);
    /// }
    /// ```
    waitWithin(after: f64, seconds: f64): f64;
}

/// Lets workers that split one computation meet between its steps, and
/// combine a share of f32 values from each as they meet. The caller numbers
/// the rounds and gives each its participant count, which may change from
/// round to round. A barrier crosses to workers through Worker.spawn as the
/// shared types do.
///
/// Rounds count up from 0 with no gaps, over every use of the barrier. The
/// participants of a round pass the same count, each a different index from
/// 0 to that count less one, and all call the same method with shares of
/// the same length. A worker that sits rounds out calls the next round it
/// takes part in, which waits until the rounds before it are over, so it
/// never counts toward one of them.
/// ```as
/// // In each of the four parts, its sums over its slice of the data:
/// let met = await barrier.sum(step, 4, index, sums, sums);
/// if (!met) {
///     return;
/// }
/// // sums now holds the totals over every part.
/// ```
@sendable
export class Barrier {
    /// A barrier for rounds of up to maxParticipants participants, each
    /// bringing a share of up to shareFloats values. Throws when
    /// maxParticipants is 0, or when its shares and one result take more
    /// than a shared object holds.
    static create(maxParticipants: u32, shareFloats: u32 = 0): Barrier;

    /// Settles true once every participant of round has arrived, and false
    /// once the barrier is broken or gone, or inside a worker being stopped.
    /// Throws when participants is 0 or above the barrier's maximum, or when
    /// round is already over.
    arrive(round: u32, participants: u32): Promise<bool>;

    /// As arrive, bringing index's share. Once it settles true, out holds the
    /// shares added in index order, the same bits for every participant.
    /// share holds up to the barrier's shareFloats values, out as many as
    /// share, and out may be share. Throws as arrive does, and when index is
    /// not below participants or share or out breaks those rules.
    sum(round: u32, participants: u32, index: u32, share: Float32Array, out: Float32Array): Promise<bool>;

    /// As sum, out holding the smallest value at each position, taking -0
    /// as below +0, or NaN where any share holds NaN.
    min(round: u32, participants: u32, index: u32, share: Float32Array, out: Float32Array): Promise<bool>;

    /// As sum, out holding the largest value at each position, taking +0 as
    /// above -0, or NaN where any share holds NaN.
    max(round: u32, participants: u32, index: u32, share: Float32Array, out: Float32Array): Promise<bool>;

    /// Settles every wait on the barrier false, and every call from then
    /// on, so the others stop waiting for a participant that failed, was
    /// stopped or had its call cancelled. None of those breaks the barrier by
    /// itself.
    break(): void;

    /// Releases the barrier's region and signals as Shared.release does; its
    /// calls then settle false.
    release(): void;
}

/// Values of type T in arrival order, bounded by a byte capacity that each
/// value's encoded bytes plus four count against, and four more per shared
/// object it names plus four when it names any; writers and readers never
/// wait, so the audio thread may use one. Values cross as deep copies, and a
/// job or worker taking the ring as a `Ring<T>` parameter reads the same T.
/// ```as
/// let ring = Ring.create<Point>(4096);
/// ring.send(point);
/// let got = ring.receive();
/// ```
@sendable
@sends
export class Ring<T> extends Shared {
    /// An empty ring whose queued records take at most capacityBytes.
    static create<V>(capacityBytes: u32 = 4096): Ring<V>;

    /// Bytes the queued records take.
    get used(): u32;

    /// Notified on every write.
    get dataSignal(): Signal;

    /// Notified on every read.
    get spaceSignal(): Signal;

    /// False when the value does not fit right now. One whose record, the
    /// value with its length and the ids of the shared objects it names, is
    /// larger than the whole ring never fits, and the first such send warns
    /// on the console, except on an audio processor, which never warns.
    send(value: T): bool;

    /// The oldest value, or null when the ring is empty. It allocates the value
    /// and its box, so audio code reads with receiveInto instead.
    receive(): Box<T>?;

    /// Decodes the oldest value into out without allocating; false, leaving
    /// out alone, when the ring is empty. T is a class of numbers, a
    /// StaticArray of numbers or a typed array, its arrays as long as the
    /// ones sent.
    @decodesInPlace
    receiveInto(out: T): bool;

    /// Writes count samples as one raw record; the audio path, read back with
    /// readF32 whatever T is.
    writeF32(samples: StaticArray<f32>, count: i32): bool;

    /// Reads one record of samples into out; answers the samples read, 0 when
    /// empty, and -1 when the record was larger than out, which is dropped so
    /// the ring keeps moving.
    readF32(out: StaticArray<f32>): i32;
}

/// The latest published value of type T; readers always see a whole value.
/// Values fit a capacity set at creation, 1024 bytes unless given, so a
/// publish never allocates and the audio thread may publish.
/// ```as
/// let meter = Snapshot.create<Meter>();
/// meter.publish(levels);
/// let latest = meter.latest();
/// ```
@sendable
@sends
export class Snapshot<T> extends Shared {
    /// A snapshot for values whose encoded bytes fit capacityBytes, counting
    /// the shared objects they name as a ring does.
    static create<V>(capacityBytes: u32 = 1024): Snapshot<V>;

    /// Bumped by every publish.
    get seq(): f64;

    /// False, publishing nothing, when the encoded value is larger than the
    /// capacity; readers then keep the last value that fit. The first such
    /// publish warns on the console, except on an audio processor.
    publish(value: T): bool;

    /// The latest value, or null before the first publish. It allocates the
    /// value and its box, so audio code reads with latestInto instead.
    latest(): Box<T>?;

    /// Decodes the latest value into out without allocating; false, leaving
    /// out alone, before the first publish. T is a class of numbers, a
    /// StaticArray of numbers or a typed array, its arrays as long as the
    /// ones published.
    @decodesInPlace
    latestInto(out: T): bool;
}

```as
/// An expectation on a value, from `that` on an `Expect`. Each method asserts
/// how the value compares to the expected one and records a failure on the test
/// when it does not hold.
export class Expectation<T> {
    /// An expectation that negates the assertion that follows.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(5).never.is(3);
    /// expect.that(5).never.greaterThan(10);
    /// ```
    get never(): Expectation<T>;

    /// Asserts that the value equals the expected value. Class instances
    /// compare by reference unless their class overloads `==`.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(5).is(5);
    /// expect.that("hello").is("hello");
    /// ```
    is(expected: T): void;

    /// Asserts that the value is less than the expected value.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(3).lessThan(10);
    /// ```
    lessThan(expected: T): void;

    /// Asserts that the value is less than or equal to the expected value.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(5).lessThanOrEqual(5);
    /// expect.that(4).lessThanOrEqual(5);
    /// ```
    lessThanOrEqual(expected: T): void;

    /// Asserts that the value is greater than the expected value.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(10).greaterThan(5);
    /// ```
    greaterThan(expected: T): void;

    /// Asserts that the value is greater than or equal to the expected value.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(5).greaterThanOrEqual(5);
    /// expect.that(6).greaterThanOrEqual(5);
    /// ```
    greaterThanOrEqual(expected: T): void;
}

/// Creates expectations for one test case. Each test body receives its own
/// `Expect`, and a helper that asserts takes it as a parameter.
export class Expect {
    /// Starts an `Expectation` on `value`. A failure reports `line`, which
    /// defaults to the line of the call.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(2 + 3).is(5);
    /// ```
    that<T>(value: T, line: i32 = callerLine()): Expectation<T>;
}

/// A test suite. Extend it, export the class, and declare test cases and groups
/// in `run`. The editor's test pane and `rive <dir> --test` run every exported
/// suite.
///
/// Test code exists only at edit time and never ships in the exported file.
/// Subclasses of `Tests` are edit time already; mark any other declaration
/// that names `Expect` or `Expectation`, such as a helper, `@editTime`.
/// ```as
/// import { Expect, Tests } from "rive/test";
///
/// function clamp(value: f64, low: f64, high: f64): f64 {
///   return Math.min(Math.max(value, low), high);
/// }
///
/// @editTime
/// function expectClamped(expect: Expect, value: f64, want: f64): void {
///   expect.that(clamp(value, 0, 5)).is(want);
/// }
///
/// export class MathTests extends Tests {
///   override run(): void {
///     group("clamp", () => {
///       test("clamps high values", (expect) => {
///         expectClamped(expect, 10, 5);
///       });
///       test("passes values in range through", (expect) => {
///         expect.that(clamp(3, 0, 5)).is(3);
///       });
///     });
///   }
/// }
/// ```
export abstract class Tests extends Protocol {
    /// Declares the suite's test cases and groups by calling `test` and
    /// `group`. Inside `run` and its lambdas they need no `this.`.
    abstract run(): void;

    /// Looks up a blob asset by name, or null when it is missing or empty.
    /// The test runner supplies the project's blobs.
    /// ```as
    /// test("reads fixtures", (expect) => {
    ///     let data = this.blob("fixtures");
    ///     expect.that(data != null).is(true);
    /// });
    /// ```
    blob(name: string): ArrayBuffer?;

    /// Groups related test cases under a common name. Groups can nest.
    /// ```as
    /// group("math", () => {
    ///   test("adds numbers", (expect) => {
    ///     expect.that(2 + 2).is(4);
    ///   });
    ///   test("multiplies numbers", (expect) => {
    ///     expect.that(3 * 4).is(12);
    ///   });
    /// });
    /// ```
    group(name: string, body: () => void): void;

    /// Declares a named test case. `body` receives the case's `Expect`, used to
    /// create expectations on values.
    /// ```as
    /// test("adds two numbers", (expect) => {
    ///   let result = 2 + 3;
    ///   expect.that(result).is(5);
    /// });
    /// ```
    test(name: string, body: (expect: Expect) => void): void;

    /// Declares a test case that passes only when `body` throws. With a
    /// `message`, the error must also contain it. A case that runs past its
    /// time budget fails.
    /// ```as
    /// errors("rejects a negative size", (expect) => {
    ///   Buffer.create(-1);
    /// }, "invalid argument #1 to 'create' (size)");
    /// ```
    errors(
        name: string,
        body: (expect: Expect) => void,
        message: string = ""
    ): void;
}
```

/// A variable axis of a `Font`, such as weight or width.
export class FontAxis {
    /// Four letter axis tag, for example "wght".
    tag: string = "";

    /// Smallest value the axis accepts.

/// so multiply by the size and expect `ascent` below zero.
/// ```as
/// export class Label extends Node {
///     text: Text = new Text();
///
///     override init(context: Context): bool {
///         let font = context.font("Inter");
///         if (font != null) {
///             let style = new TextRunStyle(font);
///             style.size = 24;
///             style.paint = new Paint();
///             this.text.append("Hello", style);
///         }
///         return true;
///     }
/// }
/// ```

    /// font.

    /// Distance from the baseline to the top of lowercase letters, negative.

    /// are not a font.

    /// let downloadedBytes = new ArrayBuffer(0);
    /// let font = Font.decode(downloadedBytes);

    get weight(): u32;

    /// Whether the font is italic.
    get isItalic(): bool;

    /// Height of one line of text at the given size.
    lineHeight(size: f32): f32;

    /// Whether the font has a glyph for the unicode codepoint.
    hasGlyph(codepoint: u32): bool;

    /// Current value of a variable axis, by tag.
    axisValue(tag: string): f32;

    /// Variable axes the font offers.
    axes(): Array<FontAxis>;

    /// The UTF-16 code unit index nearest a point in the text's local space.

    /// The caret before the code unit at `index`, as three values: its x, top
    /// and bottom. Returns `null` when the text has no layout.
    /// ```as
    /// let caret = text.caret(0);
    /// if (caret != null) {
    ///     let x = caret[0];
    ///     let height = caret[2] - caret[1];
    /// }
    /// ```
    caret(index: i32): StaticArray<f32>?;

    /// Rectangles covering the code units from one index to another, one per
    /// glyph, as consecutive minimum and maximum corners.
    /// ```as
    /// let corners = text.selectionRects(0, 5);
    /// for (let i = 0; i + 1 < corners.length; i += 2) {
    ///     let min = corners[i];
    ///     let max = corners[i + 1];
    /// }
    /// ```
    selectionRects(from: i32, to: i32): Array<Vector>;

    /// Releases the text and its layout.
    release(): void;
}
```

```as
/// A vector with three components. Vectors built from x and y alone have
/// z = 0. All magnitude and interpolation operations (`length`, `dot`,
/// `distance`, `normalized`, `lerp`, ...) use all three components; with
/// z = 0 they behave exactly as 2D math. `Vector` is a value type: assigning
/// or passing one copies it.
/// ```as
/// let a = Vector.xy(3, 4);
/// let b = Vector(1, 2);
/// let c = a + b * 2; // 5 8
/// let len = a.length(); // 5
/// ```
export struct Vector {
    /// The x component of the vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xy(10, -5);
    /// let xValue = v.x; // 10
    /// ```
    x: f32 = 0;

    /// The y component of the vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xy(10, -5);
    /// let yValue = v.y; // -5
    /// ```
    y: f32 = 0;

    /// The z component of the vector. Zero for vectors built from x and y
    /// alone; populated by 3D APIs that return a `Vector`.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xyz(1, 2, 3);
    /// let zValue = v.z; // 3
    /// ```
    z: f32 = 0;

    /// Creates the zero vector.
    constructor();

    /// Creates a vector with the given x and y components and z = 0.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector(5, -2); // 5 -2
    /// ```
    constructor(x: f32, y: f32);

    /// Creates a vector with the given x, y and z components.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector(1, 2, 3);
    /// ```
    constructor(x: f32, y: f32, z: f32);

    /// Returns the sum of two vectors.
    /// ```as
    /// let a = Vector.xy(2, 3);
    /// let b = Vector.xy(-1, 5);
    /// let c = a + b; // 1 8
    /// ```
    operator+(a: Vector, b: Vector): Vector;

    /// Returns the difference between two vectors.
    /// ```as
    /// let a = Vector.xy(2, 3);
    /// let b = Vector.xy(-1, 5);
    /// let c = a - b; // 3 -2
    /// ```
    operator-(a: Vector, b: Vector): Vector;

    /// Returns the negated vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xy(2, -3);
    /// let neg = -v; // -2 3
    /// ```
    operator-(v: Vector): Vector;

    /// Returns the vector scaled by the given number. The number goes on the
    /// right; `2 * v` does not compile.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xy(3, -2);
    /// let doubled = v * 2; // 6 -4
    /// ```
    operator*(v: Vector, s: f32): Vector;

    /// Returns the vector divided by the given number.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xy(6, -4);
    /// let half = v / 2; // 3 -2
    /// ```
    operator/(v: Vector, s: f32): Vector;

    /// Returns true if the two vectors have equal components.
    /// ```as
    /// let a = Vector.xy(1, 2);
    /// let b = Vector.xy(1, 2);
    /// let c = Vector.xy(2, 1);
    /// let same = a == b; // true
    /// let different = a == c; // false
    /// ```
    operator==(a: Vector, b: Vector): bool;

    /// A hash of the components. Together with `==` it lets vectors key a
    /// `Map` or `Set`.
    readonly hash(): u32;

    /// Returns the squared length of the vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xy(3, 4);
    /// let len2 = v.lengthSquared(); // 25
    /// ```
    readonly lengthSquared(): f32;

    /// Returns the length of the vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xy(3, 4);
    /// let len = v.length(); // 5
    /// ```
    readonly length(): f32;

    /// Returns a normalized copy of the vector. If the length is zero, the
    /// result is the zero vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xy(10, 0);
    /// let n = v.normalized(); // 1 0
    /// ```
    readonly normalized(): Vector;

    /// Returns the dot product of the vector and the other vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let a = Vector.xy(1, 2);
    /// let b = Vector.xy(3, 4);
    /// let dp = a.dot(b); // 11 (1*3 + 2*4)
    /// ```
    readonly dot(other: Vector): f32;

    /// Returns the squared distance to the other vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let a = Vector.xy(0, 0);
    /// let b = Vector.xy(3, 4);
    /// let d2 = a.distanceSquared(b); // 25
    /// ```
    readonly distanceSquared(other: Vector): f32;

    /// Returns the distance to the other vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let a = Vector.xy(0, 0);
    /// let b = Vector.xy(3, 4);
    /// let d = a.distance(b); // 5
    /// ```
    readonly distance(other: Vector): f32;

    /// Returns the linear interpolation between the vector and the other
    /// vector, using t where 0 returns the vector and 1 returns the other.
    /// ```as
    /// let a = Vector.xy(0, 0);
    /// let b = Vector.xy(10, 0);
    /// let p = a.lerp(b, 0.5); // 5 0
    /// ```
    readonly lerp(other: Vector, t: f32): Vector;

    /// Returns the component at `index`: 0 is x, 1 is y and 2 is z. Throws
    /// for any other index.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xyz(3, 4, 5);
    /// let sum: f32 = 0;
    /// for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    ///     sum += v.at(i); // 12 after the loop
    /// }
    /// ```
    readonly at(index: i32): f32;

    /// Writes x, y and z as 12 bytes, three 32 bit floats, into `buffer` at
    /// `byteOffset`. Throws when the 12 bytes do not fit.
    /// ```as
    /// let bytes = new ArrayBuffer(12);
    /// Vector.xyz(1, 2, 3).writeToBuffer(bytes, 0);
    /// ```
    readonly writeToBuffer(buffer: ArrayBuffer, byteOffset: u32): void;

    /// Writes x, y, z and `w` as 16 bytes, four 32 bit floats, into `buffer`
    /// at `byteOffset`, matching a `vec4` slot of a uniform buffer. Throws
    /// when the 16 bytes do not fit.
    /// ```as
    /// let ubo = new ArrayBuffer(16);
    /// let lightDir = Vector.xyz(0, -1, 0);
    /// lightDir.writeVec4(ubo, 0, 0); // w = 0 for a direction
    /// ```
    readonly writeVec4(buffer: ArrayBuffer, byteOffset: u32, w: f32): void;
}

/// Static helpers that build and combine vectors, called as `Vector.xy`,
/// `Vector.cross` and so on.
export namespace Vector {
    /// Creates a vector with the specified x and y components.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xy(5, -2); // 5 -2
    /// ```
    export function xy(x: f32, y: f32): Vector;

    /// Creates a vector with the specified x, y and z components.
    /// ```as
    /// let v = Vector.xyz(1, 2, 3);
    /// ```
    export function xyz(x: f32, y: f32, z: f32): Vector;

    /// Returns the zero vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let origin = Vector.origin(); // 0 0
    /// ```
    export function origin(): Vector;

    /// Returns the distance between the two vectors.
    /// ```as
    /// let d = Vector.distance(Vector.xy(3, 4), Vector.xy(0, 0)); // 5
    /// ```
    export function distance(a: Vector, b: Vector): f32;

    /// Returns the squared distance between the two vectors.
    /// ```as
    /// let d2 = Vector.distanceSquared(Vector.xy(3, 4), Vector.xy(0, 0)); // 25
    /// ```
    export function distanceSquared(a: Vector, b: Vector): f32;

    /// Returns the dot product of the two vectors.
    /// ```as
    /// let dp = Vector.dot(Vector.xy(1, 2), Vector.xy(3, 4)); // 11 (1*3 + 2*4)
    /// ```
    export function dot(a: Vector, b: Vector): f32;

    /// Returns the 2D cross product of two vectors, the z component of their
    /// 3D cross product.
    /// ```as
    /// let c = Vector.cross(Vector.xy(1, 0), Vector.xy(0, 1)); // 1
    /// ```
    export function cross(a: Vector, b: Vector): f32;

    /// Returns the 3D cross product of two vectors.
    /// ```as
    /// let z = Vector.cross3(Vector.xyz(1, 0, 0), Vector.xyz(0, 1, 0)); // 0 0 1
    /// ```
    export function cross3(a: Vector, b: Vector): Vector;

    /// Returns a + b * scale.
    /// ```as
    /// let r = Vector.scaleAndAdd(Vector.xy(1, 2), Vector.xy(3, 4), 2); // 7 10
    /// ```
    export function scaleAndAdd(a: Vector, b: Vector, scale: f32): Vector;

    /// Returns a - b * scale.
    /// ```as
    /// let r = Vector.scaleAndSub(Vector.xy(7, 10), Vector.xy(3, 4), 2); // 1 2
    /// ```
    export function scaleAndSub(a: Vector, b: Vector, scale: f32): Vector;

    /// Returns the linear interpolation from one vector to another, using t
    /// where 0 returns `from` and 1 returns `to`.
    /// ```as
    /// let p = Vector.lerp(Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(8, 0), 0.25); // 2 0
    /// ```
    export function lerp(from: Vector, to: Vector, t: f32): Vector;

    /// Returns the length of the given vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let len = Vector.length(Vector.xy(3, 4)); // 5
    /// ```
    export function length(v: Vector): f32;

    /// Returns the squared length of the given vector.
    /// ```as
    /// let len2 = Vector.lengthSquared(Vector.xy(3, 4)); // 25
    /// ```
    export function lengthSquared(v: Vector): f32;

    /// Returns a normalized copy of the given vector, or the zero vector when
    /// its length is zero.
    /// ```as
    /// let n = Vector.normalized(Vector.xy(10, 0)); // 1 0
    /// ```
    export function normalized(v: Vector): Vector;
}

/// A pair of corners returned by `Artboard.bounds` and `Text.bounds`.
export class ArtboardBounds {
    /// The minimum corner.
    v0: Vector;

    /// The maximum corner.
    v1: Vector;
}

## TOPIC: animascript/api/workers

# Workers

<!-- GENERATED by docsgen/gen_as_api.py from
     rasc/animascript/std/rive -- do not edit -->

Import from `"rive/workers"`. Declares: `Worker`

```as
/// A spawned worker. It talks to other lanes only through shared memory:
/// rings, snapshots, signals and regions it was handed or created. What it
/// creates belongs to the script that spawned it, and the worker holds it
/// until it releases it, or until the worker is over and its handle goes.
/// What its promise resolves with crosses back as a deep copy once it
/// returns. A worker has no time limit: it runs until it returns or is
/// stopped. A browser build without threads steps workers on the page's
/// thread, where one with fuel fails once a step passes the call budget.
/// ```as
/// let ring = Ring.create<f32>(4096);
/// let worker = Worker.spawn(synth, ring);
/// ```
export class Worker<R = void> extends ResultLane<R> {
    /// Spawns an exported async @worker function in its own instance, the
    /// arguments after it deep copied as its parameters. The compiler writes
    /// each call, so the worker is named directly and Worker.spawn is never
    /// taken as a value.
    /// ```as
    /// @worker export async function synth(ring: Ring<f32>): Promise<void> {
    ///     let seen = 0.0;
    ///     while (seen != kWaitStopping) {
    ///         seen = await ring.dataSignal.next(seen);
    ///     }
    /// }
    ///
    /// let worker = Worker.spawn(synth, ring);
    /// ```
    @builtin static spawn<R>(worker: (...args: unknown[]) => Promise<R>, ...args: unknown[]): Worker<R>;

    /// Settles with 0 after the given seconds, or early with kWaitStopping
    /// inside a worker being stopped. On the main lane it settles on the
    /// first advance after the time passes.
    static sleep(seconds: f64): Promise<f64>;
}
```

    rightStickButton: boolean

    dpadUp: boolean
    dpadDown: boolean
    dpadLeft: boolean
    dpadRight: boolean
    start: boolean

    --- Left and right analog stick deflection (axes 0–3 when standard).
    leftStick: Vector
    rightStick: Vector

    --- Analog shoulder triggers (axes 4–5 when standard).
    leftTrigger: number
    rightTrigger: number

    --- Digital trigger buttons (indices 6–7 when standard).
    leftTriggerPressed: boolean
    rightTriggerPressed: boolean

end


--- One field change on an already-connected gamepad (`gamepadEvent`); includes
--- the full post-update state and optional standard-layout intent.
declare extern type GamepadEvent with

    --- W3C change kind: `"button"` or `"axis"`.
    changeKind: string
    --- 1-based W3C button or axis index for this change.
    changeIndex: number
    changeValue: number
    hasStandardButtonIntent: boolean
    hasStandardAxisIntent: boolean
    intentButton: string?
    intentAxis: string?

    --- Read-only full device state after the change (same fields as [GamepadConnected]).
    deviceId: number
    buttonMask: number
    buttons: { number }
    axes: { number }
    isStandardMapping: boolean
    mapping: GamepadMappingKind
    gamepadMapping: number

    buttonPressed: (self: GamepadEvent, index: number) -> boolean
    buttonValue: (self: GamepadEvent, index: number) -> number
    axis: (self: GamepadEvent, index: number) -> number
    west: boolean
    south: boolean
    north: boolean
    east: boolean
    leftShoulder: boolean
    rightShoulder: boolean
    back: boolean
    forward: boolean
    leftStickButton: boolean
    rightStickButton: boolean
    dpadUp: boolean
    dpadDown: boolean
    dpadLeft: boolean
    dpadRight: boolean
    start: boolean
    leftStick: Vector
    rightStick: Vector
    leftTrigger: number
    rightTrigger: number
    leftTriggerPressed: boolean
    rightTriggerPressed: boolean

end


--- Device id when a gamepad is removed (`gamepadDisconnected`).
declare extern type GamepadDisconnected with

    deviceId: number

end


--- Provides access to the context that triggered a listener action.
---
--- A `ListenerContext` can represent different event types (pointer, keyboard,
--- text input, focus, view model changes, or reported events). Use the
--- `is...` methods to check the type, and the corresponding `as...` methods
--- to retrieve the event data.
declare extern type ListenerContext with

    --- Returns true if the action was triggered by a pointer event.
    isPointerEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean

    --- Returns true if the action was triggered by a keyboard event.
    isKeyboardEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean

    --- Returns true if the action was triggered by a text input event.
    isTextInput: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean

    --- Returns true if the action was triggered by a focus change.
    isFocus: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean

    --- Returns true if the action was triggered by a reported Rive event.
    isReportedEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean

    --- Returns true if the action was triggered by a view model change.
    isViewModelChange: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean

    isGamepadConnected: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean
    isGamepadEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean
    isGamepadDisconnected: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean

    --- Returns true if the action was triggered by an unknown or unsupported event type.
    isNone: (self: ListenerContext) -> boolean

    --- Returns the pointer event if applicable, otherwise nil.
    asPointerEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> PointerEvent?

    --- Returns the keyboard event if applicable, otherwise nil.
    asKeyboardEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> KeyboardEvent?

    --- Returns the text input event if applicable, otherwise nil.
    asTextInput: (self: ListenerContext) -> TextInput?

    --- Returns the focus event if applicable, otherwise nil.
    asFocus: (self: ListenerContext) -> FocusEvent?

    --- Returns the reported event if applicable, otherwise nil.
    asReportedEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> ReportedEvent?

    --- Returns the view model change if applicable, otherwise nil.
    asViewModelChange: (self: ListenerContext) -> ViewModelChange?

    asGamepadConnected: (self: ListenerContext) -> GamepadConnected?
    asGamepadEvent: (self: ListenerContext) -> GamepadEvent?
    asGamepadDisconnected: (self: ListenerContext) -> GamepadDisconnected?

    --- Returns a none event if applicable, otherwise nil.
    asNone: (self: ListenerContext) -> NoneEvent?

end

--- Represents a node in the hierarchy, providing transform properties and
--- access to parent and child nodes.
declare extern type NodeReadData with

    --- The local position of the node.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     node.position = Vector.xy(199, 299)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    position: Vector

    --- The local rotation of the node in radians.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     node.rotation = math.rad(45)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    rotation: number

    --- The local scale of the node.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     node.scale = Vector.xy(1.4, 2)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    scale: Vector

    --- The read-only world transform of the node.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     local wt = node.worldTransform
    ---     print("world xx:", wt.xx, "xy:", wt.xy)
    ---     print("world yx:", wt.yx, "yy:", wt.yy)
    ---     print("world tx:", wt.tx, "ty:", wt.ty)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    worldTransform: Mat2D

    --- The x-coordinate of the local position.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     node.x = 100
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    x: number

    --- The y-coordinate of the local position.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     node.y = 200
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    y: number

    --- The x component of the local scale.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     node.scaleX = 2
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    scaleX: number

    --- The y component of the local scale.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     node.scaleY = 2
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    scaleY: number

    --- The stroke or fill a path effect applies to, on the node its `update`
    --- receives, otherwise nil. The same as `asPaint`.
    --- ```lua
    --- function update(self: MyEffect, path: PathData, node: NodeReadData): PathData
    ---   local paint = node.paint
    ---   if paint then
    ---     print(paint.color)
    ---   end
    ---   return path
    --- end
    --- ```
    paint: Paint?

    --- If node is a Path, returns the node as `PathData`.
    --- ```lua
    --- function pointerDown(self: PaintInstance, event: PointerEvent)
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     local myPath = self.instance:node('MyPath')
    ---     if myPath then
    ---       local path = myPath:asPath()
    ---       if path then
    ---         local cmd: PathCommand = path[1]
    ---         print(cmd.type) -- moveTo
    ---       end
    ---     end
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function asPath(self):  PathData?

    --- Returns the stroke or fill a path effect applies to, on the node its
    --- `update` receives, otherwise nil.
    --- ```lua
    --- function update(self: MyEffect, path: PathData, node: NodeReadData): PathData
    ---   local paint = node:asPaint()
    ---   if paint then
    ---     print(paint.thickness)
    ---   end
    ---   return path
    --- end
    --- ```
    function asPaint(self):  Paint?
end

--- Represents a node in the hierarchy, providing transform properties and
--- access to parent and child nodes.
declare extern type NodeData extends NodeReadData with

    --- Updates the node’s position, rotation, and scale from the given world
    --- transform.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Root')
    ---   if node then
    ---     local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 100)
    ---     node:decompose(m)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function decompose(self, worldTransform:Mat2D): ()

    --- The node’s children.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     local hipsFirstChild = node.children[1]
    ---     print(hipsFirstChild)
    ---     local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 100)
    ---
    ---     if hipsFirstChild then
    ---       hipsFirstChild:decompose(m)
    ---     end
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    children: { NodeData }

    --- The parent of the node, or nil if it has none.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Hips')
    ---   if node then
    ---     local hipsParent = node.parent
    ---     local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 100)
    ---     if hipsParent then
    ---       hipsParent:decompose(m)
    ---     end
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    parent: NodeData?
end

export type Animation = {

    --- Advances the animation by the given time in seconds. Returns true if the
    --- animation hasn't reached its end. If the animation is set to loop or ping
    --- pong, it will always return true. The example works only when the component
    --- artboard has no default state machine; otherwise let the machine play.
    --- ```lua
    --- type AnimationExample = {
    ---   -- Artboard input, assigned in the Rive editor by the designer
    ---   character: Input<Artboard<nil>>,
    ---
    ---   -- The live instance and its animation
    ---   artboardInstance: Artboard<nil>?,
    ---   anim: Animation?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: AnimationExample, context: Context): boolean
    ---   self.artboardInstance = self.character:instance()
    ---
    ---   if self.artboardInstance then
    ---     self.anim = self.artboardInstance:animation('Idle')
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   if self.anim and self.artboardInstance then
    ---     -- Advance the animation to apply keyframe values to the artboard
    ---     self.anim:advance(seconds * 2)
    ---     -- Advance the artboard with 0 to propagate changes without double-counting time
    ---     self.artboardInstance:advance(0)
    ---   end
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function draw(self: AnimationExample, renderer: Renderer)
    ---   if self.artboardInstance then
    ---     renderer:save()
    ---     self.artboardInstance:draw(renderer)
    ---     renderer:restore()
    ---   end
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<AnimationExample>
    ---   return {
    ---     character = late(),
    ---     artboardInstance = nil,
    ---     anim = nil,
    ---     init = init,
    ---     advance = advance,
    ---     draw = draw,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    advance: (self: Animation, seconds: number) -> boolean,

    --- set the animation time in seconds
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   if self.anim and self.artboardInstance then
    ---     -- Set the animation to a specific time in seconds
    ---     self.anim:setTime(0.3)
    ---     -- Advance the artboard with 0 to propagate changes without double-counting time
    ---     self.artboardInstance:advance(0)
    ---   end
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    setTime: (self: Animation, time: number) -> (),

    --- set the animation time in frames
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   if self.anim and self.artboardInstance then
    ---     -- Set the animation to a specific frame
    ---     self.anim:setTimeFrames(3)
    ---     -- Advance the artboard with 0 to propagate changes without double-counting time
    ---     self.artboardInstance:advance(0)
    ---   end
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    setTimeFrames: (self: Animation, frames: number) -> (),

    --- set the animation time as a percentage of the duration
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   if self.anim and self.artboardInstance then
    ---     -- Set the animation to a specific percentage of the duration.
    ---     self.anim:setTimePercentage(.5)
    ---     -- Advance the artboard with 0 to propagate changes without double-counting time
    ---     self.artboardInstance:advance(0)
    ---   end
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    setTimePercentage: (self: Animation, percentage: number) -> (),

    --- The duration of the animation.
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AnimationExample, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   if self.anim
    ---     print(self.anim.duration)
    ---   end
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    duration: number,
}

--- The kind of a custom property on a Drawable.
export type DrawablePropertyKind = "number" | "boolean" | "string" | "color" | "enum" | "trigger"

--- One custom property as `drawable:properties()` lists them.
export type DrawableProperty = { name: string, kind: DrawablePropertyKind }

--- What a custom property is read by. Get one from `artboard:propertyKey`
--- once, in `init`, and keep it: resolving a name scans the file's name
--- table, reading by key does not.
export type PropertyKey = number

--- A drawable that carries custom properties, handed to the visitor of
--- `artboard:draw(renderer, visitor)`. It is only valid inside that visitor
--- call.
export type Drawable = {
    --- The custom number property of this key, nil when there is none.
    number: (self: Drawable, key: PropertyKey) -> number?,
    --- The custom boolean property of this key, nil when there is none.
    boolean: (self: Drawable, key: PropertyKey) -> boolean?,
    --- The custom color property of this key, nil when there is none.
    color: (self: Drawable, key: PropertyKey) -> Color?,
    --- The custom string property of this key, nil when there is none.
    string: (self: Drawable, key: PropertyKey) -> string?,
    --- Every custom property on the drawable. For tooling and debugging:
    --- the editor and rive-cli have it, a shipping runtime does not, so do
    --- not call it from a script you ship.
    properties: (self: Drawable) -> { DrawableProperty },
    --- Draws the drawable under the renderer's current state.
    draw: (self: Drawable, renderer: Renderer) -> (),
}

--- Represents a Rive artboard instance, providing drawing, advancing,
--- interaction handling, and access to named nodes and data.
export type Artboard<T = nil> = {

    --- If true, the artboard’s origin is treated as the frame origin.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: RenderInstance, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vm = Data.Character.new()
    ---
    ---   self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     self.instance.frameOrigin = true
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    frameOrigin: boolean,

    --- Draws the artboard using the provided renderer.
    --- ```lua
    --- type RenderInstances = {
    ---   character: Input<Artboard<Data.Character>>,
    ---
    ---   instance: Artboard<Data.Character>?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: RenderInstances, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vm = Data.Character.new()
    ---
    ---   self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function draw(self: RenderInstances, renderer: Renderer)
    ---   local instance = self.instance
    ---
    ---   if instance then
    ---     renderer:save()
    ---     instance:draw(renderer)
    ---     renderer:restore()
    ---   end
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<RenderInstances>
    ---   return {
    ---     character = late(),
    ---     instance = nil,
    ---     init = init,
    ---     draw = draw,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    ---
    --- With a `visitor`, each drawable that has custom properties is handed
    --- to it instead of being drawn: the visitor decides whether to call
    --- `drawable:draw(renderer)` and under what renderer state. Whatever it
    --- sets on the renderer ends with that visit. Every other drawable draws
    --- as usual, and clipping still applies. `context` is passed through to
    --- the visitor untouched.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- In init: local GLOW = artboard:propertyKey("glow")
    --- -- Draw only the drawables tagged `glow`, in their own paint.
    --- artboard:draw(renderer, function(context, drawable, renderer)
    ---   if drawable:boolean(GLOW) then
    ---     drawable:draw(renderer)
    ---   end
    --- end)
    --- ```
    ---
    --- Drawing a tagged nested artboard visits the tagged drawables inside
    --- it from within that `drawable:draw` call, so a value carries down in
    --- a local:
    --- ```lua
    --- local level = 1
    --- artboard:draw(renderer, function(context, drawable, renderer)
    ---   local outer = level
    ---   level = outer * math.min(drawable:number(EMISSIVE) or 0, 1)
    ---   local c = math.floor(level * 255)
    ---   renderer:setColorModulation(Color.rgba(c, c, c, 255))
    ---   drawable:draw(renderer)
    ---   level = outer
    --- end)
    --- ```
    draw: (self: Artboard<T>, renderer: Renderer, visitor: ((context: any, drawable: Drawable, renderer: Renderer) -> ())?, context: any?) -> (),

    --- Draws the artboard with the color modulation set, per drawable, from
    --- its custom property of this key: a number as a gray level clamped to
    --- 0..1, a color as is. Drawables without it draw under the renderer's
    --- current state. Levels multiply down through tagged drawables that
    --- hold others: inside a nested artboard tagged 0.5, a shape tagged 0.2
    --- draws at 0.1 and an untagged one at 0.5. Nothing calls back into the
    --- script, so this is the cheapest way to draw a pass like emission.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- In init: local EMISSIVE = artboard:propertyKey("emissive")
    --- -- Everything black except drawables tagged `emissive`.
    --- renderer:save()
    --- renderer:setColorModulation(Color.rgba(0, 0, 0, 255))
    --- artboard:drawModulated(renderer, EMISSIVE)
    --- renderer:restore()
    --- ```
    drawModulated: (self: Artboard<T>, renderer: Renderer, key: PropertyKey) -> (),

    --- The key custom properties called `name` are read by. When no
    --- property in the file carries that name the key matches nothing, so
    --- every read by it comes back nil. Custom properties are added to a
    --- drawable in the editor's inspector.
    propertyKey: (self: Artboard<T>, name: string) -> PropertyKey,


    --- Advances the artboard by the given time in seconds. Returns true if the
    --- artboard should continue receiving advance calls.
    --- ```lua
    --- type RenderInstances = {
    ---   character: Input<Artboard<Data.Character>>,
    ---
    ---   instance: Artboard<Data.Character>?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: RenderInstances, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vm = Data.Character.new()
    ---
    ---   self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function advance(self: RenderInstances, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     return self.instance:advance(seconds)
    ---   end
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<RenderInstances>
    ---   return {
    ---     character = late(),
    ---     instance = nil,
    ---     init = init,
    ---     advance = advance,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    advance: (self: Artboard<T>, seconds: number) -> boolean,

    --- The typed data associated with the artboard.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: RenderInstance, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vm = Data.Character.new()
    ---
    ---   self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
    ---
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     self.instance.frameOrigin = true
    ---
    ---     local data = self.instance.data
    ---     if data then
    ---       print(data.nickname)
    ---     end
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    read data: T,

    --- Creates a new instance of the artboard with independent state.
    --- ```lua
    --- type ViewModelExample = {
    ---   character: Input<Artboard<Data.Character>>,
    ---   instance: Artboard<Data.Character>?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: ViewModelExample, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vm = Data.Character.new()
    ---   self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<ViewModelExample>
    ---   return {
    ---     character = late(),
    ---     instance = nil,
    ---     init = init,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    instance: (self: Artboard<T>, viewModel: ViewModel?) -> Artboard<T>,

    --- Creates an animation instance linked to the artboard instance
    animation: (self: Artboard<T>, name: string) -> Animation?,

    --- The width of the artboard.
    --- ```lua
    --- self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     print(self.instance.width)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    width: number,

    --- The height of the artboard.
    --- ```lua
    --- self.instance = self.character:instance(vm)
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     print(self.instance.height)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    height: number,

    --- Returns the bounding box of the artboard as two `Vector` values: the
    --- minimum point and the maximum point.
    --- ```lua
    --- local minPt, maxPt = self.instance:bounds()
    --- print("Bounds width", maxPt.x - minPt.x)
    --- print("Bounds height", maxPt.y - minPt.y)
    --- ```
    bounds: (self:Artboard<T>) -> (Vector, Vector),

    --- Returns the node with the given name, or nil if no such node exists.
    --- The node's name must be exported
    --- (in the Hierarchy, right-click the node and select **Export Name**).
    --- Names that aren't exported are left out of the exported file, so
    --- `node` returns nil for them.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.instance then
    ---   local node = self.instance:node('Root')
    ---   if node then
    ---     local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(100, 100)
    ---     node:decompose(m)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    node: (self:Artboard<T>, name:string) -> NodeData?,

    --- Pointer event down handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit).
    --- Only returns a non-zero value if a hit-testable object inside the nested
    --- artboard is hit.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerDown(self: PointerExample, event: PointerEvent)
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     local hit = self.instance:pointerDown(event)
    ---     if hit ~= 0 then
    ---       print(event.id)
    ---       print(event.position)
    ---     end
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerDown: (self: Artboard<T>, event: PointerEvent) -> number,

    --- Pointer event up handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit).
    --- Only returns a non-zero value if a hit-testable object inside the nested
    --- artboard is hit.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerUp(self: PointerExample, event: PointerEvent)
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     local hit = self.instance:pointerUp(event)
    ---     if hit ~= 0 then
    ---       print(event.id)
    ---       print(event.position)
    ---     end
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerUp: (self: Artboard<T>, event: PointerEvent) -> number,

    --- Pointer event move handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit).
    --- Only returns a non-zero value if a hit-testable object inside the nested
    --- artboard is hit.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerMove(self: PointerExample, event: PointerEvent)
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     local hit = self.instance:pointerMove(event)
    ---     if hit ~= 0 then
    ---       print(event.id)
    ---       print(event.position)
    ---     end
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerMove: (self: Artboard<T>, event: PointerEvent) -> number,

    --- Pointer event exit handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit).
    --- Only returns a non-zero value if a hit-testable object inside the nested
    --- artboard is hit.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerExit(self: PointerExample, event: PointerEvent)
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     local hit = self.instance:pointerExit(event)
    ---     if hit ~= 0 then
    ---       print(event.id)
    ---       print(event.position)
    ---     end
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerExit: (self: Artboard<T>, event: PointerEvent) -> number,

    --- Scroll handler. Returns a hit-test result (0 = no hit), non-zero when
    --- a `ScrollConstraint` view inside the artboard took the scroll. Claim
    --- the outer event when it does, so the gesture stays with this node.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerScroll(self: RenderInstance, event: ScrollEvent)
    ---   if self.instance then
    ---     local localPos = event.position - Vector.xy(self.x, self.y)
    ---     local localEvent = ScrollEvent.new(
    ---       event.id,
    ---       localPos,
    ---       event.delta,
    ---       event.phase,
    ---       event.precise,
    ---       event.timeStamp
    ---     )
    ---     if self.instance:pointerScroll(localEvent) ~= 0 then
    ---       event:hit()
    ---     end
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerScroll: (self: Artboard<T>, event: ScrollEvent) -> number,

    --- Adds the artboard’s geometry to the given path, optionally transformed
    --- by the provided matrix.
    ---
    --- For a complete working example, see the [Add to Path](https://rive.app/community/files/27188-51290-add-to-path-scripting-demo?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=scripting_api&utm_campaign=docs_to_marketplace_links) demo.
    --- ```lua
    --- function draw(self: AddToPathExample, renderer: Renderer)
    ---   local instance = self.instance
    ---   if not instance then
    ---     return
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   -- Draw the artboard normally first.
    ---   renderer:save()
    ---   instance:draw(renderer)
    ---   renderer:restore()
    ---
    ---   -- Reset the path each frame, then rebuild it from the artboard's geometry.
    ---   self.outlinePath:reset()
    ---
    ---   -- Add the artboard's geometry into the path with an optional transform.
    ---   -- Here we apply a slight offset via Mat2D to show the transform parameter.
    ---   local transform = Mat2D.withTranslation(8, 8)
    ---   instance:addToPath(self.outlinePath, transform)
    ---
    ---   -- Draw the extracted path with a custom stroke paint as an outline / shadow effect.
    ---   renderer:drawPath(self.outlinePath, self.outlinePaint)
    --- end
    --- ```
    addToPath: (self:Artboard<T>, path:Path, transform:Mat2D?) -> (),

    --- Forwards a gamepad connection to the artboard: its focused control
    --- first, then every scripted node that did not take it. Returns how
    --- many scripted nodes received it.
    --- ```lua
    --- function gamepadConnected(self: Forwarder, event: GamepadConnected)
    ---   self.instance:gamepadConnected(event)
    --- end
    --- ```
    gamepadConnected: (self: Artboard<T>, event: GamepadConnected) -> number,

    --- Forwards a gamepad button or axis change to the artboard, the same way
    --- as `gamepadConnected`.
    gamepadEvent: (self: Artboard<T>, event: GamepadEvent) -> number,

    --- Forwards a gamepad disconnection to the artboard, the same way as
    --- `gamepadConnected`.
    gamepadDisconnected: (self: Artboard<T>, event: GamepadDisconnected) -> number,
}

## TOPIC: luau/api/color
