```luau
export type Color = number

declare Color: {

    --- Returns the red channel of the color. If a value is
    --- provided, returns a new color with that channel updated.
    --- ```lua
    --- local myColor = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)
    --- local redChannel = Color.red(myColor)
    --- print(redChannel)
    --- -- 128
    ---
    --- local newColor = Color.red(myColor, 200)
    --- print(Color.red(newColor))
    --- -- 200
    --- ```
    red: @checked (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color,

    --- Returns the green channel of the color. If a value is
    --- provided, returns a new color with that channel updated.
    --- ```lua
    --- local myColor = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)
    --- local greenChannel = Color.green(myColor)
    --- print(greenChannel)
    --- -- 55
    ---
    --- local newColor = Color.green(myColor, 200)
    --- print(Color.green(newColor))
    --- -- 200
    --- ```
    green: @checked (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color,

    --- Returns the blue channel of the color. If a value is
    --- provided, returns a new color with that channel updated.
    --- ```lua
    --- local myColor = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)
    --- local blueChannel = Color.blue(myColor)
    --- print(blueChannel)
    --- -- 12
    ---
    --- local newColor = Color.blue(myColor, 200)
    --- print(Color.blue(newColor))
    --- -- 200
    --- ```
    blue: @checked (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color,

    --- Returns the alpha channel of the color, or returns a new color with the
    --- alpha channel set to the specified value. Only the low 8 bits of the
    --- value are kept.
    --- ```lua
    --- local myColor = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 128)
    --- local alphaChannel = Color.alpha(myColor)
    --- print(alphaChannel)
    --- -- 128
    ---
    --- local newColor = Color.alpha(myColor, 200)
    --- print(Color.alpha(newColor))
    --- -- 200
    --- ```
    alpha: @checked (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color,

    --- Returns the opacity of the color as a normalized value in the range
    --- [0.0, 1.0], or returns a new color with its alpha set from the specified
    --- opacity.
    --- ```lua
    --- local myColor = Color.rgba(255, 0, 0, 128)
    ---
    --- -- Get the opacity of a color
    --- local myOpacity = Color.opacity(myColor)
    --- print(myOpacity)
    --- -- 0.502
    ---
    --- -- Get a new color with the specified opacity
    --- local newColor = Color.opacity(myColor, 1.0)
    --- print(Color.opacity(newColor))
    --- -- 1.0
    --- ```
    opacity: @checked (color: Color, value: number?) -> number | Color,

    --- Linearly interpolates between two colors using the parameter t, where
    --- t = 0 returns 'from' and t = 1 returns 'to'.
    --- ```lua
    --- local black = Color.rgb(0, 0, 0)
    --- local white = Color.rgb(255, 255, 255)
    ---
    --- local t = 0.5
    ---
    --- -- Linearly interpolate halfway between black and white
    --- local gray = Color.lerp(black, white, t)
    ---
    --- print(gray)
    --- -- Returns a gray color between black and white
    --- ```
    lerp: @checked (from: Color, to: Color, t:number) -> Color,

    --- Returns a color constructed from red, green, and blue channels. Alpha
    --- defaults to 255 (fully opaque). Only the low 8 bits of each channel are
    --- kept, so 300 becomes 44 and -1 becomes 255.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Red
    --- self.color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0)
    --- ```
    rgb: @checked(r: number, g:number, b:number) -> Color,

    --- Returns a color constructed from red, green, blue, and alpha channels.
    --- Only the low 8 bits of each channel are kept, so 300 becomes 44 and -1
    --- becomes 255.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Red at 50% opacity
    --- self.color = Color.rgba(255, 0, 0, 128)
    --- ```
    rgba: @checked(r: number, g:number, b:number, a:number) -> Color,

    --- Convert a Color (ARGB packed integer) to an `{r, g, b, a}` table
    --- with values in 0–1 range. Use with `clearColor` in render passes.
    --- ```lua
    --- local cc = Color.toFloat(Color.rgba(255, 0, 0, 128))
    --- -- cc = {1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.502}
    --- ```
    toFloat: @checked (color: Color) -> { number },
}
```

    --- ```

    --- local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
    --- print(dv.isBoolean) -- false
    --- ```

end


--- `DataValue` that stores a string value.

    --- The stored string value.

end

--- `DataValue` that stores a boolean value.

    --- The stored boolean value.

end

    --- data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)

    --- print(data.red) -- 128
    --- data.red = 233

    --- Color components in the range [0, 255].
    --- ```lua
    --- local data = DataValue.color()
    --- data.value = Color.rgba(128, 55, 12, 1)
    ---
    --- print(data.green) -- 55

    --- data.alpha = 255

--- Constructors for `DataValue` types. Each function returns a mutable
--- DataValue container of the corresponding underlying type.
declare DataValue: {

    --- Creates a `DataValueNumber` that stores a number.

--- Represents a listener callback that can observe changes on an object.
--- See Property addListener and PropertyTrigger addListener.
export type Listener<T> = <K>(self:T, obj:K, (K)->()) -> () & (self:T, ()->()) -> ()

--- Represents a mutable property that stores a value and supports change listeners.
export type Property<T> = {
    --- The current value of the property.
    ---
    --- You can both read and assign to this field.
    --- ```lua
    --- local health = vm:getNumber("health")
    ---
    --- if health then
    ---   print(health.value) -- read
    ---   health.value = 100  -- write
    --- end
    --- ```
    value: T,

    --- Registers a listener that is called whenever the property's value changes.
    ---
    --- This function has two signatures:
    --- - `addListener(callback)` — Simple form, just pass the callback function.
    --- - `addListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor object and a callback.
    ---   The anchor is stored alongside the listener and passed to the callback
    ---   when invoked. This is useful for preventing garbage collection of objects
    ---   you need to keep alive while the listener is active.
    ---
    --- **Important:** If you obtain a ViewModel or property using a local variable
    --- (e.g., `local vm = context:viewModel()`) and add listeners without storing
    --- the ViewModel elsewhere, it may be garbage collected after the function
    --- returns. To prevent this, either:
    --- - Store the ViewModel on `self` (e.g., `self.vm = context:viewModel()`)
    --- - Pass the ViewModel as the anchor parameter to `addListener`
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- local health = vm:getNumber("health")
    ---
    --- if health then
    ---   local function onHealthChanged(prop)
    ---     print("New health:", prop.value)
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   health:addListener(onHealthChanged)
    ---
    ---   health.value = 50 -- Triggers listener
    --- end
    --- ```
    ---
    --- Using the anchor parameter to keep the ViewModel alive:
    --- ```lua
    --- local vm = context:viewModel()
    --- local health = vm:getNumber("health")
    ---
    --- if health then
    ---   health:addListener(vm, function(anchor)
    ---     -- 'anchor' is the vm we passed, kept alive by the listener
    ---     print("Health changed!")
    ---   end)
    --- end
    --- ```
    addListener: Listener<Property<T>>,

    --- Removes a previously registered listener.
    ---
    --- This function has two signatures:
    --- - `removeListener(callback)` — Pass the callback function to remove.
    --- - `removeListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor and the callback.
    ---   The anchor parameter is accepted for API symmetry with `addListener`,
    ---   but only the callback is used for matching.
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- local health = vm:getNumber("health")
    ---
    --- if health then
    ---   local function onHealthChanged(prop)
    ---     print("New health:", prop.value)
    ---     health:removeListener(onHealthChanged)
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   health:addListener(onHealthChanged)
    ---
    ---   health.value = 50 -- Triggers listener
    --- end
    --- ```
    removeListener: Listener<Property<T>>,
}

--- Represents a trigger property that can fire events and notify listeners.
--- Unlike other `Property` types, a trigger does not store a persistent value. It emits an event when fire() is called.
export type PropertyTrigger = {

    --- Registers a listener that is invoked when the trigger fires.
    ---
    --- This function has two signatures:
    --- - `addListener(callback)` — Simple form, just pass the callback function.
    --- - `addListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor object and a callback.
    ---   The anchor is stored alongside the listener and passed to the callback
    ---   when invoked. This is useful for preventing garbage collection of objects
    ---   you need to keep alive while the listener is active.
    ---
    --- **Important:** If you obtain a ViewModel or property using a local variable
    --- (e.g., `local vm = context:viewModel()`) and add listeners without storing
    --- the ViewModel elsewhere, it may be garbage collected after the function
    --- returns. To prevent this, either:
    --- - Store the ViewModel on `self` (e.g., `self.vm = context:viewModel()`)
    --- - Pass the ViewModel as the anchor parameter to `addListener`
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- local vmi = context:viewModel()
    --- if vmi then
    ---   local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---   if cannon then
    ---     cannon:addListener(function()
    ---       print("cannon fired!")
    ---     end)
    ---
    ---     cannon:fire()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    ---
    --- Using the anchor parameter to keep the ViewModel alive:
    --- ```lua
    --- local vm = context:viewModel()
    --- if vm then
    ---   local cannon = vm:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---   if cannon then
    ---     cannon:addListener(vm, function(anchor)
    ---       -- 'anchor' is the vm we passed, kept alive by the listener
    ---       print("cannon fired!")
    ---     end)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    addListener: Listener<PropertyTrigger>,

    --- Removes a previously registered listener.
    --- Always remove listeners when they are no longer needed to avoid leaks.
    ---
    --- This function has two signatures:
    --- - `removeListener(callback)` — Pass the callback function to remove.
    --- - `removeListener(anchor, callback)` — Pass an anchor and the callback.
    ---   The anchor parameter is accepted for API symmetry with `addListener`,
    ---   but only the callback is used for matching.
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vmi = context:viewModel()
    ---   if vmi then
    ---     local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---     if cannon then
    ---       self.cannon = cannon
    ---       self.onCannonFired = onCannonFired
    ---       cannon:addListener(onCannonFired)
    ---     end
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function removeCannonListener(self: MyNode)
    ---   if self.cannon then
    ---     self.cannon:removeListener(self.onCannonFired)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    removeListener: Listener<PropertyTrigger>,

    --- Fires the trigger and notifies all registered listeners.
    --- ```lua
    --- local vmi = context:viewModel()
    --- if vmi then
    ---   local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---   if cannon then
    ---     cannon:addListener(function()
    ---       print("cannon fired!")
    ---     end)
    ---
    ---     cannon:fire()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    fire: (self:PropertyTrigger) -> (),
}
```

--- of `text` (text documents) or `bytes` (binary documents) is set. Positions

export type FormatDocument = {

    read name: string,

    --- File extension of the document without the dot, e.g. "md".
    read extension: string,

    --- Full document text, nil for binary documents.
    read text: string?,

    --- Document bytes, nil for text documents.
    read bytes: buffer?,
}

--- Highlight scope for a token. Scopes map onto the same theme colors used by
--- the Luau and WGSL editors.
---
--- * `none`
--- * `keyword`
--- * `type`
--- * `literal`
--- * `number`
--- * `operator`
--- * `punctuation`
--- * `property`
--- * `string`
--- * `comment`
--- * `boolean`
--- * `nil`
--- * `interp`
--- * `function`
export type FormatScope = 'none' | 'keyword' | 'type' | 'literal' | 'number'
    | 'operator' | 'punctuation' | 'property' | 'string' | 'comment'
    | 'boolean' | 'nil' | 'interp' | 'function'

--- One highlight run. When `length` is omitted the run extends to the next
--- token on the same line, or the end of the line.
export type FormatToken = {
    line: number,
    column: number,
    scope: FormatScope,
    length: number?,
}

--- A problem to show in the document's gutter and problems panel.
export type FormatDiagnostic = {
    startLine: number,
    startColumn: number,
    endLine: number,
    endColumn: number,
    message: string,

    --- Defaults to 'error' when omitted.
    severity: ('error' | 'warning')?,
}

--- An autocomplete entry. When the range is omitted the completion inserts at
--- the cursor position.
export type FormatCompletion = {
    text: string,
    startLine: number?,
    startColumn: number?,
    endLine: number?,
    endColumn: number?,
}

--- Documentation shown when hovering the given range.
export type FormatHover = {
    startLine: number,
    startColumn: number,
    endLine: number,
    endColumn: number,

    --- Short single line preview, e.g. a signature.
    preview: string?,

    --- Markdown body.
    documentation: string?,
}

--- Style for one highlight scope, plain values so they can feed paints,
--- view models, or anything else.
export type EditorThemeStyle = {
    read color: Color,
    read weight: number?,
}

--- The editor's resolved code theme (defaults, the user's Luau config, and
--- overrides already merged). Values refresh live when the user's config
--- changes; read inside draw/measure rather than caching across frames.
export type EditorTheme = {

    --- Per-scope styles, the same palette the editor uses for this
    --- document's highlight tokens.
    read scopes: { [FormatScope]: EditorThemeStyle },
    read background: Color,
    read divider: Color,
    read dividerHighlight: Color,
    read error: Color,
    read warning: Color,
    read lineNumber: Color,
    read fontSize: number,
    read lineHeight: number,
}

--- Scroll position of the text editor pane showing this document. `line` is
--- the fractional 0-based line at the top of the viewport: 10.5 means the
--- viewport top sits halfway through line 10. `percent` runs 0 to 1 across
--- the editor's scrollable range.
export type EditorScroll = {
    read percent: number,
    read line: number,
    --- Scrollable range in line units (the top line when fully scrolled).
    read maxLine: number,
    --- The primary cursor's line, and where it sits in the viewport
    --- (0 top to 1 bottom, outside that range when off screen). Nil when
    --- the editor has no cursor.
    read cursorLine: number?,
    read cursorFraction: number?,
}

--- Edit time context handed to FileFormat views. Everything it returns is
--- either immutable or a private instance; nothing reaches back into the
--- open file's live state.
declare extern type EditorContext with

    --- Looks up an image asset by name, or nil when missing.
    function image(self, name: string): Image?

    --- Looks up a blob asset by name, or nil when missing.
    function blob(self, name: string): Blob?

    --- A fresh instance of a named artboard, private to this view. The
    --- artboard's default view model instance is bound and reachable through
    --- `data`, nil when the artboard has no view model.
    ---
    --- Names resolve against this script's own file, so a format shipped in a
    --- library reaches that library's artboards. Prefix a name with a
    --- library's namespace (`markdown@0/Document`) to name one explicitly,
    --- and use `hostArtboard` for the file being edited.
    function artboard(self, name: string): Artboard<ViewModel?>?

    --- Like `artboard`, but always resolves in the file being edited. When
    --- this script is authored in that same file the two are identical, so a
    --- library developed in place behaves as it does once shipped.
    function hostArtboard(self, name: string): Artboard<ViewModel?>?

    --- The editor's current theme.
    function theme(self): EditorTheme

    --- Opens a url in the user's browser.
    function openUrl(self, url: string)

    --- The font the code editor renders with, for previews that want to
    --- match its typography. Assign to a view model font property.
    function themeFont(self): Font?

    --- The editor's default UI font, for preview prose. Assign to a view
    --- model font property.
    function defaultFont(self): Font?

    --- The editor's built-in code font, for preview code regions. Assign to
    --- a view model font property.
    function codeFont(self): Font?

    --- The text editor's scroll position, refreshed each draw while the user
    --- scrolls, or nil on surfaces without an attached editor (inspector,
    --- viewer tab). Use with `scrollTo` to keep the preview in sync.
    function editorScroll(self): EditorScroll?

    --- Scrolls the pane hosting this view to a content offset, clamped to
    --- the measured content. Only meaningful for pane views with `measure`;
    --- elsewhere it is ignored.
    function scrollTo(self, x: number, y: number): ()

    --- Scrolls the attached text editor to a fractional line factor (the
    --- same unit `editorScroll` reports), clamped to the editor's range.
    --- Ignored without an attached editor. Guard against ping-pong when
    --- combining with `editorScroll` driven syncing.
    function scrollEditorTo(self, line: number): ()

    --- Asks the host to repaint the view outside the advance loop, e.g. when
    --- an async decode completes.
    function requestDraw(self): ()

    --- Looks up a compiled shader by name, or nil when missing.
    function shader(self, name: string): Shader?

    --- Creates a CPU canvas. Zero or missing size defers the backing
    --- texture.
    function canvas(self, desc: { width: number?, height: number? }?): Canvas

    --- Creates a GPU canvas for render pass drawing. Zero or missing size
    --- defers the backing texture.
    function gpuCanvas(self, desc: { width: number?, height: number? }?): GPUCanvas

    --- Capabilities of the active GPU device.
    function features(self): GPUFeatures

    --- Decodes an encoded image (png, jpeg, webp) into a drawable image.
    function decodeImage(self, data: buffer): Promise<DecodedImage>

end

--- Where a FileFormat view is hosted: 'pane' for the editor split or full
--- viewer tab, 'inspector' for the selected asset strip.
export type FormatSurface = {
    read kind: 'pane' | 'inspector',
}

--- A live preview of one document on one surface. Created by
--- `FileFormat.view`; disposed when its surface closes.
export type FormatView = {

    --- Draws the current frame into a viewport of width by height.
    draw: (self: FormatView, renderer: Renderer,
        width: number, height: number) -> (),

    --- Pane surfaces only: the content's intrinsic size for the given
    --- viewport, driving the pane's scrollbars. Called when the view is
    --- created, the document changes, the viewport resizes, or requestDraw
    --- fires. Omit for fit-to-viewport views; the inspector never measures.
    measure: ((self: FormatView, viewportWidth: number,
        viewportHeight: number) -> (number, number))?,

    --- Advances animation state. Return true to keep receiving frames.
    advance: ((self: FormatView, seconds: number) -> boolean)?,

    --- The user scrolled the text editor. x/y are scroll percentages and
    --- line is the fractional top visible line. Never fired for scrolls the
    --- host performed on the view's behalf (scrollEditorTo), so handlers can
    --- follow without echo bookkeeping.
    textScrolled: ((self: FormatView, x: number, y: number,
        line: number, maxLine: number) -> ())?,

    --- The user scrolled the preview pane (measured views only). x/y are the
    --- new offsets in content coordinates. Never fired for scrolls the host
    --- applied from `editor:scrollTo`.
    paneScrolled: ((self: FormatView, x: number, y: number) -> ())?,

    --- Raw wheel/trackpad input over an unmeasured (self-scrolling) preview,
    --- in pixels with positive y scrolling down. Implement to route pane
    --- input into the view's own scrolling; without it the host falls back
    --- to scrolling the paired text editor.
    paneWheel: ((self: FormatView, dx: number, dy: number) -> ())?,

    --- Pointer input over the preview surface, in the same coordinate space
    --- draw receives. Signatures match the Layout protocol so live artboards
    --- can forward events directly (board:pointerDown(event), ...).
    pointerDown: ((self: FormatView, event: PointerEvent) -> ())?,
    pointerMove: ((self: FormatView, event: PointerEvent) -> ())?,
    pointerUp: ((self: FormatView, event: PointerEvent) -> ())?,

    --- Text documents only: the document changed; refresh derived state.
    documentChanged: ((self: FormatView, doc: FormatDocument,
        parsed: buffer?) -> ())?,

    --- Text documents only: the primary cursor moved. line and column are
    --- zero based code point coordinates.
    selectionChanged: ((self: FormatView, line: number,
        column: number) -> ())?,

    --- The surface is closing; release resources.
    dispose: ((self: FormatView) -> ())?,
}

--- Implement this protocol to add editor support for a custom binary file
--- format. Files with a claimed extension import as blobs, keeping their raw
--- bytes, and get previews from `view`. For text formats that should be
--- editable in the editor, implement TextFileFormat instead.
--- ```lua
--- local format: FileFormat = {
---     name = 'Model',
---     extensions = { 'glb' },
--- }
---
--- return function(): FileFormat
---     return format
--- end
--- ```
export type FileFormat = {

    --- Display name of the format, e.g. "Markdown".
    name: string,

    --- File extensions handled, without dots, e.g. `{"md", "markdown"}`.
    extensions: {string},

    --- Optional. Called once per document version; the returned buffer is
    --- cached by Rive, keyed to the document's content, and passed back into
    --- every other callback. Within one VM the same buffer object is reused;
    --- across VMs the bytes are copied once.
    parse: ((self: Self, doc: FormatDocument) -> buffer?)?,

    --- Creates the preview for a document on a surface. Each surface gets
    --- its own view; a document can be visible on several at once.
    view: ((self: Self,
        doc: FormatDocument,
        editor: EditorContext,
        surface: FormatSurface,
        parsed: buffer?) -> FormatView?)?,

}

--- A FileFormat for text. Files with a claimed extension import as in-band
--- text documents, editable in the editor and synced across collaborators,
--- and the callbacks below drive the text editor's intelligence. Documents
--- export as plain blobs, so scripts read them via `context:blob(name)` at
--- both edit time and runtime.
---
--- Analysis callbacks are pure functions of `(doc, parsed)`; state lives
--- only in views. `parsed` carries the cached result of `parse`, or nil when
--- `parse` is not implemented.
--- ```lua
--- local format: TextFileFormat = {
---     name = 'Markdown',
---     extensions = { 'md' },
--- }
---
--- return function(): TextFileFormat
---     return format
--- end
--- ```
export type TextFileFormat = {

    --- Returns highlight tokens for the document.
    highlight: ((self: TextFileFormat, doc: FormatDocument,
        parsed: buffer?) -> {FormatToken})?,

    --- Returns problems for the document.
    diagnostics: ((self: TextFileFormat, doc: FormatDocument,
        parsed: buffer?) -> {FormatDiagnostic})?,

    --- Returns completions at the given position.
    completions: ((self: TextFileFormat,
        doc: FormatDocument,
        line: number,
        column: number,
        parsed: buffer?) -> {FormatCompletion})?,

    --- Returns hover documentation at the given position, or nil.
    hover: ((self: TextFileFormat,
        doc: FormatDocument,
        line: number,
        column: number,
        parsed: buffer?) -> FormatHover?)?,

    --- Returns the fully formatted text, or nil to leave the document
    --- unchanged. Rive diffs the result against the current text and applies
    --- minimal edits.
    format: ((self: TextFileFormat, doc: FormatDocument,
        parsed: buffer?) -> string?)?,
}
```

    | 'decrement-clamp' | 'invert' | 'increment-wrap' | 'decrement-wrap'

--- An entry binding a uniform buffer into a BindGroup.

    slot: number,
    buffer: GPUBuffer,
    offset: number?,

--- An entry binding a sampler into a BindGroup.

--- Public BindGroupLayout — describes the contract a BindGroup conforms
--- to and a Pipeline references for one of its `@group(N)` slots.
---
--- You typically don't construct one directly. Two paths:
---   1. Auto (default) — omit `bindGroupLayouts` on `GPUPipeline.new` and
---      retrieve via `pipeline:getBindGroupLayout(N)` for `GPUBindGroup.new`.
---      Holds only what the pipeline's own entry points bind. Mirrors
---      WebGPU's `layout: 'auto'`.
---   2. Explicit — call `GPUBindGroupLayout.new` and pass the layout to N
---      pipelines via `bindGroupLayouts = { sharedLayout }`. ONE BindGroup
---      then binds across all those pipelines (e.g. a per-frame
---      camera/lights group reused by many materials), avoiding per-
---      pipeline BindGroup duplication and reducing descriptor traffic.

end

declare GPUBindGroupLayout: {
    new: @checked (desc: BindGroupLayoutDesc) -> GPUBindGroupLayout,

--- TextureView, Sampler), keeping them alive for the BindGroup's lifetime.

declare GPUBindGroup: {

-- ============================================================================
-- Pipeline descriptor types
-- ============================================================================

--- Per-vertex attribute within a vertex buffer layout.
--- `offset` is the byte offset of this attribute within the vertex (default 0).
--- For interleaved layouts with multiple attributes you must set offset explicitly,
--- e.g. offset = 0 for position (float3 = 12 bytes), offset = 12 for normal, etc.
export type VertexAttribute = { format: VertexFormat, slot: number, offset: number? }

--- Describes how one vertex buffer feeds attributes to the vertex shader.
export type VertexBufferLayout = {
    --- Byte stride between vertices.
    stride: number,
    --- Advance per vertex or per instance (default 'vertex').
    stepMode: ('vertex' | 'instance')?,
    --- Vertex attributes sourced from this buffer.
    attributes: { VertexAttribute },
}

--- Blend equation for a single color target.
export type BlendState = {
    srcColor: BlendFactor?, dstColor: BlendFactor?, colorOp: BlendOp?,
    srcAlpha: BlendFactor?, dstAlpha: BlendFactor?, alphaOp: BlendOp?,
}

--- Color target format and optional blend state.
export type ColorTarget = {
    format: ColorFormat?,
    blend: BlendState?,
    --- Channels to write: 'all' (default), 'none', or a string of r/g/b/a
    --- characters such as 'rg'. An empty string also disables color writes.
    writeMask: string?,
}

--- Stencil operations for one triangle face. Set `stencilFront` and
--- `stencilBack` on GPUPipeline.new's descriptor, alongside `depthStencil`.
export type StencilFaceState = {
    --- Stencil comparison (default 'always').
    compare: CompareFunction?,
    --- Stencil test failed (default 'keep').
    failOp: StencilOp?,
    --- Stencil passed but depth failed (default 'keep').
    depthFailOp: StencilOp?,
    --- Both stencil and depth passed (default 'keep').
    passOp: StencilOp?,
}

--- Attachment format and depth fixed-function state. Omit from the pipeline
--- to disable depth testing. Stencil face operations and masks are separate
--- top-level pipeline fields, not members of this table.
export type DepthStencilState = {
    format: DepthFormat?,
    compare: CompareFunction?,
    --- Write depth on pass (default false).
    write: boolean?,
    depthBias: number?,
    depthBiasSlopeScale: number?,
    --- Maximum depth bias magnitude (default 0: no clamp). A nonzero value
    --- requires context:features().depthBiasClamp.
    depthBiasClamp: number?,
}

-- ============================================================================
-- Render pass descriptor types
-- ============================================================================

--- Color attachment descriptor for canvas:beginRenderPass.
export type ColorAttachment = {
    --- Optional render target view. Defaults to the receiving target's
    --- own `view` when omitted. Provide an explicit view for cases
    --- where the target differs — most commonly MSAA, where `view` is the
    --- multisampled GPUTexture:view() and `resolveTarget` is the canvas's
    --- 1× colorView().
    view: GPUTextureView?,
    --- 1× resolve target for MSAA (formats must match `view`).
    resolveTarget: GPUTextureView?,
    loadOp: LoadOp?,
    --- Required; 'discard' after MSAA resolve, 'store' otherwise.
    storeOp: StoreOp,
    clearColor: GPUColor?,
}

--- Depth/stencil attachment descriptor for canvas:beginRenderPass.
--- Independent stencil load/store controls are not exposed by this binding.
--- Metal clears stencil to 0 and discards it at pass end; Vulkan currently
--- derives stencil load/store actions from depthLoadOp/depthStoreOp.
--- For portability, clear the attachment and write/test stencil in one pass
--- rather than relying on stencil preservation across passes.
export type DepthStencilAttachment = {
    --- Required. Use GPUTexture:view().
    view: GPUTextureView,
    depthLoadOp: LoadOp?,
    --- Required; 'discard' for transient depth, 'store' to read it later.
    depthStoreOp: StoreOp,
    depthClearValue: number?,
}

--- Render pass descriptor for canvas:beginRenderPass. Must include at
--- least one color attachment or a depthStencil attachment. All attachments
--- (color views + depth) must share one sampleCount, derived per WebGPU
--- rules — pass sampleCount is inferred from the views, not declared.
export type RenderPassDesc = {
    color: { ColorAttachment }?,
    depthStencil: DepthStencilAttachment?,
    --- Names the pass in Vulkan GPU profiles and Metal or WebGPU debug captures.
    label: string?,
}

-- ============================================================================
-- GPUPipeline
-- ============================================================================

--- A compiled GPU render pipeline (shaders + fixed-function state).
declare extern type GPUPipeline with
    --- Returns the layout the pipeline auto-derived for `@group(N)`.
    --- Errors if `bindGroupLayouts` was supplied at construction (reuse
    --- the explicit one) or if the pipeline's entry points do not bind N.
    --- Mirrors WebGPU's `pipeline.getBindGroupLayout(index)`.
    function getBindGroupLayout(self, groupIndex: number): GPUBindGroupLayout
end

--- A pipeline stage: a Shader, or WebGPU-style `{ module = Shader,
--- entryPoint = name }`. The Shader's `@vertex`/`@fragment` functions are the
--- selectable entry points; omit `entryPoint` to use the first one of that
--- stage (like WebGPU).
---
--- Vertex and fragment may come from different Shaders. Each file's bindings
--- are numbered on its own, so on Vulkan, D3D12 and GL — which share one slot
--- namespace between the stages — two files that declare different bindings
--- can collide; `GPUPipeline.new` rejects that case naming both bindings.
--- Declaring the same bindings in both files always works.
export type PipelineStage = Shader | { module: Shader, entryPoint: string? }

declare GPUPipeline: {
    new: @checked (desc: {
        --- Vertex stage (required). A Shader, or `{ module, entryPoint? }`.
        vertex: PipelineStage,
        --- Fragment stage (optional for depth-only passes). A Shader, or
        --- `{ module, entryPoint? }`. When omitted but colorTargets are set,
        --- falls back to the vertex shader's first @fragment.
        fragment: PipelineStage?,
        --- Vertex buffer layouts. Each entry maps to one buffer slot; pass
        --- an empty table for a shader that builds its own positions from
        --- `@builtin(vertex_index)`.
        vertexLayout: { VertexBufferLayout },
        --- Optional. Omit to derive a layout per `@group(N)` from what the
        --- pipeline's own entry points bind (WebGPU's `layout: 'auto'`); a
        --- group they never bind needs no BindGroup. Retrieve via
        --- `pipeline:getBindGroupLayout(N)` for BindGroup creation.
        --- Supply explicitly only to share one layout across multiple
        --- pipelines — e.g. a per-frame camera/lights group reused by
        --- many materials, so a single BindGroup binds to all of them.
        bindGroupLayouts: { GPUBindGroupLayout }?,
        --- Color attachment formats and blend state. Must match the render pass.
        colorTargets: { ColorTarget }?,
        --- Depth/stencil state. Omit to disable depth testing entirely.
        depthStencil: DepthStencilState?,
        --- Front/back stencil tests and operations. Require a stencil-bearing
        --- depthStencil.format and a matching render-pass attachment, e.g.
        --- 'depth24plus-stencil8'. Defaults: compare 'always', operations 'keep'.
        --- These are top-level fields, not nested inside depthStencil.
        stencilFront: StencilFaceState?,
        stencilBack: StencilFaceState?,
        --- 8-bit comparison/write masks, each defaulting to 255 (0xFF).
        stencilReadMask: number?,
        stencilWriteMask: number?,
        --- Face culling (default 'none').
        cullMode: CullMode?,
        --- Front-face winding (default 'ccw').
        winding: FaceWinding?,
        --- Primitive topology (default 'triangle-list').
        topology: PrimitiveTopology?,
        --- Must match the sampleCount of the render target. Default: 1.
        sampleCount: number?,
    }) -> GPUPipeline,
}

-- ============================================================================
-- Canvas — Rive 2-D renderer canvas
-- ============================================================================

--- A Rive 2-D renderer canvas. Use `.image` with `renderer:drawImage()`.
--- Call `beginFrame()` to get a Renderer, issue draw calls, then `endFrame()`.
--- Its contents last until the next `beginFrame()`, so a frame that skips it
--- still draws or samples the last one.
declare extern type Canvas with
    --- Backing image for `renderer:drawImage()`.
    image: Image
    --- Width in pixels.
    width: number
    --- Height in pixels.
    height: number
    --- Resize the canvas. Must not be called between beginFrame() and endFrame().
    function resize(self, width: number, height: number): ()
    --- Begin a Rive frame. Returns a Renderer valid until endFrame().
    --- clearColor is an ARGB integer (e.g. 0xFF000000 = opaque black; default transparent).
    function beginFrame(self, desc: { clearColor: Color? }?): Renderer
    --- Flush draw calls to the backing texture and release the Renderer.
    function endFrame(self): ()
end

-- ============================================================================
-- GPUTarget — anything a render pass draws into
-- ============================================================================

--- Something a render pass can draw into. It promises neither sampling nor
--- contents kept between frames; `GPUCanvas` adds both.
declare extern type GPUTarget with
    --- Width in pixels.
    width: number
    --- Height in pixels.
    height: number
    --- Pixel format of the target. MSAA resolve requires source and target to
    --- have identical formats — always derive GPUTexture and pipeline formats
    --- from this value:
    --- ```lua
    ---   local fmt = target.format
    ---   GPUPipeline.new({ colorTargets = {{ format = fmt }}, sampleCount = 4 })
    --- ```
    format: ColorFormat
    --- Samples per pixel. Always 1 for a canvas; can be above 1 for
    --- `context:gpuTarget()` on some hosts.
    sampleCount: number
    --- View of the target, for a color attachment or an MSAA resolve target.
    --- Nil on a frame with nothing to draw into. Read it each frame; a view
    --- kept across a resize errors when a pass uses it.
    view: GPUTextureView?
    --- Open a GPU render pass targeting this target. The descriptor must
    --- include at least one color attachment or a depthStencil attachment.
    --- Color attachment views default to this target's view when omitted;
    --- provide them explicitly when rendering to a different target (e.g.
    --- MSAA). The pass's sampleCount is derived from the attachments (WebGPU
    --- rule: all attachments share one sampleCount). Must be called during
    --- draw. Issue draw calls on the returned pass, then call `:finish()`. A
    --- pass may begin while another is open, as when a drawn artboard's own
    --- scripts render: it runs ahead of the pass it was begun inside, so that
    --- pass can sample its output. With nothing to draw into, the pass drops
    --- its commands.
    function beginRenderPass(self, desc: RenderPassDesc): GPURenderPass
end

-- ============================================================================
-- GPUCanvas — GPU canvas
-- ============================================================================

--- A GPU canvas — a 1× presentation target, same role as a WebGPU surface
--- texture. Use `.image` with `renderer:drawImage()` to composite the
--- result. Render to it via `canvas:beginRenderPass({ color = {{ loadOp =
--- 'clear', storeOp = 'store', ... }} })`. MSAA requires a user-allocated
--- `GPUTexture.new({ sampleCount = N, renderTarget = true })` as the
--- explicit color view, with the canvas's `colorView()` as `resolveTarget`.
--- Its format is always 'rgba8unorm', reported before a deferred canvas
--- allocates its texture.
export type GPUCanvas = GPUTarget & {
    --- Backing image for `renderer:drawImage()`.
    image: Image,
    --- Resize the canvas. Recreates the 1× backing texture. Any
    --- user-allocated MSAA / depth textures must be recreated by the
    --- script to match the new dimensions.
    resize: (self: GPUCanvas, width: number, height: number) -> (),
    --- View of the canvas backing texture. Use as a color attachment, an
    --- MSAA resolve target, or a sampler input in a subsequent pass.
    colorView: (self: GPUCanvas) -> GPUTextureView,
}

-- ============================================================================
-- GPURenderPass
-- ============================================================================

--- An active render pass. Issue all draw calls before calling finish().
declare extern type GPURenderPass with
    --- Bind a pipeline for subsequent draw calls.
    function setPipeline(self, pipeline: GPUPipeline): ()
    --- Bind a vertex buffer to slot (0-based).
    function setVertexBuffer(self, slot: number, buffer: GPUBuffer): ()
    --- Bind an index buffer. format defaults to 'uint16'.
    function setIndexBuffer(self, buffer: GPUBuffer, format: ('uint16' | 'uint32')?): ()
    --- Bind a pre-created BindGroup to a group slot.
    --- dynamicOffsets: one byte offset per dynamic UBO in this group
    --- (dynamic UBOs are declared with `dynamicUBOs` on
    --- `GPUBindGroupLayout.new`; auto-derived layouts have none). Order matches the UBOs' appearance
    --- in `BindGroupDesc.ubos`. Typical 3D pattern: shared texture
    --- BindGroup at group 1, per-object UBO dynamic offset at group 0.
    function setBindGroup(self, groupIndex: number, bg: GPUBindGroup, dynamicOffsets: {number}?): ()
    --- Set the render viewport in pixels. Origin is top-left on all backends except GL (bottom-left).
    function setViewport(self, x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number): ()
    --- Set the scissor rectangle in pixels.
    function setScissorRect(self, x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number): ()
    --- Set the stencil reference used for comparison and the 'replace'
    --- operation. Configure tests/operations on GPUPipeline.new using its
    --- top-level stencilFront/stencilBack fields; use a stencil attachment.
    function setStencilReference(self, ref: number): ()
    --- Set the constant blend color, 0–1 per channel, for 'constant' /
    --- 'one-minus-constant' factors.
    function setBlendColor(self, r: number, g: number, b: number, a: number): ()
    --- Non-indexed draw. instanceCount defaults to 1, firstVertex to 0.
    function draw(self, vertexCount: number, instanceCount: number?, firstVertex: number?): ()
    --- Indexed draw. instanceCount defaults to 1, firstIndex to 0.
    function drawIndexed(self, indexCount: number, instanceCount: number?, firstIndex: number?): ()
    --- Submit the pass, along with any pass begun inside it that is still
    --- open. Any further method calls on this object will error.
    function finish(self): ()
end
```

--- A color stop in a `Gradient`, defined by its position in the range [0, 1] and

export type GradientStop = {

    ---     {
    ---         position = 0,
    ---         color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0)

    ---         color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255)

    --- })

    --- ```lua
    --- local g = Gradient.linear(Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(100, 0), {
    ---     {
    ---         position = 0,
    ---         color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0)
    ---     },
    ---     {
    ---         position = 1,
    ---         color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255)
    ---     },
    --- })
    --- ```
    color: number,
}

declare Gradient: {

    --- Creates a linear gradient that transitions between the specified color
    --- stops along the line from 'from' to 'to'.
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- local g = Gradient.linear(Vector.xy(0, 0), Vector.xy(100, 0), {
    ---   { position = 0, color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0) },
    ---   { position = 1, color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255) },
    --- })
    --- ```
    linear: @checked (from: Vector, to: Vector, stops: { GradientStop } ) -> Gradient,

    --- Creates a radial gradient centered at 'from', extending outward to the
    --- given radius, using the specified color stops.
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- local g = Gradient.radial(Vector.xy(50, 50), 40, {
    ---   { position = 0, color = Color.rgb(255, 0, 0) },
    ---   { position = 1, color = Color.rgb(0, 0, 255) },
    --- })
    --- ```
    radial: @checked (from: Vector, radius: number, stops: { GradientStop } ) -> Gradient,
}

--- }
---

---   self.myImage = context:image('myImage')
---   self.sampler = ImageSampler('clamp', 'clamp', 'bilinear')
---
---   return true
--- end
---
--- function draw(self: DrawImage, renderer: Renderer)
---   if self.myImage and self.sampler then
---     renderer:drawImage(self.myImage, self.sampler, 'srcOver', 1)
---   end
--- end
---
--- return function(): Node<DrawImage>

---     myImage = nil,
---     sampler = nil,
---     init = init,
---     draw = draw,
---   }
--- end

declare extern type ImageSampler with
end

--- Defines how texture coordinates outside the [0, 1] range are handled.
--- * `clamp`
--- * `repeat`
--- * `mirror`
---
--- See `ImageSampler` for usage.
--- ```lua
--- function init(self: DrawImage, context: Context): boolean
---   self.myImage = context:image('myImage')
---   self.sampler = ImageSampler(
---     -- Image wrap X
---     'clamp',
---     -- Image wrap Y
---     'clamp',
---     'bilinear'
---   )
---
---   return true
--- end
--- ```
export type ImageWrap = 'clamp' | 'repeat' | 'mirror'

---   )
---
---   return true
--- end

export type ImageFilter = 'bilinear' | 'nearest'

--- ```lua
--- local function rebuildSampler(self: DrawImageSampler)

--- end
--- ```
declare function ImageSampler(wrapX: ImageWrap, wrapY: ImageWrap, filter: ImageFilter): ImageSampler
