    ---   end
    ---
    ---   local insertIndex = math.max(1, math.min(index, menu.length + 1))
    ---   menu:insert(buttonVm, insertIndex)
    --- end
    --- ```
    function insert(self, vm: ViewModel, index: number): ()

    --- Swaps the positions of the view models at `index1` and `index2`.
    --- ```lua
    --- function swapItems(menu: PropertyList, index1: number, index2: number)
    ---   local highestIndex = math.max(index1, index2)
    ---
    ---   if menu and menu.length >= highestIndex then
    ---     menu:swap(index1, index2)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function swap(self, index1: number, index2: number): ()

    --- Removes and returns the last view model in the list.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePop(self: MenuListController)
    ---   if self.menu then
    ---     self.menu:pop()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function pop(self): ViewModel?

    --- Removes and returns the first view model in the list.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handleShift(self: MenuListController)
    ---   if self.menu then
    ---     self.menu:shift()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function shift(self): ViewModel?

    --- Removes all view models from the list.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handleClearItems(self: MenuListController)
    ---   if self.menu then
    ---     self.menu:clear()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function clear(self): ()

    --- Removes a view model from the list.
    function remove(self, viewModel: ViewModel): ()

    --- Removes every list entry that references the given view model instance.
    function removeAllOf(self, viewModel: ViewModel): ()

    --- Removes the view model at the given 1-based index from the list.
    function removeAt(self, index: number): ()

    --- Adds a listener that is called when the list changes.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MenuListController, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vmi = context:rootViewModel() :: Data.Main
    ---   if vmi then
    ---     self.menu = vmi.menu
    ---     self.listChanged = listChanged
    ---
    ---     self.menu:addListener(self.listChanged)
    ---   else
    ---     print('[MenuListController] Warning: Could not find Main ViewModel.')
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    addListener: Listener<PropertyList>

    --- Removes a previously added list-change listener.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handleRemoveListener(self: MenuListController)
    ---   if self.menu and self.listChanged then
    ---     self.menu:removeListener(self.listChanged)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    removeListener: Listener<PropertyList>
end

--- Represents a property that holds a `ViewModel` value.
declare extern type PropertyViewModel with

    --- The current view model value.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: VMNameNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---     local vm = context:viewModel()
    ---     if vm then
    ---         local nestedVMProp = vm:getViewModel("nestedVM")
    ---         if nestedVMProp then
    ---             local nestedVM = nestedVMProp.value
    ---             local age = nestedVM:getNumber("age")
    ---             if age then
    ---                 print("nestedVM age:", age.value)
    ---             else
    ---                 print("'age' property not found on nestedVM.")
    ---             end
    ---         else
    ---             print("'nestedVM' property not found on ViewModel.")
    ---         end
    ---     else
    ---         print("No ViewModel found on context.")
    ---     end
    ---     return true
    --- end
    --- ```

    value: ViewModel
end

--- The file's view model factories, keyed by view model name.
--- `Data.MyViewModel.new()` creates a fresh instance of the view model named
--- `MyViewModel`; pass an instance name to copy an existing instance from the
--- file. Looking up a name with no matching view model returns nil.
--- ```lua
--- local button = Data.Button.new()
--- local label = button:getString('label')
--- if label then
---   label.value = 'Play'
--- end
--- ```
declare Data: { [string]: { new: (instanceName: string?) -> ViewModel } }

--- A blob asset containing raw binary data.
declare extern type Blob with

    --- The size of the blob data in bytes.
    --- ```lua
    --- type DrawBlob = {
    ---     myBlob: Blob?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: DrawBlob, context: Context): boolean
    ---     self.myBlob = context:blob('myBlob')
    ---
    ---     if self.myBlob then
    ---         print('Blob size:', self.myBlob.size, 'bytes')
    ---     end
    ---
    ---     return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<DrawBlob>
    ---     return {
    ---         myBlob = nil,
    ---         init = init,
    ---     }
    --- end
    --- ```
    size: number

    --- The name of the blob asset.
    --- ```lua
    --- type DrawBlob = {
    ---     myBlob: Blob?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: DrawBlob, context: Context): boolean
    ---     self.myBlob = context:blob('myBlob')
    ---
    ---     if self.myBlob then
    ---         print('Blob name:', self.myBlob.name)
    ---     end
    ---
    ---     return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<DrawBlob>
    ---     return {
    ---         myBlob = nil,
    ---         init = init,
    ---     }
    --- end
    --- ```
    name: string

    --- The raw binary data as a buffer. Read it with the `buffer` library,
    --- for example `buffer.readu8(blob.data, 0)`.
    --- ```lua
    --- type DrawBlob = {
    ---     myBlob: Blob?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: DrawBlob, context: Context): boolean
    ---     self.myBlob = context:blob('myBlob')
    ---
    ---     if self.myBlob then
    ---         print('First byte:', buffer.readu8(self.myBlob.data, 0))
    ---     end
    ---
    ---     return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<DrawBlob>
    ---     return {
    ---         myBlob = nil,
    ---         init = init,
    ---     }
    --- end
    --- ```
    data: buffer
end

--- An audio asset handle returned by `Context:audio(name)` and used with the global `Audio` API.
declare extern type AudioSource with

    --- Duration of the sound in seconds.
    duration: number
end

--- A playback instance returned by `Audio:play*`, with controls for transport and volume.
declare extern type AudioSound with

    --- Stops the audio, fading out over `fadeToStopTime` PCM frames. Omit it
    --- to stop at once. A sound that has not started yet stops at once
    --- whatever the fade.
    --- ```lua
    --- function stopSound(self: AudioScript)
    ---   if self.soundInstance then
    ---     self.soundInstance:stop()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function stop(self, fadeToStopTime: number?) : ()

    --- Seeks the audio to a specific time in seconds. Returns false when the
    --- sound was disposed or the seek failed.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.soundInstance then
    ---   self.soundInstance:seek(self.seekSeconds)
    --- end
    --- ```
    function seek(self, seconds: number) : boolean

    --- Seeks the audio to a specific time in PCM frames. Returns false when
    --- the sound was disposed or the seek failed.
    --- ```lua
    --- if self.soundInstance then
    ---   self.soundInstance:seekFrame(self.seekFrameNumber)
    --- end
    --- ```
    function seekFrame(self, frame: number) : boolean

    --- Whether the sound has completed playing.
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AudioScript, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   if self.soundInstance then
    ---     self.isCompleted = self.soundInstance:completed()      -- whether playback has finished
    ---   end
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function completed(self) : boolean

    --- Current sound time in seconds.
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AudioScript, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   if self.soundInstance then
    ---     self.currentTime = self.soundInstance:time()           -- current playback time in seconds
    ---   end
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function time(self) : number

    --- Current sound time in PCM frames.
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AudioScript, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   if self.soundInstance then
    ---     self.currentTimeFrame = self.soundInstance:timeFrame() -- current playback time in PCM frames
    ---   end
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function timeFrame(self) : number

    --- volume of the sound.
    --- ```lua
    --- function update(self: AudioScript)
    ---   -- updates the volume for AudioSound playback when the input is changed
    ---   if self.soundInstance then
    ---     self.soundInstance.volume = self.volumeNumber / 100
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    volume: number

    --- pauses the audio.
    --- ```lua
    --- function pauseSound(self: AudioScript)
    ---   if self.soundInstance then
    ---     self.soundInstance:pause()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function pause(self) : ()

    --- resumes the audio from its current position.
    --- ```lua
    --- function resumeSound(self: AudioScript)
    ---   if self.soundInstance then
    ---     self.soundInstance:resume()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function resume(self) : ()

    --- plays the audio.
    --- ```lua
    --- function playSound(self: AudioScript)
    ---   if self.soundInstance then
    ---     self.soundInstance:play()
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    function play(self) : ()
end

declare Audio: {
    --- Returns the absolute time of the underlying audio engine in seconds.
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AudioScript, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   -- Audio engine outputs: global clock independent of any sound instance
    ---   self.engineTime = Audio.time()           -- absolute engine time in seconds
    ---   self.engineTimeFrame = Audio.timeFrame() -- absolute engine time in PCM frames
    ---   self.sampleRate = Audio.sampleRate()     -- sample rate in Hz; use to convert: frames = seconds * sampleRate
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    time: @checked () -> number,

    --- Returns sample rate of the audio engine.
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AudioScript, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   -- Audio engine outputs: global clock independent of any sound instance
    ---   self.engineTime = Audio.time()           -- absolute engine time in seconds
    ---   self.engineTimeFrame = Audio.timeFrame() -- absolute engine time in PCM frames
    ---   self.sampleRate = Audio.sampleRate()     -- sample rate in Hz; use to convert: frames = seconds * sampleRate
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    sampleRate: @checked () -> number,

    --- Returns the absolute time of the underlying audio engine in PCM frames.
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: AudioScript, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   -- Audio engine outputs: global clock independent of any sound instance
    ---   self.engineTime = Audio.time()           -- absolute engine time in seconds
    ---   self.engineTimeFrame = Audio.timeFrame() -- absolute engine time in PCM frames
    ---   self.sampleRate = Audio.sampleRate()     -- sample rate in Hz; use to convert: frames = seconds * sampleRate
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    timeFrame: @checked () -> number,

    --- Play the audio immediately.
    ---
    --- Returns `AudioSound`.
    --- ```lua
    --- function playSound(self: AudioScript)
    ---   if self.sourceAsset then
    ---     self.soundInstance = Audio.play(self.sourceAsset)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    play: @checked (AudioSource) -> AudioSound?,

    --- Play the sound at a specified absolute time in seconds. Use for better control of sounds initialization.
    ---
    --- Returns `AudioSound`.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Play at an absolute engine time in seconds using Audio.playAtTime()
    --- -- Set scheduleSeconds to Audio.time() + desired offset before firing
    --- function playAtTimeSound(self: AudioScript)
    ---   if self.sourceAsset then
    ---     self.soundInstance = Audio.playAtTime(self.sourceAsset, self.scheduleSeconds)
    ---     applyVolume(self)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    playAtTime: @checked (AudioSource, number) -> AudioSound?,

    --- Play the sound at a specified relative time in seconds. Relative to current Audio engine time.
    ---
    --- Returns `AudioSound`.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Play after a relative delay in seconds using Audio.playInTime()
    --- -- Set scheduleSeconds to the number of seconds to wait before playback starts
    --- function playInTimeSound(self: AudioScript)
    ---   if self.sourceAsset then
    ---     self.soundInstance = Audio.playInTime(self.sourceAsset, self.scheduleSeconds)
    ---     applyVolume(self)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    playInTime: @checked (AudioSource, number) -> AudioSound?,

    --- Play the sound at a specified absolute time in frames. Use for better control of sounds initialization.
    ---
    --- Returns `AudioSound`.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Play at an absolute engine frame using Audio.playAtFrame()
    --- -- Set scheduleFrames to Audio.timeFrame() + desired frame offset before firing
    --- function playAtFrameSound(self: AudioScript)
    ---   if self.sourceAsset then
    ---     self.soundInstance = Audio.playAtFrame(self.sourceAsset, self.scheduleFrames)
    ---     applyVolume(self)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    playAtFrame: @checked (AudioSource, number) -> AudioSound?,

    --- Play the sound at a specified relative time in frames. Relative to current Audio engine time.
    ---
    --- Returns `AudioSound`.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Play after a relative delay in PCM frames using Audio.playInFrame()
    --- -- Set scheduleFrames to the number of frames to wait before playback starts
    --- -- Tip: frames = seconds * Audio.sampleRate()
    --- function playInFrameSound(self: AudioScript)
    ---   if self.sourceAsset then
    ---     self.soundInstance = Audio.playInFrame(self.sourceAsset, self.scheduleFrames)
    ---     applyVolume(self)
    ---   end
    --- end
    --- ```
    playInFrame: @checked (AudioSource, number) -> AudioSound?,
}

--- Raw decoded image pixels returned by context:decodeImage().
export type DecodedImage = {
    --- Premultiplied RGBA8 pixel data (width * height * 4 bytes).
    data: buffer,
    --- Width in pixels.
    width: number,
    --- Height in pixels.
    height: number,
}

--- An artboard of a file decoded with `context:decodeFile`. Assign it to a
--- view model artboard property (see `ViewModel:getArtboard`) and whatever
--- is bound to that property shows it.
declare extern type BindableArtboard with
    --- The artboard's name.
    name: string

    --- The instance of the artboard's own view model that it is bound to,
    --- or nil when the artboard has none. Changes to it show in the
    --- artboard.
    data: ViewModel?
end

--- A Rive file decoded with `context:decodeFile`. Only assets embedded in
--- the file load, and its scripts run only if Rive signed them.
declare extern type RiveFile with
    --- The names of the file's artboards, in file order.
    artboardNames: { string }

    --- The named artboard, or the file's default artboard when name is nil;
    --- nil when there is no such artboard.
    function bindableArtboard(self, name: string?): BindableArtboard?
end

--- Context is an object provided to scripted nodes during initialization (via the `init` function).
--- It serves as a bridge between your script and the Rive runtime, giving you access to:
--- - Update scheduling — Request that your node be updated on the next frame.
--- - Data (ViewModels) — Access the ViewModel data context bound to the node or the root artboard.
--- - Assets — Retrieve named assets (images, blobs, and audio) that have been added to the Rive file.
declare extern type Context with

    --- Logs a message through the host: the CLI watch log and problems
    --- surface, the editor console. Available on both script backends.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---     context.log('hello')
    ---     return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    log: (message: string) -> ()

    --- Marks the object as needing an update on the next frame.
    --- Call this when something has changed (e.g., from a listener callback) and you need the runtime to re-invoke your node's update function.
    --- Note: Calls to `markNeedsUpdate` from inside `update()` are ignored. Use it from `init()`, `advance()`, listener callbacks, or event handlers instead.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---     self.context = context
    ---     -- Access a ViewModel property and listen for changes
    ---     local vm = context:viewModel()
    ---     if vm then
    ---         local name = vm:getString("name")
    ---         if name then
    ---             name:addListener(function()
    ---                 -- Re-trigger update when the data changes
    ---                 if self.context then
    ---                     self.context:markNeedsUpdate()
    ---                 end
    ---             end)
    ---         end
    ---     end
    ---     return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function markNeedsUpdate(self): ()

    --- Returns the `ViewModel` bound to the node's immediate data context. This is the most common way
    --- to read data-bound properties from a script.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vmi = context:viewModel()
    ---   if vmi then
    ---     local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function viewModel(self): ViewModel?

    --- Returns the `ViewModel` bound to the root artboard's data context.
    --- Useful when you need to access top-level data from a deeply nested node.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local vmi = context:rootViewModel()
    ---   if vmi then
    ---     local cannon = vmi:getTrigger('cannon')
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function rootViewModel(self): ViewModel?

    --- Returns the global `ViewModel` with the given name, or nil if there is no
    --- global view model by that name or none is currently bound.
    --- Global view models are shared, singleton-like view models addressed by name
    --- rather than through the node's own data context.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local settings = context:globalViewModel('AppSettings')
    ---   if settings then
    ---     local volume = settings:getNumber('volume')
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function globalViewModel(self, name: string): ViewModel?

    --- Returns a list of the names of all global view models defined in the file.
    --- Pass any of these names to `globalViewModel` to fetch the corresponding view model.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---   for _, name in ipairs(context:globalViewModelNames()) do
    ---     print(name)
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function globalViewModelNames(self): { string }

    --- Returns the data context provided to this node.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---   local dc = context:dataContext()
    ---   if dc then
    ---      local parentDC = dc:parent()
    ---      local vm = dc:viewModel()
    ---   end
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function dataContext(self): DataContext?

    --- Returns an image asset by name, or nil if not found.
    --- The returned `Image` can be drawn via `drawImage`.
    ---
    --- See also `ImageSampler`.
    ---
    --- Check out Scripting demos to see a working example.
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- type DrawImage = {
    ---   myImage: Image?,
    ---   sampler: ImageSampler?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: DrawImage, context: Context): boolean
    ---   self.myImage = context:image('myImage')
    ---   self.sampler = ImageSampler('clamp', 'clamp', 'bilinear')
    ---
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function draw(self: DrawImage, renderer: Renderer)
    ---   if self.myImage and self.sampler then
    ---     renderer:drawImage(self.myImage, self.sampler, 'srcOver', 1)
    ---   end
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<DrawImage>
    ---   return {
    ---     myImage = nil,
    ---     sampler = nil,
    ---     init = init,
    ---     draw = draw,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    function image(self, name: string): Image?

    --- Returns a `Blob` (raw binary data) asset by name, or nil if not found.
    --- Useful for loading custom data files embedded in the Rive file.
    --- ```lua
    --- type DrawBlob = {
    ---     myBlob: Blob?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: DrawBlob, context: Context): boolean
    ---     self.myBlob = context:blob('myBlob')
    ---
    ---     if self.myBlob then
    ---         print('Blob name:', self.myBlob.name)
    ---         print('Blob size:', self.myBlob.size, 'bytes')
    ---         print('First byte:', buffer.readu8(self.myBlob.data, 0))
    ---     end
    ---
    ---     return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<DrawBlob>
    ---     return {
    ---         myBlob = nil,
    ---         init = init,
    ---     }
    --- end
    --- ```
    function blob(self, name: string): Blob?

    --- Returns a `Font` asset by name, or nil if not found.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: Label, context: Context): boolean
    ---     local font = context:font('Inter')
    ---     if font then
    ---         self.text:append('Hello', { font = font, size = 24, paint = self.paint })
    ---     end
    ---     return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function font(self, name: string): Font?

    --- Returns an `AudioSource` asset by name. The returned source can be played using the global `Audio` API.
    --- ```lua
    --- type AudioExample = {
    ---   play: Input<Trigger>,
    ---
    ---   source: AudioSource?,
    --- }
    ---
    --- function init(self: AudioExample, context: Context): boolean
    ---   self.source = context:audio("myAudio")
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function playSound(self: AudioExample)
    ---   if self.source then
    ---     Audio.play(self.source)
    ---   end
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<AudioExample>
    ---   return {
    ---     play = playSound,
    ---     source = nil,
    ---     init = init,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    function audio(self, name: string): AudioSource?

    --- Create a 2D canvas for Rive Renderer drawing.
    --- Use beginFrame/endFrame during draw to render.
    ---
    --- The descriptor is optional. Omitting it (or passing width/height of
    --- 0) creates a deferred canvas with no backing texture — useful in
    --- layout scripts that don't know their size at init. Call
    --- `canvas:resize(w, h)` once the real size is known. While deferred,
    --- `canvas.image` is nil and `width`/`height` report 0; calling
    --- `beginFrame()` raises an error pointing to `resize()`. Check
    --- `canvas.width > 0` to gate work.
    ---
    --- `clearColor` is ignored here; pass it to `beginFrame` instead.
    function canvas(self, desc: {
        width: number,
        height: number,
        clearColor: Color?,
    }?): Canvas

    --- Create a GPU canvas — a 1× presentation target. Render to it via
    --- `canvas:beginRenderPass(...)`. For MSAA, allocate the multisampled
    --- color and depth textures yourself with `GPUTexture.new({
    --- sampleCount = N, renderTarget = true })` and pass them in the
    --- descriptor.
    ---
    --- The descriptor is optional. Omitting it (or passing width/height of
    --- 0) creates a deferred canvas with no backing texture — useful in
    --- layout scripts that don't know their size at init. Call
    --- `canvas:resize(w, h)` once the real size is known. While deferred,
    --- `width`/`height` report 0 and calling `colorView()` raises an error
    --- pointing to `resize()`. Check `canvas.width > 0` to gate work.
    function gpuCanvas(self, desc: {
        width: number,
        height: number,
    }?): GPUCanvas

    --- Rive's render target: passes into it land under all of Rive's
    --- content. It cannot be sampled and starts each frame undefined, so the
    --- first pass must clear or cover it. With a sampleCount of 1 it can
    --- resolve a script's MSAA texture. On a frame the host hides it, `view`
    --- is nil and passes into it drop. Nil where the host can never expose
    --- one; keep a `gpuCanvas` and draw its image instead.
    function gpuTarget(self): GPUTarget?

    --- Query GPU capabilities. Returns a table of supported features
    --- and limits for the current backend.
    function features(self): GPUFeatures

    --- Get a compiled shader by asset name (the name as added in the editor,
    --- with no ".wgsl" extension). Returns a Shader ready for use in
    --- GPUPipeline.new(), or nil if the named shader is not found.
    function shader(self, name: string): Shader?

    --- Decode compressed image data (PNG, JPEG, WebP) into premultiplied RGBA8 pixels.
    --- Returns a Promise that resolves with a DecodedImage table.
    --- Use with await() inside async(), or chain with :andThen().
    function decodeImage(self, data: buffer): Promise<DecodedImage>

    --- Decodes the bytes of a .riv file, such as a `fetch` response body.
    --- The Promise resolves with the file, or rejects with
    --- "malformed: <message>" or "unsupportedVersion: <message>". It may
    --- settle on a later frame, so wait for it with `await` or `andThen`
    --- rather than reading its status right away. Decoding currently runs
    --- on the calling thread, so large files are best decoded from an async
    --- body, where the script time limit does not apply.
    --- ```lua
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---     local vm = context:viewModel()
    ---     if vm == nil then
    ---         return true
    ---     end
    ---     local character = vm:getArtboard('character')
    ---     async(function()
    ---         local ok, response = await(fetch("https://example.com/a.riv"))
    ---         if not ok then
    ---             return nil
    ---         end
    ---         local _, bytes = await(response:arrayBuffer())
    ---         local loaded, file = await(context:decodeFile(bytes))
    ---         if loaded and character then
    ---             character.value = file:bindableArtboard()
    ---         end
    ---         return nil
    ---     end)
    ---     return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    function decodeFile(self, data: buffer): Promise<RiveFile>

end

--- Node scripts can be used to render shapes, images, text, artboards, and more.
--- A scripted node can be attached to any Node and is rendered
--- in the local transform space of the hosting Node.
---
--- For more information, see Node Scripts.
export type Node<T> = {

    --- Called once when the node is created. Returns true if initialization
    --- succeeds.
    ---
    --- For a more complete example using `init`, see Instantiating Components.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Define the script's data and inputs.
    --- type MyNode = {}
    ---
    --- -- Called once when the script initializes.
    --- function init(self: MyNode, context: Context): boolean
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- -- Return a factory function that Rive uses to build the Node instance.
    --- return function(): Node<MyNode>
    ---   return {
    ---     init = init
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    init: ((self: T, context: Context) -> boolean)?,

    --- Optional per-frame update. Returns true if the node should continue
    --- receiving advance calls.
    ---
    --- For a more complete example using `advance`, see Fixed-step Advanced.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Define the script's data and inputs.
    --- type MyNode = {}
    ---
    --- -- Called every frame to advance the simulation.
    --- -- 'seconds' is the elapsed time since the previous frame.
    --- function advance(self: MyNode, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   return false
    --- end
    ---
    --- -- Return a factory function that Rive uses to build the Node instance.
    --- return function(): Node<MyNode>
    ---   return {
    ---     advance = advance,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    advance: ((self: T, seconds: number) -> boolean)?,

    --- Called when an input value changes.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Define the script's data and inputs.
    --- type MyNode = {}
    ---
    --- -- Called when any input value changes.
    --- function update(self: MyNode)
    ---   print('An script input value has changed.')
    --- end
    ---
    --- -- Return a factory function that Rive uses to build the Node instance.
    --- return function(): Node<MyNode>
    ---   return {
    ---     update = update,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    update: (self: T) -> ()?,

    --- Called to render the node using the provided `Renderer`.
    ---
    --- For a more complete example using draw, see Instantiating Components.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Define the script's data and inputs.
    --- type MyNode = {}
    ---
    --- -- Called every frame (after advance) to render the content.
    --- function draw(self: MyNode, renderer: Renderer) end
    ---
    --- -- Return a factory function that Rive uses to build the Node instance.
    --- return function(): Node<MyNode>
    ---   return {
    ---     draw = draw,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    --- GPU canvas work (canvas:beginFrame, gpuCanvas:beginRenderPass) also
    --- happens here, in any order; replay schedules canvas dependencies. The
    --- former drawCanvas callback was removed: move its body into draw.
    draw: ((self: T, renderer: Renderer) -> ())?,

    --- Pointer event down handler.
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerDown(self: MyGame, event: PointerEvent)
    ---   print('Pointer Position: ', event.position.x, event.position.y)
    ---
    ---   event:hit()
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<MyGame>
    ---     return {
    ---         init = init,
    ---         advance = advance,
    ---         draw = draw,
    ---         pointerDown = handlePointerDown,
    ---     }
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerDown: (self: T, event:PointerEvent) -> ()?,

    --- Pointer event move handler.
    ---
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerMove(self: MyGame, event: PointerEvent)
    ---   print('Pointer Position: ', event.position.x, event.position.y)
    ---
    ---   event:hit()
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<MyGame>
    ---     return {
    ---         init = init,
    ---         advance = advance,
    ---         draw = draw,
    ---         pointerMove = handlePointerMove,
    ---     }
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerMove: (self: T, event:PointerEvent) -> ()?,

    --- Pointer event up handler.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerUp(self: MyGame, event: PointerEvent)
    ---   print('Pointer Position: ', event.position.x, event.position.y)
    ---
    ---   event:hit()
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<MyGame>
    ---     return {
    ---         init = init,
    ---         advance = advance,
    ---         draw = draw,
    ---         pointerUp = handlePointerUp,
    ---     }
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerUp: (self: T, event:PointerEvent) -> ()?,

    --- Pointer event exit handler.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerExit(self: MyGame, event: PointerEvent)
    ---   print('Pointer Position: ', event.position.x, event.position.y)
    ---
    ---   event:hit()
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<MyGame>
    ---     return {
    ---         init = init,
    ---         advance = advance,
    ---         draw = draw,
    ---         pointerExit = handlePointerExit,
    ---     }
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerExit: (self: T, event:PointerEvent) -> ()?,

    --- Mouse wheel and trackpad scroll handler. Call `event:hit()` to claim
    --- the scroll; otherwise it passes to whatever lies behind, such as a
    --- `ScrollConstraint` view.
    --- ```lua
    --- function handlePointerScroll(self: MyZoomView, event: ScrollEvent)
    ---   self.zoom *= math.exp(-event.delta.y * 0.01)
    ---   event:hit()
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): Node<MyZoomView>
    ---     return {
    ---         init = init,
    ---         draw = draw,
    ---         pointerScroll = handlePointerScroll,
    ---     }
    --- end
    --- ```
    pointerScroll: (self: T, event:ScrollEvent) -> ()?,

    gamepadConnected: (self: T, event:GamepadConnected) -> ()?,
    gamepadEvent: (self: T, event:GamepadEvent) -> ()?,
    gamepadDisconnected: (self: T, event:GamepadDisconnected) -> ()?,
} & T

--- A scripted converter used for transforming values between ViewModel data
--- bindings and Rive properties.
---
--- Type parameters:
---   T: The converter type
---   I: The input type, must be a DataValue type
---      (DataValueNumber, DataValueString, DataValueBoolean, DataValueColor, etc)
---   O: The output type, must be a DataValue type
---      (DataValueNumber, DataValueString, DataValueBoolean, DataValueColor, etc)
---
--- For more information, see Converter Scripts.
export type Converter<T, I, O> = {

    --- Called once when the converter is created. Returns true if initialization
    --- succeeds.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Called once when the script initializes.
    --- function init(self: MyConverter, context: Context): boolean
    ---
    ---     -- Return false to stop the script.
    ---     return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    init: ((self: T, context: Context) -> boolean)?,

    --- Converts the input value (a view model property) to an output value.
    --- The input parameter must be a DataValue type.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Converts the value when binding from source to target.
    --- function convert(self: MyConverter, input: DataInputs): DataOutput
    ---
    ---   local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
    ---   if input:isNumber() then
    ---     -- Example: Add 1 to the incoming number
    ---     dv.value = (input :: DataValueNumber).value + 1
    ---   end
    ---   return dv
    --- end
    --- ```
    convert: (self: T, input: I) -> O,

    --- Converts the output value back to an input value (a view model property).
    --- The input parameter must be a DataValue type.
    --- ```lua
    --- function reverseConvert(
    ---   self: MyConverter,
    ---   input: DataOutput
    --- ): DataInputs
    ---   local dv: DataValueNumber = DataValue.number()
    ---   if input:isNumber() then
    ---     -- Example: Subract 1 from the target number
    ---     dv.value = (input :: DataValueNumber).value - 1
    ---   end
    ---   return dv
    --- end
    --- ```
    reverseConvert: (self: T, input: O) -> I,

    --- Optional per-frame update. Returns true if the converter should continue
    --- receiving advance calls.
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: MyConverter, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   return false
    --- end
    --- ```
    advance: ((self: T, seconds: number) -> boolean)?,
} & T

--- A scripted Layout which can function just like a `Node` but
--- also has the ability to fit into a layout box provided via
--- resize. It can also be intrinsically sized allowing hosting
--- layouts to attempt to fit to its size by using the measure
--- function to report desired dimensions.
---
--- For more information, see Layout Scripts.
export type Layout<T> = Node<T> & {

    --- When provided this Layout can be intrinsically sized/request
    --- to be a specific size. This is not guaranteed as the layout
    --- may have min/max dimensions. Resize will be called with the
    --- granted size after being measured.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Measure the computed size of the layout on resize
    --- function measure(self: MyLayout): Vector
    ---   return Vector.xy(100, 100)
    --- end
    --- ```
    measure: ((self: T) -> Vector) | nil,

    --- When provided, called to set the initial size and again whenever
    --- the size changes. Layouts that do not react to their box may omit
    --- it; the runtime no-ops when it is not implemented.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Called when the layout resizes based on the content
    --- -- This only applies to Layouts with a fit type of Hug
    --- -- scale is the presenting surface's device pixels per point.
    --- function resize(self: MyLayout, size: Vector, scale: number)
    ---   print('Resize:', size, scale)
    --- end
    --- ```
    resize: ((self: T, size: Vector, scale: number) -> ()) | nil,
} & T

--- Represents a typed input value.
--- ```lua
--- -- Define the script's data and inputs.
--- type MyNode = {
---   speed: Input<number>,
---   title: Input<string>,
---   enabled: Input<boolean>,
---   onReset: Input<Trigger>,
--- }
---
--- -- Return a factory function that Rive uses to build the Node instance.
--- return function(): Node<MyNode>
---   return {
---     speed = 1,
---     title = 'Rive so coooool!',
---     enabled = false,
---     onReset = function() end,
---   }
--- end
--- ```
export type Input<T> = T

--- Represents a typed output value.
---
--- (Coming soon)
export type Output<T> = T

--- A function that triggers an action when invoked.
--- ```lua
--- -- Define the script's data and inputs.
--- type MyNode = {
---   onReset: Input<Trigger>,
--- }
---
--- -- Return a factory function that Rive uses to build the Node instance.
--- return function(): Node<MyNode>
---   return {
---     onReset = function() end,
---   }
--- end
--- ```
export type Trigger = (any)->()

--- A scripted effect applied to a path
--- For effects that can change over time, even
--- when the path does not change, markNeedsUpdate()
--- should be called on its context in the advance function
---
--- For more information, see Path Effect Scripts.
export type PathEffect<T> = {

    --- Called once when the effect is created or attached.
    --- Return `true` to keep the effect active, or `false` to disable it.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Called once when the script initializes.
    --- function init(self: MyPathEffect, context: Context): boolean
    ---
    ---     -- Return false to stop the script.
    ---     return true
    --- end
    --- ```
    init: ((self: T, context: Context) -> boolean)?,

    --- Called any time an input changes or an update is requested.
    --- You receive the original `PathData` and the node it belongs to, and
    --- must return the path that should be used for rendering.
    --- ```lua
    --- function update(self: MyPathEffect, inPath: PathData, node: NodeReadData): PathData
    ---     local path = Path.new()
    ---     return path
    --- end
    --- ```
    update: (self: T, path: PathData, node: NodeReadData) -> PathData,

    --- Called every frame to advance the effect over time.
    --- `seconds` is the time delta since the last frame.
    --- Return `true` to keep the effect active, or `false` to disable it.
    --- ```lua
    --- function advance(self: MyPathEffect, seconds: number): boolean
    ---   return false
    --- end
    --- ```
    advance: ((self: T, seconds: number) -> boolean)?,
} & T

--- An action performed when an associated State Machine Listener is triggered.
---
--- For more information, see Listener Action Scripts.
export type ListenerAction<T> = {

    --- Called once when the listener is created or attached.
    --- ```lua
    --- type MyListenerAction = {}
    ---
    --- -- Called once when the script initializes.
    --- function init(self: MyListenerAction, context: Context): boolean
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function perform(self: MyListenerAction, pointerEvent: PointerEvent) end
    ---
    --- return function(): ListenerAction<MyListenerAction>
    ---   return {
    ---     init = init,
    ---     perform = perform,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    init: ((self: T, context: Context) -> boolean)?,

    --- Called when the associated State Machine Listener is triggered.
    --- This method includes a `PointerEvent` parameter containing details about the triggering interaction.
    ---
    --- **Deprecated.** Prefer `performAction` with `ListenerContext`; this overload may be removed.
    --- ```lua
    --- type MyListenerAction = {}
    ---
    --- function init(self: MyListenerAction, context: Context): boolean
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- -- Add your transition logic here.
    --- function perform(self: MyListenerAction, pointerEvent: PointerEvent)
    ---   -- perform action here
    --- end
    ---
    --- -- Return a factory function that Rive uses to build the Listener Action instance.
    --- return function(): ListenerAction<MyListenerAction>
    ---   return {
    ---     init = init,
    ---     perform = perform,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    perform: ((self: T, pointerEvent: PointerEvent) -> ())?,

    --- Called when the associated State Machine Listener is triggered.
    --- This method includes a `ListenerContext` parameter containing details about the triggering interaction.
    --- ```lua
    --- type MyListenerAction = {}
    ---
    --- function init(self: MyListenerAction, context: Context): boolean
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- -- Called each time the listener fires.
    --- function performAction(self: MyListenerAction, listenerContext: ListenerContext)
    ---   if listenerContext:isPointerEvent() then
    ---     print('clicked')
    ---   end
    --- end
    ---
    --- -- Return a factory function that Rive uses to build the Listener Action instance.
    --- return function(): ListenerAction<MyListenerAction>
    ---   return {
    ---     init = init,
    ---     performAction = performAction,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    performAction: ((self: T, listenerContext: ListenerContext) -> ())?,

} & T

--- A condition to evaluate for a transition between state machine states to be taken.
---
--- For more information, see Transition Condition Scripts.
export type TransitionCondition<T> = {

    --- Called once when the transition condition is created or attached.
    --- ```lua
    --- type MyTransitionCondition = {}
    ---
    --- -- Called once when the script initializes.
    --- function init(self: MyTransitionCondition, context: Context): boolean
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- function evaluate(self: MyTransitionCondition): boolean
    ---   return false
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): TransitionCondition<MyTransitionCondition>
    ---   return {
    ---     init = init,
    ---     evaluate = evaluate,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    init: ((self: T, context: Context) -> boolean)?,

    --- Called every frame while the transition is active.
    --- ```lua
    --- type MyTransitionCondition = {}
    ---
    --- function init(self: MyTransitionCondition, context: Context): boolean
    ---   return true
    --- end
    ---
    --- -- Add your transition logic here.
    --- -- `evaluate` is fired every frame while the transition is active.
    --- -- Returning false prevents a transition, true allows a transition.
    --- function evaluate(self: MyTransitionCondition): boolean
    ---   return false
    --- end
    ---
    --- return function(): TransitionCondition<MyTransitionCondition>
    ---   return {
    ---     init = init,
    ---     evaluate = evaluate,
    ---   }
    --- end
    --- ```
    evaluate: (self: T) -> boolean,

} & T
--- An interpolator: eases keyframes, state transitions, layout animations and
--- interpolating data converters.
---
--- Rive creates an instance per owner instance: each playing animation gets one
--- per keyframe, each state machine one per interpolator its transitions use,
--- each artboard one per interpolator its layout styles use, and each bound
--- converter its own. Transitions or layout styles that use the same
--- interpolator share its instance, as do layouts that inherit their animation
--- from a parent layout (including nested artboards and list items).
---
--- So `transform` and `transformValue` can be called many times per frame, by
--- several layouts, in any order. Compute the result from `value` (and `from`
--- and `to`), the inputs and whatever `init` set up; don't keep progress in
--- `self` between calls.
export type Interpolator<T> = {

    init: ((self: T, context: Context) -> boolean)?,

    --- Maps a linear progress `value` in 0..1 to an eased one.
    transform: (self: T, value: number) -> number,
    --- Returns the value between `from` and `to` at linear progress `value`.
    transformValue: (self: T, from: number, to: number, value: number) -> number,

} & T

--- A handle to one child (a nested artboard) of a Transition, valid only for
--- the duration of the `draw` (and `changed`) call it is passed to. Draw it
--- with `child:draw(renderer)`, wrapping the call in renderer state
--- (save / modulateOpacity / transform / clipPath / restore) to author the
--- transition effect.
export type TransitionChild = {
    --- Draw this child's content at the renderer's current transform.
    draw: (self: TransitionChild, renderer: Renderer) -> (),
    --- The child artboard's natural width, useful for slide/scale math.
    width: number,
    --- The child artboard's natural height.
    height: number,
}

--- Renders the visual change between an outgoing ("from") and incoming ("to")
--- child when a Transition's active child changes. The active child is chosen
--- natively (and is data-bindable, Solo-style); the script owns only how the
--- two children are composited. Declare any inputs you need (e.g. a director
--- Artboard, numbers, curves) as ordinary script inputs and drive the effect
--- however you like.
---
--- For more information, see Transition Scripts.
export type Transition<T> = {

    --- Called once when the transition is created.
    init: ((self: T, context: Context) -> boolean)?,

    --- Called when the active child changes. `from` is the outgoing child
    --- (nil on the first show); `to` is the incoming child. `direction` is 1
    --- when `to` is at a higher combined index than `from`, -1 when lower, and
    --- 0 when unknown (e.g. the first show). Reset your progress clock / seek
    --- any input you drive here. Called again on interruption, where `from` is
    --- the previously-incoming child.
    changed: ((self: T, from: TransitionChild?, to: TransitionChild?, direction: number) -> ())?,

    --- Called every frame while a transition is in flight. Advance your own
    --- progress (and any input you drive). Return true while running; return
    --- false to signal completion, after which the runtime retires the
    --- outgoing child and resumes drawing the active child normally.
    advance: (self: T, seconds: number) -> boolean,

    --- When false, the incoming ("to") child renders normally through the
    --- artboard draw loop and is passed as nil to draw; the script composites
    --- only the outgoing ("from") child (useful for "reveal" transitions where
    --- the new content is already on-stage). Defaults to true (the script
    --- composites both children). Read at the start of each transition, so it
    --- may be set in init or changed.
    managesTo: boolean?,

    --- Composite the two children. Wrap each `child:draw(renderer)` in renderer
    --- state (save / modulateOpacity / transform / clipPath / restore) to
    --- author crossfade, slide, wipe, scale, and custom effects. Either child
    --- may be nil (see `managesTo`).
    draw: (self: T, renderer: Renderer, from: TransitionChild?, to: TransitionChild?) -> (),

} & T
```

```luau
--- Represents a 2D transformation matrix with components for scaling,
--- rotation, shear, and translation.
--- ```lua
--- -- Construct a matrix manually
--- local m = Mat2D.identity()
---
--- m.xx = 2    -- scale x
--- m.yy = 3    -- scale y
--- m.tx = 50   -- translate x
--- m.ty = 100  -- translate y
---
--- local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 20)
---
--- -- (10,20) → (20,60) → (70,160)
--- print(r.x, r.y) -- 70, 160
--- ```
declare extern type Mat2D with

    --- The xx component of the matrix.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat2D.identity()
    ---
    --- -- Double horizontal scale
    --- m.xx = 2
    ---
    --- local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 5)
    --- print(r.x, r.y) -- 20, 5
    --- ```
    xx: number

    --- The xy component of the matrix, the vertical skew.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat2D.identity()
    ---
    --- -- Add vertical skew
    --- m.xy = 1
    ---
    --- local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 5)
    --- -- y = 5 + (1 * 10)
    --- print(r.x, r.y) -- 10, 15
    --- ```
    xy: number

    --- The yx component of the matrix, the horizontal skew.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat2D.identity()
    ---
    --- -- Add horizontal skew
    --- m.yx = 1
    ---
    --- local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 5)
    --- -- x = 10 + (1 * 5)
    --- print(r.x, r.y) -- 15, 5
    --- ```
    yx: number

    --- The yy component of the matrix.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat2D.identity()
    ---
    --- -- Triple vertical scale
    --- m.yy = 3
    ---
    --- local r = m * Vector.xy(4, 5)
    --- print(r.x, r.y) -- 4, 15
    --- ```
    yy: number

    --- Translation along the x-axis.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat2D.identity()
    ---
    --- m.tx = 50
    ---
    --- local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 20)
    --- print(r.x, r.y) -- 60, 20
    --- ```
    tx: number

    --- Translation along the y-axis.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat2D.identity()
    ---
    --- m.ty = 100
    ---
    --- local r = m * Vector.xy(10, 20)
    --- print(r.x, r.y) -- 10, 120
    --- ```
    ty: number

    --- Provides indexed access to the matrix components.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat2D.identity()
    ---
    --- -- Indices map to: xx, xy, yx, yy, tx, ty
    --- m[1] = 2    -- xx
    --- m[5] = 50   -- tx
    ---
    --- print(m[1], m.xx) -- 2, 2
    --- print(m[5], m.tx) -- 50, 50
    --- ```
    [number]: number

    --- Returns the inverse of the matrix, or nil if the matrix is not invertible.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(50, 100)
    --- local inv = m:invert()
    ---
    --- if inv then
    ---   local p = Vector.xy(10, 20)
    ---   local result = inv * (m * p)
    ---   print(result.x, result.y) -- 10, 20
    --- end
    --- ```
    function invert(self): Mat2D?

    --- Returns true if the matrix is the identity transform.
    --- ```lua
    --- local newMat = Mat2D.identity()
    --- print(newMat:isIdentity())
    --- ```
    function isIdentity(self): boolean

    --- Returns true if all components of the two matrices are equal.
    --- ```lua
    --- local a = Mat2D.values(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)
    --- local b = Mat2D.identity()
    ---
    --- print(a == b) -- true
    --- ```
    function __eq(self, rhs: Mat2D): boolean

    --- Transforms the given `Vector` by the matrix and returns the result.
    --- ```lua
    --- local translation = Mat2D.values(1, 0, 0, 1, 50, 100)
    --- local point = Vector.xy(10, 20)
    ---
    --- -- Multiply matrix by vector
    --- local result = translation * point
    ---
    --- print(result.x, result.y) -- 60, 120
    --- ```
    function __mul(self, rhs: Vector): Vector

    --- Returns the matrix product of this matrix and the given matrix
    --- ```lua
    --- local translation = Mat2D.values(1, 0, 0, 1, 50, 100)
    --- local scale = Mat2D.values(2, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0)
    ---
    --- -- Combine transforms
    --- local combined = translation * scale
    ---
    --- local point = Vector.xy(10, 20)
    --- local result = combined * point
    ---
    --- print(result.x, result.y) -- 70, 140
    --- ```
    function __mul(self, rhs: Mat2D): Mat2D
end

declare Mat2D: {

    --- Creates a matrix using the specified components.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- xx=1, xy=skewY (vertical skew), yx=skewX (horizontal skew), yy=1, tx=0, ty=0
    --- local newMat = Mat2D.values(1, self.skewY, self.skewX, 1, 0, 0)

    --- Returns the identity matrix.

    --- local newMat = Mat2D.identity()

    --- Creates a translation matrix from the given x and y values or from a

    --- local t2 = Mat2D.withTranslation(pos)

    withTranslation: @checked ((x: number, y: number) -> Mat2D) & ((pos: Vector) -> Mat2D),

    --- Creates a rotation matrix from the given angle in radians.
    --- ```lua
    --- local rot = Mat2D.withRotation(math.rad(90))
    --- local r = rot * Vector.xy(1, 0)
    ---
    --- print(math.floor(r.x + 0.5), math.floor(r.y + 0.5)) -- 0, 1
    --- ```
    withRotation: @checked (radians: number) -> Mat2D,

    --- Creates a scale matrix from the given x and y values or from a `Vector`.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Uniform scale (y defaults to x if omitted)
    --- local s1 = Mat2D.withScale(2)
    ---
    --- -- Non-uniform scale
    --- local s2 = Mat2D.withScale(2, 3)
    ---
    --- -- From a Vector
    --- local scale = Vector.xy(2, 3)
    --- local s3 = Mat2D.withScale(scale)
    --- ```
    withScale: @checked ((x: number, y: number?) -> Mat2D) & ((scale: Vector) -> Mat2D),

    --- Creates a scale-and-translation matrix from numeric values or vectors.
    --- ```lua
    --- -- Numbers Overloaded
    ---
    --- -- Scale by (2, 3) then translate by (50, 100)
    --- local st = Mat2D.withScaleAndTranslation(2, 3, 50, 100)
    ---
    --- local p = Vector.xy(10, 20)
    --- local r = st * p
    ---
    --- -- (10,20) -> scaled (20,60) -> translated (70,160)
    --- print(r.x, r.y) -- 70, 160
    ---
    --- -- Vectors Overloaded
    ---
    --- local st = Mat2D.withScaleAndTranslation(
    ---   Vector.xy(2, 3),      -- scale
    ---   Vector.xy(50, 100)    -- position / translation
    --- )
    ---
    --- local r = st * Vector.xy(10, 20)
    --- print(r.x, r.y) -- 70, 160
    --- ```
    withScaleAndTranslation: @checked ((xs: number, ys: number, x: number, y: number) -> Mat2D)
        & ((scale: Vector, position: Vector) -> Mat2D),

    --- Writes the inverse of 'input' into 'output'. Returns true if the input
    --- matrix is invertible.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat2D.withTranslation(50, 100)
    ---
    --- local inv = Mat2D.identity()
    --- local ok = Mat2D.invert(inv, m)
    --- print(ok) -- true
    ---
    --- local p = Vector.xy(10, 20)
    --- local r = inv * (m * p)
    ---
    --- -- Applying m then inv returns the original point
    --- print(r.x, r.y) -- 10, 20
    --- ```
    invert: @checked (output: Mat2D, input: Mat2D) -> boolean,
}
```

```luau
--- Represents a 4x4 column-major transformation matrix, suitable for 3D
--- transforms and direct upload to a GPU uniform buffer.
--- ```lua
--- -- Construct an MVP matrix
--- local proj = Mat4.perspective(math.rad(60), 16 / 9, 0.1, 100)
--- local view = Mat4.fromTranslation(0, 0, -3) -- camera 3 units back
--- local model = Mat4.fromRotationY(angle)
--- local mvp = proj * view * model
---
--- -- Upload to a uniform buffer (64 bytes, column-major)
--- mvp:writeToBuffer(uboBytes, 0)
--- ```
declare extern type Mat4 with

    --- Element at row R, column C (1-indexed). For example `m.m12` is the
    --- entry in row 1, column 2.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat4.identity()
    --- m.m11 = 2 -- scale x
    --- m.m22 = 3 -- scale y
    --- m.m14 = 50 -- translate x
    --- ```
    m11: number
    m12: number
    m13: number
    m14: number
    m21: number
    m22: number
    m23: number
    m24: number
    m31: number
    m32: number
    m33: number
    m34: number
    m41: number
    m42: number
    m43: number
    m44: number

    --- Linear column-major access. Indices 1..4 are column 0, 5..8 are
    --- column 1, 9..12 are column 2, 13..16 are column 3 (translation).
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat4.identity()
    --- m[13] = 50 -- translate x
    --- m[14] = 100 -- translate y
    --- m[15] = 25 -- translate z
    --- ```
    [number]: number

    --- Returns the inverse of the matrix, or `nil` if the matrix is singular.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat4.fromTranslation(50, 100, 25)
    --- local inv = m:invert()
    --- ```
    function invert(self): Mat4?

    --- Returns the transpose of the matrix.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat4.fromRotationY(math.rad(45))
    --- local t = m:transpose()
    --- ```
    function transpose(self): Mat4

    --- Transforms the given 3D point by the matrix (treating w = 1) and
    --- returns the result as a `Vector`. If the homogeneous w of the result
    --- is non-unit (e.g. after a perspective matrix), the returned point is
    --- divided through.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat4.fromTranslation(10, 20, 30)
    --- local p = m:transformPoint(1, 2, 3)
    --- print(p.x, p.y, p.z) -- 11, 22, 33
    --- ```
    function transformPoint(self, x: number, y: number, z: number): Vector

    --- Transforms the given homogeneous 4D vector by the matrix and returns
    --- the four components as multiple values, without perspective divide.
    --- Use this when the caller needs to inspect or carry the homogeneous
    --- `w` (e.g. clip-space coordinates).
    --- ```lua
    --- local mvp = proj * view * model
    --- local x, y, z, w = mvp:transformVec4(px, py, pz, 1)
    --- ```
    function transformVec4(
        self, x: number, y: number, z: number, w: number): (number, number, number, number)

    --- Writes the matrix as 64 bytes (column-major, 16 float32 entries) into
    --- the given buffer at `byteOffset`. The buffer must have at least 64
    --- bytes available from the offset.
    --- ```lua
    --- local mvp = Mat4.identity()
    --- local ubo = buffer.create(64)
    --- mvp:writeToBuffer(ubo, 0)
    --- ```
    function writeToBuffer(self, buf: buffer, byteOffset: number): ()

    --- Returns true if all 16 components of the two matrices are equal.
    function __eq(self, rhs: Mat4): boolean

    --- Returns the matrix product of two matrices. Useful for composing
    --- transforms, e.g. `proj * view * model`. Allocates a new `Mat4`; in
    --- tight loops prefer `Mat4.multiply(out, a, b)` to reuse storage.
    function __mul(self, rhs: Mat4): Mat4

    --- Closed-form inverse for affine matrices (bottom row [0, 0, 0, 1] —
    --- any composition of `fromTranslation`/`fromScale`/`fromRotationX/Y/Z`
    --- qualifies). Returns nil if the linear part is singular. Faster than
    --- `:invert()` and avoids the full 4x4 cofactor work.
    --- ```lua
    --- local m = Mat4.fromTranslation(3, -4, 5) * Mat4.fromRotationY(0.4)
    --- local inv = m:invertAffine()
    --- ```
    function invertAffine(self): Mat4?
end

declare Mat4: {

    --- Returns the 4x4 identity matrix.
    identity: @checked () -> Mat4,

    --- Creates a matrix from 16 components, supplied column-major (column 0
    --- first: c0x, c0y, c0z, c0w, c1x, ...).
    values: @checked (
        c0x: number, c0y: number, c0z: number, c0w: number,
        c1x: number, c1y: number, c1z: number, c1w: number,
        c2x: number, c2y: number, c2z: number, c2w: number,
        c3x: number, c3y: number, c3z: number, c3w: number) -> Mat4,

    --- Creates a translation matrix.
    --- ```lua
    --- local t = Mat4.fromTranslation(10, 20, 30)
    --- ```
    fromTranslation: @checked (x: number, y: number, z: number) -> Mat4,

    --- Creates a scale matrix. If `y` and `z` are omitted, uniform scaling
    --- by `x` is applied to all axes.
    --- ```lua
    --- local s1 = Mat4.fromScale(2)        -- uniform 2x
    --- local s2 = Mat4.fromScale(1, 2, 1)  -- 2x in Y only
    --- ```
    fromScale: @checked (x: number, y: number?, z: number?) -> Mat4,

    --- Creates a rotation matrix around the X axis (radians).
    fromRotationX: @checked (radians: number) -> Mat4,

    --- Creates a rotation matrix around the Y axis (radians).
    fromRotationY: @checked (radians: number) -> Mat4,

    --- Creates a rotation matrix around the Z axis (radians).
    fromRotationZ: @checked (radians: number) -> Mat4,

    --- Creates a right-handed perspective projection matrix that maps z to
    --- the [0, 1] NDC depth range. `fovY` is in radians; `near` and `far`
    --- are positive distances.
    --- ```lua
    --- local proj = Mat4.perspective(math.rad(60), 16 / 9, 0.1, 100)
    --- ```
    perspective: @checked (fovY: number, aspect: number, near: number, far: number) -> Mat4,

    --- Right-handed perspective with reverse-Z (near -> 1, far -> 0) and an
    --- infinite far plane. Combined with a float depth buffer this gives a
    --- near-uniform 1/z depth distribution across the entire frustum — the
    --- best precision an arbitrary scene can achieve. The depth buffer must
    --- be cleared to 0 (not 1) and the depth test flipped to GREATER.
    --- ```lua
    --- local proj = Mat4.perspectiveReverseZ(math.rad(60), 16 / 9, 0.1)
    --- ```
    perspectiveReverseZ: @checked (fovY: number, aspect: number, near: number) -> Mat4,

    --- Creates a right-handed view matrix looking from `eye` toward
    --- `center` (GLM convention). `up` need not be normalized.
    --- ```lua
    --- local view = Mat4.lookAt(Vector.xyz(0, 2, 5), Vector.origin(), Vector.xyz(0, 1, 0))
    --- ```
    lookAt: @checked (eye: Vector, center: Vector, up: Vector) -> Mat4,

    --- Creates a right-handed orthographic projection matrix that maps z to
    --- the [0, 1] NDC depth range (matching `Mat4.perspective`), e.g. for
    --- shadow-map cascades or 2D overlays.
    --- ```lua
    --- local proj = Mat4.ortho(-10, 10, -10, 10, 0.1, 100)
    --- ```
    ortho: @checked (left: number, right: number, bottom: number, top: number, near: number, far: number) -> Mat4,

    --- Writes `a * b` into `output`, reusing its storage. Returns `output`.
    --- Use this in tight loops to avoid allocating a new `Mat4` per
    --- multiplication. `output` may alias `a` or `b`.
    --- ```lua
    --- local out = Mat4.identity()
    --- for i = 1, 1000 do Mat4.multiply(out, view, model) end
    --- ```
    multiply: @checked (output: Mat4, a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4,

    --- Like `Mat4.multiply`, but assumes both inputs are affine (bottom row
    --- [0, 0, 0, 1] — any composition of translation/scale/rotation matrices
    --- qualifies). Skips the bottom-row work for ~25% fewer FLOPs per
    --- multiplication. The result is always affine. Caller must ensure both
    --- inputs are affine; passing a non-affine input gives an incorrect
    --- result.
    --- ```lua
    --- local world = Mat4.identity()
    --- for _, bone in ipairs(bones) do
    ---     Mat4.multiplyAffine(world, parent, bone.local)
    --- end
    --- ```
    multiplyAffine: @checked (output: Mat4, a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4,

    --- Writes the inverse of `input` into `output`, returning true on
    --- success or false if `input` is singular.
    --- ```lua
    --- local inv = Mat4.identity()
    --- local ok = Mat4.invert(inv, m)
    --- ```
    invert: @checked (output: Mat4, input: Mat4) -> boolean,

    --- Writes the affine inverse of `input` into `output`. See
    --- `Mat4:invertAffine` for the contract; faster than `Mat4.invert`.
    invertAffine: @checked (output: Mat4, input: Mat4) -> boolean,
}
```

## TOPIC: luau/api/net

# Net

```luau
--- The response to a `fetch` request.
declare extern type Response with
    --- HTTP status code, e.g. 200 or 404.
    status: number

    --- The standard reason phrase for `status`, e.g. "Not Found".
    statusText: string

    --- True when `status` is in the 200-299 range.
    ok: boolean

    --- The final URL, after any redirects.
    url: string

    --- Response headers keyed by lower-case name. Repeated headers are
    --- joined with ", ".
    headers: { [string]: string }

    --- Resolves with the body as a string.
    function text(self): Promise<string>

    --- Resolves with the body as a new buffer.
    function arrayBuffer(self): Promise<buffer>

    --- One header by case-insensitive name, or nil when it is absent.
    function header(self, name: string): string?
end

--- Options for `fetch`.
export type FetchOptions = {
    --- HTTP method: GET (the default), HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or
    --- OPTIONS.
    method: string?,
    --- Request headers. Cookie, Host, Origin, Referer, Sec-* and Proxy-*
    --- cannot be set.
    headers: { [string]: string }?,
    --- Request body. Not allowed with GET or HEAD.
    body: (string | buffer)?,
    --- Milliseconds before the request fails with "timeout". Defaults to
    --- 30000 and is capped at 60000.
    timeout: number?,
}

--- Requests an https: URL on a public host and resolves with its
--- `Response`. Requests never carry cookies or stored credentials, and the
--- host decides whether scripts may use the network at all.
---
--- Failures reject with a string "<code>: <message>", where code is one of
--- disabled, policy, rateLimited, timeout, aborted, tooLarge or network.
--- ```lua
--- async(function()
---     local ok, result = await(fetch("https://example.com/"))
---     if ok then
---         local _, body = await(result:text())
---         print(result.status, #body)
---     else
---         print("fetch failed:", result)
---     end
---     return nil
--- end)
--- ```
declare function fetch(url: string, options: FetchOptions?): Promise<Response>
```

--- path:lineTo(Vector.xy(10, 0))

--- end
--- -- 1 moveTo
--- -- 2 lineTo

export type CommandType =
    'none'
    | 'moveTo'
    | 'lineTo'
    | 'cubicTo'
    | 'quadTo'
    | 'close'

--- Each command has a type, and a variable number of points depending on that type.

    --- ```lua

    ---   print(i, command.type)
    --- end
    --- -- 1 moveTo
    --- -- 2 lineTo

    --- - `moveTo`: 1 point
    --- - `lineTo`: 1 point
    --- - `quadTo`: 2 points
    --- - `cubicTo`: 3 points
    --- - `close`: 0 points

    --- path:moveTo(Vector.xy(0, 0))
    --- path:cubicTo(
    ---   Vector.xy(25, -40),
    ---   Vector.xy(75, 40),
    ---   Vector.xy(100, 0)
    --- )
    ---

    --- print(command.type)      -- cubicTo
    --- print(#command)          -- 3
    --- ```
    [index]: Vector

    --- Returns the number of points stored on this command.

    --- local count = #command
    --- ```

end

--- Both Path and PathData behave like arrays of commands and support iteration via ipairs.

    --- Each entry is a `PathCommand` describing one segment or action in the path.

## TOPIC: luau/api/promise

# Promises

<!-- GENERATED by docsgen/gen_luau_api.py from
     scripting_workspace/src/tools/builtins -- do not edit -->

Declares: `Promise`, `async`, `await`

```luau
--- A value that will be available in the future.
--- Use `andThen` to register callbacks, or `await` inside `async` to
--- suspend until the value is ready.
--- Supports cancellation: call `cancel()` to abort pending work and
--- propagate cancellation to chained promises.
export type Promise<T> = {
    --- Register a callback for when the promise fulfills.
    --- The handler may return a value that becomes the next promise's result.
    andThen: ((self: Promise<T>, onFulfilled: (value: T) -> any) -> any)
           & ((self: Promise<T>, onFulfilled: (value: T) -> any, onRejected: (error: any) -> any) -> any),
    --- Register a callback for when the promise rejects.
    --- Errors can be any Lua value (string, table, number, etc.).
    catch: (self: Promise<T>, onRejected: (error: any) -> any) -> any,
    --- Register a callback that runs whether the promise fulfills or rejects.
    finally: (self: Promise<T>, onFinally: () -> ()) -> Promise<T>,
    --- Cancel this promise. Fires the onCancel hook (if registered),
    --- propagates cancellation down to chained promises, and propagates
    --- up to the parent if all its consumers are cancelled.
    --- No-op if the promise is already settled.
    cancel: (self: Promise<T>) -> Promise<T>,
    --- Register a cancellation hook that fires when cancel() is called.
    --- Used to clean up in-flight work (e.g. abort a network request).
    --- Replaces any hook registered before.
    onCancel: (self: Promise<T>, hook: () -> ()) -> Promise<T>,
    --- Returns the current state: "Pending", "Fulfilled", "Rejected", or "Cancelled".
    getStatus: (self: Promise<T>) -> string,
}

--- Static methods on the `Promise` global.
declare Promise: {
    --- Create a new promise with an executor function.
    --- The executor receives resolve, reject, and onCancel callbacks.
    new: <T>(executor: (resolve: (value: T) -> (), reject: (error: any) -> (), onCancel: (hook: () -> ()) -> ()) -> ()) -> Promise<T>,
    --- Create an already-resolved promise. Resolves with nil if no value given.
    resolve: <T>(value: T?) -> Promise<T>,
    --- Create an already-rejected promise. Error can be any Lua value.
    --- Rejects with "rejected" if no argument is provided.
    reject: <T>(error: any?) -> Promise<T>,
    --- Wait for all promises to resolve; rejects if any rejects.
    --- On rejection, the remaining promises that nothing else waits on are
    --- cancelled.
    all: <T>(promises: {Promise<T>}) -> Promise<{T}>,
}

--- Wrap a function in a coroutine and return a Promise that resolves
--- when the function returns (or rejects if it errors).
declare function async<T>(fn: () -> T): Promise<T>

--- Suspend the current `async` coroutine until the promise settles.
--- Returns (true, value) on fulfillment, (false, error) on rejection.
--- Never throws.
declare function await<T>(promise: Promise<T>): (boolean, T)
```

    ---   myImage: Image?,
    ---   sampler: ImageSampler?,

    ---

    ---   self.sampler = ImageSampler('clamp', 'clamp', 'bilinear')

    ---   return true

    --- function draw(self: DrawImage, renderer: Renderer)

    ---     myImage = nil,
    ---     sampler = nil,
    ---     init = init,
    ---     draw = draw,
    ---   }
    --- end

    --- coordinates, and triangle indices.
    ---
    --- Check out Scripting demos to see a working example.

    --- function draw(self: DrawImageMesh, renderer: Renderer)
    ---   if self.myImage and self.sampler and self.vertices and self.uvs and self.triangles then
    ---     renderer:drawImageMesh(
    ---       self.myImage,

    ---       self.uvs,
    ---       self.triangles,

    ---     )

    --- end
    --- ```

    --- The blend mode is always `srcOver`. Opacity and the UV transform come
    --- from each instance.

    --- function draw(self: DrawImageMeshInstanced, renderer: Renderer)

    ---     local h: number = self.myImage.height
    ---     local rx: number = (w / 2) * self.clipRadiusX
    ---     local ry: number = (h / 2) * self.clipRadiusY

    ---     enemy.artboard:draw(renderer)

--- Represents an expectation used within a test case. Each method performs an
--- assertion comparing the supplied value to the expected one.
export type Expectation = {

    --- Asserts that the value equals the expected value.
    --- ```lua
    --- expect(5).is(5)
    --- expect("hello").is("hello")
    --- ```
	is: (any) -> (),

    --- Asserts that the value is greater than the expected value.
    --- ```lua
    --- expect(10).greaterThan(5)
    --- ```
	greaterThan: (any) -> (),

    --- Asserts that the value is less than the expected value.
    --- ```lua
    --- expect(3).lessThan(10)
    --- ```
	lessThan: (any) -> (),

    --- Asserts that the value is greater than or equal to the expected value.
    --- ```lua
    --- expect(5).greaterThanOrEqual(5)
    --- expect(6).greaterThanOrEqual(5)
    --- ```
	greaterThanOrEqual: (any) -> (),

    --- Asserts that the value is less than or equal to the expected value.
    --- ```lua
    --- expect(5).lessThanOrEqual(5)
    --- expect(4).lessThanOrEqual(5)
    --- ```
	lessThanOrEqual: (any) -> (),

    --- Returns an `Expectation` that negates the subsequent assertion.
    --- ```lua
    --- expect(5).never.is(3)
    --- expect(5).never.greaterThan(10)
    --- ```
	read never: Expectation,
}

--- Provides functions for defining test cases and organizing them into groups.
export type Tester = {

    --- Defines a named test case. The callback receives an `expect` function
    --- used to create expectations on a value.
    --- ```lua
    --- case("adds two numbers", function(expect)
    ---   local result = 2 + 3
    ---   expect(result).is(5)
    --- end)
    --- ```
	case: (name: string, test: (expect: (value: any) -> Expectation) -> ()) -> (),

    --- Defines a test case that passes only when the callback raises an
    --- error. With a `message`, the error must also contain it.
    --- ```lua
    --- errors("rejects a negative size", function(expect)
    ---   buffer.create(-1)
    --- end, "invalid argument")
    --- ```
	errors: (name: string, test: (expect: (value: any) -> Expectation) -> (), message: string?) -> (),

    --- Groups related test cases under a common name. Nested groups are supported.
    --- ```lua
    --- group("Math utilities", function()
    ---   case("adds numbers", function(expect)
    ---     expect(2 + 2).is(4)
    ---   end)
    ---
    ---   case("multiplies numbers", function(expect)
    ---     expect(3 * 4).is(12)
    ---   end)
    --- end)
    --- ```
	group: (name: string, test: () -> ()) -> (),

    --- Looks up a blob asset in the file by name, or nil when missing.
    --- ```lua
    --- local data = test.blob("fixtures")
    --- ```
	blob: (name: string) -> Blob?,
}

--- A function that defines a collection of test cases. The `Tester` is provided
--- to allow cases and groups to be declared.
---
--- See Unit Testing for usage.
export type Tests = (test: Tester) -> ()
```

--- A variable axis of a `Font`, such as weight or width.
export type FontAxis = {
    --- Four letter axis tag, for example 'wght'.
    tag: string,
    min: number,
    default: number,
    max: number,
}

--- A font that shapes and draws text. Fonts come from the file's assets with
--- `context:font(name)`, from a view model `Property<Font>`, or from bytes with
--- `Font.decode`. Metrics are for a 1 point font and grow negative upwards,
--- so multiply by the size and expect `ascent` below zero.
--- ```lua
--- type Label = {
---   text: Text,
--- }
---
--- function init(self: Label, context: Context): boolean
---   local font = context:font('Inter')
---   if font then
---     self.text:append('Hello', { font = font, size = 24, paint = Paint.new() })
---   end
---   return true
--- end
--- ```
declare extern type Font with
    --- Distance from the baseline to the top of the em box for a 1 point font, negative.
    ascent: number
    --- Distance from the baseline to the bottom of the em box for a 1 point font.
    descent: number
    --- Distance from the baseline to the top of capital letters, negative.
    capHeight: number
    --- Distance from the baseline to the top of lowercase letters, negative.
    xHeight: number
    --- Weight from 1 to 1000, 400 being regular.
    weight: number
    isItalic: boolean
    --- Variable axes the font offers.
    axes: { FontAxis }
    --- Four letter OpenType feature tags the font offers, such as 'liga'.
    features: { string }

    --- Height of one line of text at the given size.
    function lineHeight(self, size: number): number

    --- Whether the font has a glyph for the unicode codepoint.
    function hasGlyph(self, codepoint: number): boolean

    --- Current value of a variable axis, by tag.
    function axisValue(self, tag: string): number

    --- A new font at the given axis values and feature settings.
    --- ```lua
    --- local bold = font:withOptions({ wght = 700 }, { liga = 0 })
    --- ```
    function withOptions(self, axes: { [string]: number }?, features: { [string]: number }?): Font

    --- Outline of one glyph in 1 point units with the baseline at y 0, wound
    --- for a clockwise fill. Scale by the font size to draw it.
    function glyphPath(self, glyphId: number): Path
end

declare Font: {
    --- Decodes a TrueType or OpenType font from bytes a script obtained
    --- itself, such as a downloaded file. Font files in a project are font
    --- assets, reached with `context:font`, not blobs. Returns nil when the
    --- bytes are not a font.
    --- ```lua
    --- local font = Font.decode(downloadedBytes)
    --- ```
    decode: @checked (bytes: buffer) -> Font?,
}

export type TextSizing = 'autoWidth' | 'autoHeight' | 'fixed'
export type TextOverflow = 'visible' | 'hidden' | 'clipped' | 'ellipsis'
--- 'start' and 'end' follow the direction of the first paragraph, so right to
--- left text starts on the right.
export type TextAlign = 'left' | 'right' | 'center' | 'start' | 'end'
export type TextWrap = 'wrap' | 'noWrap'
export type TextWordBreak = 'breakWord' | 'normal' | 'breakAll'
export type TextOrigin = 'top' | 'baseline'
--- 'auto' detects each paragraph's direction from its text.
export type TextDirection = 'auto' | 'ltr' | 'rtl'

--- Style of one run appended to a `Text`.
export type TextRunStyle = {
    font: Font,
    --- Font size, 16 when omitted.
    size: number?,
    --- Line height, the font's own when omitted.
    lineHeight: number?,
    letterSpacing: number?,
    --- Runs sharing a paint draw as one path. A run without a paint only
    --- draws when `Text:draw` is given one.
    paint: Paint?,
    --- Color used by emoji layers that take the text color.
    foregroundColor: number?,
}

--- One glyph placed by a `Text` layout, in the text's local space.
declare extern type Glyph with
    --- Glyph id within `font`.
    id: number
    font: Font
    size: number
    --- Pen position on the baseline, the shaper's offset included.
    x: number
    y: number
    advance: number
    --- Index of the first codepoint this glyph draws, 1 based.
    textIndex: number
    --- Direction of the run the glyph belongs to.
    direction: 'ltr' | 'rtl'
    --- Whether this is a color glyph (emoji) drawn as layers rather than one outline.
    isColor: boolean
    --- Places the 1 point outline from `Font:glyphPath` at this glyph's size and position.
    transform: Mat2D

    --- The outline placed by `transform`, as a new `Path`.
    function path(self): Path
end

--- One line of a `Text` after wrapping. Iterate it to visit its glyphs in
--- visual order, left to right, whatever the writing direction.
--- ```lua
--- for _, line in text:lines() do
---   for _, glyph in line do
---     renderer:save()
---     renderer:transform(glyph.transform)
---     renderer:drawPath(glyph.font:glyphPath(glyph.id), paint)
---     renderer:restore()
---   end
--- end
--- ```
declare extern type TextLine with
    --- 1 based index of the line within the text.
    index: number
    --- Left edge after alignment.
    x: number
    top: number
    baseline: number
    bottom: number
    width: number
    --- Base direction of the paragraph the line belongs to.
    direction: 'ltr' | 'rtl'
    --- First and last codepoint index on the line, 1 based.
    firstIndex: number
    lastIndex: number
    glyphCount: number

    --- The glyph at a 1 based visual position.
